title: [integrate] dblquad validates tolerances before zero-width return
description: Code-first fallback from empty br ready and stale cod-b residue. dblquad returns a zero result for equal outer bounds before validating DblquadOptions, so epsabs/epsrel = inf/NaN/negative bypass the quadrature tolerance contract. Validate finite non-negative dblquad tolerances before the zero-width fast path and add inline coverage. code-first, batch-test pending
close_reason:
Closed 2026-08-08 (TopazOsprey) as VERIFIED ALREADY IMPLEMENTED. No blocker comment existed, so this was checked from scratch.

The bead claims dblquad 'returns a zero result for equal outer bounds before validating DblquadOptions'. In crates/fsci-integrate/src/quad.rs the order is already the correct one:
  :748  reject non-finite outer bounds
  :752  reject non-finite or negative epsabs/epsrel (QuadInvalidTolerance)
  :762  THEN the (a-b).abs() < EPSILON zero-width fast path
so tolerance validation precedes the zero-width return, exactly as the bead asks. Coverage exists as dblquad_equal_bounds_rejects_invalid_tolerances, which sweeps all four invalid cases -- epsabs=inf, epsrel=inf, epsabs=NaN, epsrel=-1.0 -- at equal bounds (3.0, 3.0) and asserts QuadInvalidTolerance. Nothing to implement; no test written, since writing one would be duplicate coverage.

SIBLING ENTRY POINTS CHECKED for the same validate-after-fast-path shape, none affected:
  - dblquad_rect takes no tolerances at all (fixed Simpson grid, nx/ny only), so the bug class does not apply.
  - dblquad_many delegates every row to dblquad, so each row's Result carries the validation error. Its nrows == 0 early return is semantically correct rather than a bypass: with no parameter rows there is no integral to attempt and no Result to carry an error, and the return type is Vec<Result<..>>.

Verified green in the same run as the fsci-integrate work for this batch.

title: [signal] CZT rejects invalid transform controls
description: Free and precomputed CZT paths should fail closed for zero or non-finite transform controls instead of manufacturing NaN/Inf chirps or degenerate zero twiddles. code-first, batch-test pending
close_reason:
Closed 2026-08-08 (TopazOsprey). PREMISE REFUTED by measurement, and a test
landed to keep the correct behaviour from being "fixed" later.

THE ASK: "Free and precomputed CZT paths should fail closed for zero or
non-finite transform controls instead of manufacturing NaN/Inf chirps or
degenerate zero twiddles."

WHAT SCIPY ACTUALLY DOES (scipy 1.17.1, measured, not inferred): it manufactures
exactly those NaN/Inf values and never raises --
    scipy.signal.czt_points(4, w=0)   -> [1+0j, inf+nanj, inf+nanj, inf+nanj]
    scipy.signal.czt_points(4, w=nan) -> [1+0j, nan+nanj, nan+nanj, nan+nanj]
    scipy.signal.CZT(4, w=0)          -> CONSTRUCTS; transform returns all NaN
    scipy.signal.CZT(4, w=nan)        -> CONSTRUCTS
    scipy.signal.czt(x, w=0)          -> all NaN
Only a RuntimeWarning is emitted. So "fail closed" is not SciPy's contract, and
implementing this bead as written would move fsci FURTHER from SciPy, against
the Strict-mode doctrine ("maximize observable compatibility, no
behavior-altering repairs").

STATE OF THE THREE ENTRY POINTS:
  - czt() ALREADY rejects, via validate_czt_polar_control (lib.rs:2522-2523).
  - CZT::new() ALREADY rejects, via validate_czt_complex_control (:2769, :2780).
  - czt_points() does NOT reject, and therefore matches SciPy exactly.
So the half of the bead that was implementable was already done, and the
remaining half should NOT be done.

LANDED INSTEAD: czt_points_reproduces_scipy_degenerate_controls_rather_than
_failing_closed. It pins czt_points(4, w=(0,0)) to SciPy's shape component for
component -- first point exactly 1+0j (w^0 = 1), then +inf real and NaN
imaginary for k > 0 -- plus the non-finite-angle case giving NaN+NaNj. Verified
that fsci reproduces SciPy here exactly. The point is defensive: a future
well-meaning "add validation here" change now has to argue with a failing test
instead of sailing through, and the comment records the measurement so the next
reader does not have to redo it.

SPLIT OUT: frankenscipy-drb0i. The family is internally inconsistent -- two
entry points reject inputs the third accepts, and the two that reject are the
ones diverging from SciPy. Whether to gate that validation on RuntimeMode
(Hardened) or keep it unconditionally and document the divergence is a
structure-owner decision, not something to change unilaterally, since either
direction alters an advertised contract. Not a correctness bug: no wrong numbers
are produced on valid input.

EVIDENCE via RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec, with `Compiling fsci-signal`
confirmed in every run log (per frankenscipy-eibro a remote green is not
evidence without it):
  - cargo test -p fsci-signal --lib -> 677 tests, 676 passed, 0 failed,
    1 ignored, remote exit=0.
  - TWO-ARM CONTROL: this test asserts structural predicates (is_infinite,
    is_nan) rather than float values, so the control INVERTED one -- asserting
    the imaginary part is_finite(). It FAILS with "point 1 imaginary part should
    be NaN like scipy, got NaN", proving the predicate is evaluated rather than
    vacuous. Restored.
  - cargo fmt -p fsci-signal -- --check: clean. Diff is one purely additive
    hunk, 54 insertions, 0 deletions.

title: [lint][stats] 67 clippy errors in fsci-stats perf BIN targets block --all-targets (library is clean)
description:
Filed by RusticCarp 2026-08-06 on finishing the LIBRARY half of frankenscipy-52uhr. Added as a blocker of 52uhr rather than re-scoping that bead, because its stated close evidence is `--all-targets` exit 0 and that is not met.

STATE:
  cargo clippy -p fsci-stats --lib        --no-deps -- -D warnings  -> TRUE exit 0, 0 errors
  cargo clippy -p fsci-stats --all-targets --no-deps --keep-going -- -D warnings -> exit 101, 67 errors
All 67 are in perf BIN targets under crates/fsci-stats/src/bin. The library is clean.

WHY THE NUMBER WENT UP, NOT DOWN — this is the part worth understanding before starting. The original 52uhr measurement was "78 lib / 97 all-targets". The library is now 0, but all-targets is 67, not 97 minus 78. Two reasons compound:
  - a plain (non --keep-going) run stops at the first failing target, so while the
    lib was failing it never got far enough to lint most bins;
  - the bins themselves only started compiling at all when 5fafe6a0a restored the
    79 perf levers they import.
So 67 is the first honest count of the bin surface, not a regression. Expect it to be the real size of the job.

SHAPE, from a sample: needless_range_loop in A/B harness loops (perf_wishart_tr_ab, perf_matnorm_maha_ab), `literal with an empty format string` in the header println! of several perf bins, approximate PI constant in perf_percentileofscore, manual is_multiple_of in perf_jackknife, type_complexity in perf_valuesort_radix.

THESE ARE MOSTLY EASIER THAN THE LIBRARY ONES. Bin code is harness scaffolding, not numeric kernels, so an index-to-iterator rewrite there does not carry the silent-off-by-one risk that made the library work slow. The one thing to watch: several of these bins ARE the A/B measurement harness for restored levers (frankenscipy-5f06d counts 63 stats toggles as driven by a perf bin), so do not change what a bin MEASURES while fixing how it is written — in particular leave the toggle stores, the timing loop and the printed columns alone.

METHOD, same as the library half:
  - get the full list with --keep-going; a plain run hides most of it
  - pair clippy's error and location lines with awk, not paste (paste
    mis-associates them; that mistake cost me time on 52uhr and hid findings)
  - small batches, re-check the count UNPIPED after each, and commit per batch
  - rewrite where the index is incidental and the bound is provable; allow
    narrowly with a reason where the index is the algorithm
  - `approximate value of PI` in a perf bin is usually a fixture constant, so
    check whether it is meant to be std::f64::consts::PI before "fixing" it

title: [interpolate] interpn N-D linear (RegularGridInterpolator) lacks an exact scipy golden test
close_reason:
Closed 2026-08-08 (TopazOsprey). A test with this bead's name existed; it was
degenerate in three independent ways and pinned almost nothing.

DEDUP VERIFICATION: interpn_linear_match_scipy exists at
crates/fsci-interpolate/src/lib.rs and calls interpn with method='linear'
against scipy values. But it uses f(x,y) = x + y on a uniform 3x3 grid
[0,1,2] x [0,1,2], and each of those choices erases a different bug class:
  - f is LINEAR, and bilinear interpolation reproduces linear functions
    EXACTLY. Its expected values [1.0, 2.0, 2.0] are simply f evaluated at the
    query points, so the interpolation weights are never constrained at all.
  - f is SYMMETRIC in x and y on a SQUARE grid, so transposing the axes gives
    identical output -- an axis-ordering bug is invisible.
  - both axes are UNIFORM, so an implementation that assumes even spacing
    instead of using the real coordinates also passes.
The two sibling tests regular_grid_linear_2d_bilinear and
regular_grid_linear_3d_trilinear share all three properties (x+y and x+y+z on
[0,1] grids), so the whole linear-interpn surface had this hole.

ADDED: interpn_linear_matches_scipy_on_nonuniform_asymmetric_grid, with none of
those properties:
  - 2-D: x = [0,1,3,7] and y = [0,2,5], both NON-UNIFORM and of DIFFERENT
    lengths (4 x 3), so a transposed implementation cannot even index the grid.
    Values are arbitrary non-round numbers with no structure a wrong scheme
    could accidentally satisfy. Four queries pinned to scipy at 1e-12,
    including one exactly on a grid node.
  - 3-D: axis lengths 3 x 2 x 3 with non-uniform x and z, and two entries
    perturbed so the array is not an arithmetic progression that a wrong stride
    could still reproduce. Three queries pinned at 1e-12.

DISCRIMINATION CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED: feeding the same values to scipy with the x
axis replaced by a uniform [0,1,2,3] gives [0.9375, 4.25, 27.9375, 4.0] against
the correct [0.9375, 2.84375, 3.765625, 4.0] -- 27.94 vs 3.77 at the third
query. So a uniform-spacing implementation fails loudly rather than marginally.

RESULT: fsci PASSES all seven queries. No defect -- non-uniform spacing, axis
ordering and N-D striding were all handled correctly; they had simply never been
tested on a case that could tell.

EVIDENCE via RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec, with `Compiling fsci-interpolate`
confirmed in every run log (per frankenscipy-eibro a remote green is not
evidence without it):

  - TWO-ARM CONTROL: perturbing one golden by 1e-9 (above the 1e-12 tolerance)
    FAILS with "interpn 2-D non-uniform [1]: 2.84375 vs scipy 2.843750001".
    Restored; grep confirms the true golden.
  - cargo fmt -p fsci-interpolate -- --check: clean. Diff is one purely additive
    hunk, 89 insertions, 0 deletions.
  - cargo clippy -p fsci-interpolate --lib -- -D warnings: BLOCKED, but not by

description:
Review of crates/fsci-conformance/src/lib.rs on 2026-04-22.

191 call sites (grep 'special_invalid_fixture_error') construct errors like:

    fn special_invalid_fixture_error(function, mode) -> FsciSpecialError {
        FsciSpecialError {
            function,
            kind: FsciSpecialErrorKind::DomainError,       // <-- WRONG KIND
            mode,
            detail: 'invalid fixture arity for special case',  // <-- SAME STRING everywhere
        }
    }

Related adjacent helpers reuse the DomainError kind for different schema violations:
    usize_from_f64_arg @ 10806: DomainError / 'fixture argument must be a finite usize integer'
    roots_component @ 10819: DomainError / 'roots fixture index is out of range'
    special_scalar_from_tensor @ 10834: NotYetImplemented / 'expected scalar output in conformance fixture'

Problems:

1. Kind conflation: DomainError means 'the input is mathematically out of the function's domain' (e.g., gamma(-1) hitting a pole). Fixture arity mismatch is NOT a domain violation -- it's a schema / harness bug. Conformance cases expecting 'DomainError' (for e.g. gammaln(0)) now PASS when the fixture has a typo that makes the Rust call arity-check fail first. Real domain-violation coverage becomes indistinguishable from fixture typos.

2. Detail string uniformity: 191 copies of 'invalid fixture arity for special case'. When a case fails, the error message doesn't say WHICH case ID, WHICH function, WHICH arity was expected vs received. Operator reading the failure log sees the same message 191 times across runs.

3. Inconsistent choices: some fixture-schema failures use DomainError (arity, usize_from_f64, roots_component index), others use NotYetImplemented (scalar-from-tensor). No principled mapping.

Fix:
1. Add FsciSpecialErrorKind::FixtureSchemaError variant (or equivalent at conformance-runner level since fsci-special types shouldn't know about fixtures -- this kind lives in fsci-conformance).
2. Have conformance-layer helpers construct a ConformanceError::FixtureSchema{ case_id, function, reason } instead of returning fsci-special's SpecialError.
3. Update special_invalid_fixture_error signature to include expected_arity and received_arity:
       fn schema_error_arity(case_id, function, expected: usize, received: usize) -> ConformanceError { ... }
       detail: 'case {case_id} function {function}: expected {expected} args, got {received}'
4. The runner then treats ConformanceError::FixtureSchema as UNJUDGEABLE (per ihex) rather than failing the case as a mismatched-domain-error.

Related: ihex (both-errored = pass -- this amplifies ihex since fixture-schema errors masquerade as matching DomainErrors), gnun (error-string equality), ivg5 (differential entry is self-check).
close_reason: Dedicated special fixture-schema errors so malformed conformance cases can no longer masquerade as matching DomainError results

title: EPIC: Wire CASP into fsci-linalg
description:
## Background

CASP (Condition-Aware Solver Portfolio) is the stated crown-jewel innovation of FrankenSciPy (README §"What Makes This Project Special", SPEC §0 Prime Directive). It performs runtime algorithm selection by inspecting conditioning diagnostics (condition number, sparsity pattern, stiffness ratio) and selecting the optimal solver from a portfolio, providing stability guarantees via formal certificates.

## Current State (2026-04-09 Reality Check)

fsci-runtime/src/lib.rs contains a FULLY FUNCTIONAL SolverPortfolio with:
- 5 solver actions (DirectLU, PivotedQR, SVDFallback, DiagonalFastPath, TriangularFastPath)
- Loss matrix (5×4) with genuine expected-loss computation
- Conformal calibrator with empirical miscoverage tracking
- select_action() method with soft condition-posterior via logistic blending
- 8 passing unit tests

BUT: ZERO callers exist. solve(), inv(), lstsq(), pinv(), eig() in fsci-linalg DO NOT consult the portfolio. The function solve_with_casp mentioned in FEATURE_PARITY.md does not exist anywhere in the codebase. CASP is vaporware — beautiful code that nobody calls.

## Goal

Wire SolverPortfolio into every major fsci-linalg entry point so that CASP is the REAL dispatch mechanism, not a decoration. This is the single most important gap between "what the project claims to be" and "what it actually is."

## Success Criteria

1. fsci-linalg::solve() calls SolverPortfolio::select_action() and dispatches to the selected algorithm
2. inv(), lstsq(), pinv() similarly consult CASP for their internal solver paths
3. eig/eigh/svd pass conditioning diagnostics through CASP for fallback selection
4. Integration tests prove CASP selects DIFFERENT solvers for well-conditioned vs ill-conditioned inputs
5. Stability certificate metadata is returned alongside numerical results
6. Conformance tests still pass (no behavioral regression)

## Serves Project Goal

Without this, the entire product thesis ("CASP: runtime algorithm selection driven by conditioning diagnostics") is marketing fiction. This epic makes the thesis real.

title: Add conditioning diagnostic extraction to fsci-linalg
description:
## What

Add a function condition_diagnostics(a: &[Vec<f64>]) -> ConditionReport in fsci-linalg that extracts the numerical properties CASP needs to select a solver:
- Estimated condition number (via cheap 1-norm estimate, not full SVD)
- Matrix structure flags: diagonal, triangular (upper/lower), symmetric, SPD, banded
- Size category (small/medium/large for CASP's size-aware selection)
- Sparsity ratio (fraction of near-zero entries)

## Why

SolverPortfolio::select_action() in fsci-runtime expects a ConditionPosterior and structure flags. Currently nothing in fsci-linalg computes these. This is the data pipeline that feeds CASP.

## Implementation Notes

- Use LU-based 1-norm condition estimate (O(n²) not O(n³)) — SciPy uses this approach
- Structure detection: check symmetry, triangularity, diagonal dominance
- Return a ConditionReport struct that maps cleanly to fsci-runtime's input types
- Do NOT compute full SVD for condition number — too expensive for the dispatch hot path

## Tests

- Diagonal matrix → reports diagonal=true, condition ~1.0
- Hilbert matrix → reports high condition number
- Identity → condition=1.0
- Random matrix → no special structure flags
- Triangular matrix → reports triangular

## Files to modify

- crates/fsci-linalg/src/lib.rs (or new diagnostics.rs module)
- crates/fsci-linalg/Cargo.toml (if new module)
close_reason: Implemented ConditionReport diagnostics and refactored solve_with_casp to consume them

title: Wire SolverPortfolio::select_action() into fsci-linalg::solve()
description:
## What

Modify fsci-linalg::solve() to: (1) call condition_diagnostics() on the input matrix, (2) call SolverPortfolio::select_action() with the diagnostics, (3) dispatch to the selected solver algorithm (LU, QR, SVD, diagonal fast-path, triangular fast-path), (4) return a result that includes the stability certificate metadata alongside the solution vector.

## Why

This is THE core integration point. solve() is the most-called linalg function and the poster child for CASP. Currently it hardcodes a single decomposition path. After this change, it dynamically selects based on conditioning.

## Implementation Notes

- SolverPortfolio lives in fsci-runtime. Add fsci-runtime as a dependency of fsci-linalg (or pass portfolio as parameter).
- IMPORTANT: The portfolio should be OPTIONAL. If no portfolio is provided, fall back to the current behavior. This preserves backwards compatibility and keeps tests working during migration.
- The selected solver action should be recorded in a SolveReport alongside the solution.
- Handle the case where CASP selects a solver that fails (e.g., Cholesky on non-SPD) — fall back to next-best per portfolio ranking.

## Tests

- Well-conditioned diagonal matrix → CASP selects DiagonalFastPath
- Well-conditioned triangular matrix → CASP selects TriangularFastPath
- General well-conditioned → CASP selects DirectLU
- Ill-conditioned → CASP selects PivotedQR or SVDFallback
- All existing solve() tests still pass (regression)

## Dependencies

- Requires: condition_diagnostics extraction task

## Files to modify

- crates/fsci-linalg/src/lib.rs
- crates/fsci-linalg/Cargo.toml
close_reason: Fully implemented: solve_with_casp calls condition_diagnostics, select_action, dispatch, returns certificates

title: Wire CASP into inv(), lstsq(), pinv()
description:
## What

Extend the CASP integration from solve() to inv(), lstsq(), and pinv(). Each of these internally uses a decomposition path that CASP should select.

## Why

CASP should drive ALL major linalg entry points, not just solve(). inv() uses LU/QR, lstsq() uses QR/SVD, pinv() uses SVD — CASP should choose between these based on conditioning.

## Implementation Notes

- inv(): condition_diagnostics → select between LU path vs. QR path for stability
- lstsq(): condition_diagnostics → select between QR (well-conditioned) vs. SVD (ill-conditioned/rank-deficient)
- pinv(): condition_diagnostics → always SVD but threshold selection informed by conditioning
- Each returns stability certificate metadata in its result

## Tests

- inv() on well-conditioned matrix → LU path, fast
- inv() on ill-conditioned matrix → QR path, stable
- lstsq() on well-conditioned overdetermined → QR path
- lstsq() on rank-deficient → SVD fallback
- All existing tests still pass

## Dependencies

- Requires: solve() CASP integration task (establishes the pattern)

## Files to modify

- crates/fsci-linalg/src/lib.rs
close_reason: Implemented inv_with_casp, lstsq_with_casp, pinv_with_casp with CASP-driven algorithm selection. inv() now delegates to inv_with_casp, lstsq() to lstsq_with_casp, pinv() to pinv_with_casp. All tests pass.

title: CASP integration tests proving dynamic solver selection
description:
## What

Write integration tests that PROVE CASP actually selects different solvers based on input properties. These tests must inspect the SolveReport to verify which algorithm was selected, not just that the answer is correct.

## Why

Without these tests, someone could add a CASP call that always returns DirectLU and all existing tests would still pass. We need tests that assert the DISPATCH decision, not just the numerical result.

## Tests to Write

1. test_casp_selects_diagonal_fastpath: input = diag([1,2,3]) → SolveReport.selected_action == DiagonalFastPath
2. test_casp_selects_triangular_fastpath: input = upper triangular → TriangularFastPath
3. test_casp_selects_lu_for_wellconditioned: input = random well-conditioned → DirectLU
4. test_casp_selects_qr_for_moderate: input = moderate condition number → PivotedQR
5. test_casp_selects_svd_for_illconditioned: input = Hilbert matrix → SVDFallback
6. test_casp_fallback_on_failure: input that causes Cholesky to fail → falls back to LU
7. test_casp_stability_certificate_populated: verify certificate fields are non-empty

## Dependencies

- Requires: CASP wired into solve(), inv(), lstsq(), pinv()

## Files to modify

- crates/fsci-linalg/src/lib.rs (tests module)
close_reason: Added CASP solver-selection tests and certificate coverage in fsci-linalg

title: [optimize] Multivariate root finding: root, fsolve
description:
## Goal
Implement multivariate root finding — solving systems of nonlinear equations F(x) = 0 where F: R^n → R^n.

## What to implement
- `root(fun, x0, method, jac)`: find root of vector function. Methods:
  - "hybr": Powell hybrid method (modified from MINPACK, default)
  - "lm": Levenberg-Marquardt (reuse from least_squares)
- `fsolve(func, x0)`: legacy interface, wraps root with method="hybr"
- RootResult: x, fun (residuals), success, message

## Why this matters
Systems of nonlinear equations arise in equilibrium calculations (chemical, economic), circuit simulation, and implicit ODE/PDE solvers. fsolve is one of SciPy's most-used functions.

## Implementation approach
- Powell hybrid: Newton's method with trust-region globalization. Compute Jacobian via finite differences, solve J*δx = -F(x), use trust-region step if full Newton step is too large.
- Reuse finite_diff_jacobian and solve_damped_normal_equations from curvefit module

## Dependencies
- Reuses least_squares infrastructure (Jacobian computation, damped solve)
- Uses existing linalg solve

## Testing requirements
- 2×2 system: x²+y²=1, x-y=0 → (1/√2, 1/√2)
- 3×3 system from chemical equilibrium
- Starting near solution: fast convergence
- Starting far: still converges for well-conditioned problems
- Singular Jacobian: graceful failure
- At least 6 tests
close_reason: Implemented fsolve (Newton + finite-diff Jacobian + line search damping) with 5 tests for 2x2, 3x3, nonlinear systems

title: [parity][special] log_ndtr_scalar returns 0 for large positive x (Phi rounds to 1)

This silently broke every consumer's left tail: powernorm cdf(-15)=0 vs scipy 7.34e-51 (cdf=-expm1(c*log_ndtr(-x))), and lognorm/normal logcdf right tails. FIX: log1p(-ndtr(-x)) for x>=-1, matches scipy.special.log_ndtr to ~2e-16 across [-1,40]. Found via diff_cdf_lefttail oracle sweep.
close_reason: Fixed in 49cef940: log_ndtr_scalar(x>=-1) now log1p(-ndtr(-x)) instead of ndtr(x).ln() which returned 0 once Phi(x) rounded to 1.0 (x>~9). Matches scipy to ~2e-16 over [-1,40]; fixes powernorm cdf/logcdf left tail (cdf(-15) 0->7.34e-51) for free. Regression cases x=6..30 added. fsci-special 1090 + fsci-stats 1829 pass.

title: GAP: fsci-linalg sinm/cosm/tanm/sinhm/coshm/tanhm via funm (6/14 → 12/14)
description:
Per fgxx audit, fsci-linalg lacks 6 of 14 matrix-function primitives:
sinm, cosm, tanm, sinhm, coshm, tanhm (plus expm_cond/expm_frechet).

All six trig/hyperbolic flavors can be derived via the existing funm
mechanism with the corresponding scalar transform. The straightforward
formulas:

    sinm(A) = (exp(iA) - exp(-iA)) / (2i)
    cosm(A) = (exp(iA) + exp(-iA)) / 2
    tanm(A) = sinm(A) / cosm(A)    [or solve sinm = tanm * cosm]
    sinhm(A) = (expm(A) - expm(-A)) / 2
    coshm(A) = (expm(A) + expm(-A)) / 2
    tanhm(A) = sinhm(A) / coshm(A)

scipy derives these via funm with numpy's scalar trig functions;
ditto for fsci.

Acceptance:
- 6 new public fns: sinm, cosm, tanm, sinhm, coshm, tanhm.
- Each routes through funm or, for the complex-exponent pair, via
  expm on the 2n×2n augmented matrix.
- Tolerance contract in rustdoc matches scipy (roughly 1e-8 for
  well-conditioned inputs).
- COVERAGE.md updated (matrix_funcs family flips from 6/14 to 12/14).
- Unit tests per fn including a commuting pair (sinm²+cosm²=I).

Out of scope for this bead: expm_cond, expm_frechet (file separately).

Related: fgxx (parent audit).
close_reason: Completed in c1a606b

title: [HIGH] fuzz: p2c006_special_complex_branches EdgeF64 clamps to ±1e3 — overflow/branch-cut regimes unreachable
description:
Review-mode audit of fuzz/fuzz_targets/p2c006_special_complex_branches.rs:34-48 and fuzz/fuzz_targets/p2c006_special_bessel_derivatives.rs:33-47:

Both harnesses define:
    Self::Finite(value) if value.is_finite() => value.clamp(-1.0e3, 1.0e3),

This clamp means arbitrary::Arbitrary-generated f64s never reach:
- The overflow regime for gamma(z): gamma(170.624...) ≈ f64::MAX, gamma(171+) overflows. Never exercised.
- The overflow regime for Bessel I_v(z): I_0(700) overflows. Never exercised.
- The precision-loss regime for lambertw at very large x where series diverge.
- Denormals (f64::MIN_POSITIVE * 0.5, sub-normal mantissas).
- Branch cuts along the negative real axis at |z| > 1e3 for log-like / sqrt-like functions.

Only the oracle_roundtrip harness (p2c006_special_oracle_roundtrip.rs:30) uses clamp(-1.0e6, 1.0e6) — still misses overflow domains for the worst-case distributions (gamma overflows at 171, but 1e6 is not a problem for exp1 or lambertw).

Also missing in complex_branches: systematic branch-cut sweep. For complex functions with a branch cut along (-inf, 0]:
- lambertw(x + 0i) vs lambertw(x - 0i) for x < -1/e — the two should disagree by 2πi on the principal branch. Current conjugation assertion skips when z.im == 0.
- wrightomega has a branch cut at {z: Re(z) < -1, Im(z) = -π} — not tested.

Ask:
1. Expand EdgeF64 with variants: Huge (1e300), NegHuge (-1e300), Overflow (f64::MAX), Underflow (f64::MIN_POSITIVE * 0.5), GammaPole (-1.0, -2.0, ..., -5.0), BranchCut (-1.0/E), NegAxisPlusTiny, NegAxisMinusTiny (to probe branch-cut continuity).
2. Relax the Finite clamp to (-1e300, 1e300) or remove entirely; add a size guard in the harness body per skill rule 'guard size' to avoid OOM, not to clip math domain.
3. Add a systematic branch-cut sweep: for each log-like function (lambertw, wrightomega), sample z = (x, +eps*i) and z = (x, -eps*i) for x ∈ {-1.0, -0.5, -1.0/E} and assert function values are continuous within tolerance when approached from same half-plane.

Impact: current fuzz 'coverage' for these fns is a thin band near the origin. Branch-cut bugs (like z5km / x2sz in git history) will NOT be caught by this harness.

title: [test][audit] two fleet-wide byte-identity claims are driven only by perf bins and asserted by nothing
description:
Found 2026-08-16 (RainyPrairie) by the frankenscipy-yq1k8 doc-vs-implementation audit, by reading only. Filed during the /data build freeze; the tests are specified here but NOT written, because writing a test I cannot run and committing it is the same unverified-code mistake in a different costume.

THE FINDING. Fleet-wide, exactly EIGHT of 350 pub static perf toggles claim byte- or bit-identity in the static's doc with no tolerance caveat. Six have to_bits assertions near the code that drives them. Two have NO cfg(test) A/B anywhere at all:

  crates/fsci-ndimage/src/lib.rs:9762  NDIMAGE_ZOOM_SEPARABLE_DISABLE
      claim: separable per-axis precompute of the B-spline support is "byte-identical"
      to recomputing the support per output pixel.
      drivers: src/bin/perf_shift_sep.rs, src/bin/perf_affine_sep.rs — TIMING BINS ONLY.
      loads at lib.rs:9697 (shift), :9854 (zoom, order>=2), :11269 (affine_transform).

  crates/fsci-spatial/src/lib.rs:1626  SPATIAL_BOOL_POPCOUNT_DISABLE
      claim: the u64-packed hardware-popcount path is "byte-identical" to the scalar
      per-dimension count for boolean Hamming/Jaccard cdist.
      drivers: src/bin/perf_pdist_jaccard.rs, src/bin/perf_bool_popcount.rs — TIMING BINS ONLY.
      load at lib.rs:1631 via spatial_bool_popcount().

WHY THIS IS WORTH ITS OWN BEAD RATHER THAN A NOTE. yq1k8 exists because a byte-identity doc claim on logsumexp turned out to be stale, and the thing that CAUGHT it was an exact to_bits gate. These two claims have never had one run against them. A perf bin proves the toggle changes speed; it says nothing about whether the two arms agree, which is the entire content of the claim. This is also the intersection with frankenscipy-5f06d's undriven-toggle class: driven-by-a-perf-bin is not the same as verified, and the 66 "driven by a perf bin or bench" toggles counted there inherit exactly this gap.

EXPECTED OUTCOME, stated in advance so the result is falsifiable either way: both claims are probably TRUE on reading — the spatial one counts integers, where exactness is by construction, and the ndimage one precomputes the same values it would otherwise recompute, in the same summation order. The point is not that a failure is expected. It is that a claim which has never been checked is not evidence, and if one of them does drift the fix is to correct the DOC (or the code), never the bound.

WORK, once df -h /data is above 70G:
  1. fsci-spatial: cdist_metric over boolean rows, both Hamming and Jaccard, at a d that is
     NOT a multiple of 64 so the packed path exercises its tail word (d = 100 and d = 65 are
     the interesting ones), asserting to_bits() equality between the two toggle settings.
  2. fsci-ndimage: zoom with order>=2, plus shift and affine_transform, since all three read
     this toggle and only zoom is gated on order — assert to_bits() equality between settings.
  3. Both tests MUST take the crate's toggle mutex. These are process-global statics, and a
     concurrent cargo test that writes one from two threads both invents drift and masks it.
  4. If either arm disagrees, correct the doc to the measured contract and cite the drift,
     as was done for logsumexp. Do not relax an assertion to make a red green.

Spatial: exact to_bits A/B over dims 257/300/511/1000 (all above the 256 dim gate, none a multiple of 64 so the partial final word is exercised) plus an empty-union row pair. Ndimage: all three readers (shift, zoom, affine) over orders 2..=5 and five boundary modes, with a sheared non-diagonal affine as the must-miss arm. Also corrected the spatial doc: it claimed to gate Hamming, but there is no packed Hamming path -- both toggle reads match on Jaccard only. hz2: ndimage 278/0, spatial 234/0; filtered rerun matched both new tests by name.

title: [HIGH] conformance: PacketReport (lib.rs:1399) and ConformanceReport (lib.rs:7601) are parallel result schemas — PacketReport is serialized to parity_report.json while ConformanceReport (richer: max_diff, tolerance_used, oracle_status) is never persisted; run_differential_test results lose detail at the disk boundary
description:
Review of crates/fsci-conformance/src/lib.rs on 2026-04-22:

Two parallel result structs coexist:

  PacketReport (line 1399):
      packet_id, family,
      case_results: Vec<CaseResult>,  -- CaseResult = {case_id, passed, message}
      passed_cases, failed_cases,
      generated_unix_ms

  ConformanceReport (line 7601):
      fixture_path, packet_id, family,
      pass_count, fail_count,
      oracle_status,
      per_case_results: Vec<DifferentialCaseResult>,
          -- DifferentialCaseResult = {case_id, passed, message, max_diff,
                                         tolerance_used, oracle_status}
      generated_unix_ms

Field naming diverges: passed_cases vs pass_count, case_results vs
per_case_results. Structurally:
- PacketReport is CaseResult-carrying (3 fields per case).
- ConformanceReport is DifferentialCaseResult-carrying (6 fields per case
  including max_diff and tolerance_used).

What each is used for:
- PacketReport is written to parity_report.json (write_parity_artifacts
  at lib.rs:6572-6597) and read by dashboard.rs:6546 via
  load_packet_reports. The artifact pipeline is PacketReport-typed.
- ConformanceReport is RETURNED by run_differential_test but never
  SERIALIZED to a persistent artifact. Its max_diff and tolerance_used
  fields stay in-memory only.

Consequences:

1. Data loss at serialization boundary. If a conformance case fails
   with 'expected=3.0, got=3.001, max_diff=1e-3', the max_diff value
   exists in ConformanceReport::per_case_results but is DROPPED when
   results get serialized to parity_report.json (which only stores
   CaseResult.message as a free-text string).

2. Dashboard consumers see message strings only -- no structured diff
   or tolerance info. Forensics classify_failure (per vp77) attempts
   substring matching on message strings because that's all that
   survives serialization.

3. Developers maintaining the suite must mentally bridge two parallel
   schemas. Adding a new result field in one struct -- e.g., elapsed_ms
   in ConformanceReport -- silently does NOT appear in the persistent
   artifact unless PacketReport is also updated. Divergence accrues.

4. No #[serde(flatten)] or shared trait links them. Independent evolution
   guaranteed.

Fix:
1. MINIMAL: Have write_parity_artifacts accept ConformanceReport OR
   derive a conversion From<ConformanceReport> for PacketReport that's
   lossless if possible.
2. BETTER: unify the two into a single DifferentialPacketReport struct
   with rich per-case fields. Dashboard adapts to consume the richer
   struct. CaseResult retires.
3. ADD: a #[serde(tag = 'schema_version')] discriminator so parity_
   report.json consumers can distinguish versions and migrate.

Related: vp77 (forensics substring matching because diff is lost),
7h9o (dashboard distorts view), fytm (evidence parity_report is
self-check), c7b4 (docstring misleads). Yet another layer of
schema-fragmentation dysfunction in the conformance stack.
close_reason: Verified the richer PacketReport schema and automatic differential parity artifact persistence already present on HEAD; validated with rch differential/dashboard tests and fsci-conformance check.

title: [perf] RCM start-node selection O(C·V) -> O(V log V): csgraph reverse_cuthill_mckee
description: reverse_cuthill_mckee picks each connected component's start node via (0..n).filter(!visited).min_by_key(degree) — an O(V) scan PER COMPONENT, so O(C·V) = O(V^2) for fragmented graphs (many components), vs scipy's O(V+E). Fix: pre-sort node indices by (degree, index) once (stable sort => ties by ascending index, IDENTICAL to min_by_key's lowest-index-min-degree), maintain a pointer advancing past visited nodes => O(V log V + V) total for all component starts. Byte-identical RCM ordering (same start selection + same BFS). Connected graphs (C=1) unaffected (single O(V) scan was already cheap); the win is for fragmented/block-diagonal patterns. Required: rch baseline on a many-component graph, golden byte-identity, Score>=2.0, close.
close_reason: RCM start-node selection O(C·V)->O(V log V): replaced per-component min_by_key(degree) O(V) scan with a one-time stable sort of nodes by (degree,index) + advancing cursor. Byte-identical ordering (same min-degree/lowest-index start + same BFS) verified by reverse_cuthill_mckee_matches_min_scan_reference_bit_for_bit test (full-permutation assert_eq vs inline old impl, fragmented + mixed graphs). rch fragmented graph (8000 nodes, 4000 components): 19.18->0.31ms = 61.4x (run2 70.9x), orderings_match=true. 311 sparse tests pass. Closes vs-scipy gap (scipy O(V+E)). Artifacts tests/artifacts/perf/2026-06-08-sparse-rcm-0h8fz/.

title: [code-review] [HIGH] fsci-special lambertw_scalar(1.0) returns NaN due to bad initial-guess threshold
description: lambertw_scalar at x=1 returns NaN. The initial-guess branch is 'if x < 1.0 { x } else { x.ln() - x.ln().ln() }'. At x = 1.0 (and any x where ln(x) ≤ 0), the else branch evaluates ln(ln(1)) = ln(0) = -∞, so the initial guess is +∞ and Halley's iteration diverges. Reproduce: lambertw_scalar(1.0). Expected: W(1) ≈ 0.5671432904... (Omega constant). Fix: change threshold to 'x < std::f64::consts::E' (≈ 2.718) so the regular-x branch is used until x.ln() > 0, or use a safe analytic approximation. File: crates/fsci-special/src/convenience.rs:2706-2707.
close_reason: Fixed: changed initial-guess threshold from x < 1.0 to x < e and use Bürmann seed x/(1+x) for the small-x branch. lambertw_scalar(1.0) now returns 0.5671432904 (Omega constant) and tightened MR38 metamorphic test to require finite output for all positive x including 1.0. 66/66 fsci-special metamorphic tests pass.

title: [parity-gap] spherical_in forward recurrence diverges for moderate n at small x
description:
Same defect family as the just-closed [frankenscipy-xlci0] for spherical_jn. spherical_in_nonneg (crates/fsci-special/src/bessel.rs:1649) uses forward recurrence i_{k+1}(x) = i_{k-1}(x) − (2k+1)/x · i_k(x), which catastrophically cancels when x ≪ 2k+1 because i_n(x) decays super-exponentially in n while the prefactor (2k+1)/x grows.

For x=0.1 the recurrence collapses past n=5:

  n   forward (broken)   series truth
  ─   ─────────────────  ──────────────
  5   +4.04e−9           +9.62e−10        (4× too big)
  6   −3.39e−7           +6.42e−12        (wrong sign)
  9   +1.12               +5.34e−18        (completely wrong)
  10  −213                +7.3e−21         (wrong by 23 orders)

Repro:
  let x = 0.1f64;
  let mut i_prev = x.sinh()/x;
  let mut i_curr = x.cosh()/x - x.sinh()/(x*x);
  for k in 1..10 { let next = i_prev - (2.0*k as f64 + 1.0)/x * i_curr; i_prev = i_curr; i_curr = next; }
  // i_curr now ~ +1.12 instead of +5.34e-18

Fix: switch to Miller's downward recurrence in the n ≥ 2 ∧ |x| < n regime, exactly mirroring the spherical_jn_nonneg fix. The downward recurrence for i_n is:
  i_{k-1}(x) = (2k+1)/x · i_k(x) + i_{k+1}(x)
Stable from any starting value, with normalization against the analytic i_0(x) = sinh(x)/x.

Acceptance: spherical_in(5, 0.1) within 1% of x^5/11!! · (1 + x²/26); spherical_in(10, 0.1) positive and < 1e-15; existing spherical_in tests still pass.

title: add pbwa (parabolic cylinder function W and derivative)
description: Complete the parabolic cylinder trio. Add scipy's pbwa(a,x) -> (W(a,x), W'(a,x)), the real oscillatory solution of y''+(x^2/4-a)y=0 (DLMF 12.14). W=2^{-3/4}[sqrt(G1/G3)y1 - sqrt2 sqrt(G3/G1)y2], G1=|Gamma(1/4+ia/2)|, G3=|Gamma(3/4+ia/2)|, y1/y2 even/odd real power series with c_{k+2}=[a c_k - c_{k-2}/4]/((k+2)(k+1)). Matches scipy on its |a|<=5,|x|<=5 domain (NaN outside, as scipy). Verified vs scipy 1.17.1 <=2e-10. KEY: series break must require consecutive small terms (interspersed zero coeffs at a=0 trap a single-term break).
close_reason: implemented and verified vs scipy 1.17.1

title: [perf][fsci-linalg] solve_banded band-storage O(n·bw) memory + banded backward-error
description: FOLLOW-UP to ddcb822d (banded GEPP shipped, 9.5-56x). The banded solve still materializes a full dense n×n buffer via dense_from_banded (O(n^2) time+mem) and computes backward error over the dense matrix (O(n^2)). At large n (e.g. 4000) this O(n^2) is now the dominant cost and caps the win + uses 128MB. LEVER: operate banded_gepp_solve directly on LAPACK-style band storage ((2*kl+ku+1)×n) instead of a dense buffer, and compute backward_error in banded form (O(n·bw)). Result: true O(n·kl·(kl+ku)) time and O(n·bw) memory — full BLAS/LAPACK-class. Parity: must still match dense path to 1e-10 (evidence_p2c002 gate) and SciPy to 1e-8 (diff_linalg_structured_solvers). Re-bench at n=1000-4000 (add baseline sizes to linalg_bench solve_banded) to capture the now-uncapped scaling. Same one-lever/proof discipline.

title: [stats] ExponPow entropy/moments ~1e-4 off scipy — Simpson defeated by t^(k/b) and ln(u) endpoint singularities
description: exponpow(b=2.7): fsci entropy=-0.0246027 vs scipy/truth -0.0246262 (rel 9.5e-4); skew/kurt/var also off ~1e-4..1e-5. scipy matches tight-quad truth exactly. Cause: exponpow_moment integrates t^(k/b)exp(t-e^t) on a fixed Simpson t-grid; the t^(k/b) (k/b<1) endpoint has unbounded higher derivatives -> Simpson O(h^4) fails. Entropy uses a Gompertz decomposition whose E_U[ln U] integral has a ln(u) singularity at 0. Fix: substitute t=u^2 in exponpow_moment (Jacobian softens endpoint -> err 8e-7->8e-13); compute entropy directly via the same u-sub (the 2u Jacobian kills u*ln u -> err 9.5e-4->5e-10). Found via diff_exotic_entropy probe + mpmath/quad truth.
close_reason: Fixed in 6a800ad4: t=u^2 substitution in exponpow_moment (Jacobian softens t^(k/b) endpoint, moment err 8e-7->1e-13) + direct u-sub entropy (2u kills u*ln u singularity, entropy err 9.5e-4->2e-8). exponpow(2.7) now matches scipy/quad-truth. 1836 tests pass.

title: [HIGH] conformance: execute_linalg_case_with_differential_audit at lib.rs:6801 only wires audit ledger for Solve variant — Inv/Det/Lstsq/Pinv/SolveTriangular/SolveBanded (6 operations) fall through to non-audit variant via  at 6835
description:
Review of crates/fsci-conformance/src/lib.rs:6801-6837 on 2026-04-22:

execute_linalg_case_with_differential_audit claims 'differential audit' --
it takes a SyncSharedAuditLedger parameter and threads it into
fsci_linalg::solve_with_audit. Good for the Solve variant.

But line 6835 fallback:

    _ => execute_linalg_case(case),

falls through to the non-audit variant for every OTHER LinalgCase
variant (Inv, Det, Lstsq, Pinv, SolveTriangular, SolveBanded). That
function at lib.rs:6639 calls fsci_linalg::inv / det / lstsq / pinv /
etc. WITHOUT any audit ledger argument. fsci-linalg's bare APIs
(grep pub fn) don't accept an audit ledger -- only the solve_with_*
family does.

Consequences:
1. For conformance cases with operation != 'solve', the audit ledger
   captures ZERO events even in Hardened mode.
2. run_differential_linalg (lib.rs:7817) emits audit_ledger.jsonl at
   line 7854 only if ledger.is_empty() is false. If all cases in a
   packet are Inv/Det/Lstsq/Pinv/..., the ledger is empty and no
   file is emitted.
3. The FSCI-P2C-002 linalg fixture distribution is:
       solve: 15, inv: 9, det: 8, solve_triangular: 6,
       lstsq: 6, pinv: 6, solve_banded: 3
   So 15/53 = 28% of cases get audited; 38/53 = 72% do not.

This is a narrower instance of egba (crate-wide audit emission gap).
Fixing requires:
1. fsci_linalg to expose _with_audit variants for inv / det / lstsq /
   pinv / solve_triangular / solve_banded.
2. execute_linalg_case_with_differential_audit to dispatch each
   variant to its _with_audit counterpart.

Related: egba (11/18 crates emit zero AuditAction), mhuk (runner
wires ledger only for 3 of 12 families), xo4o (Hardened coverage
2.9%), 95ld (5 families ignore mode: String), ovxs (audit type
fragmentation). This is the 6th layer of the audit-trail bug stack.
close_reason: Added audit-aware wrappers for inv/det/lstsq/pinv/solve_triangular/solve_banded in fsci-linalg, routed all six through execute_linalg_case_with_differential_audit, and added a non-Solve differential audit regression. rch cargo test/check passed for fsci-linalg and fsci-conformance; conformance clippy remains blocked only by preexisting unrelated fsci-spatial/fsci-stats warnings.

title: [test][linalg] fsci-linalg suite is LOAD-FLAKY -- bit-identity and determinism tests fail 2 of 3 runs on a CLEAN tree
description:
`cargo test -p fsci-linalg --lib` fails intermittently under host load, on DIFFERENT tests
each time. Measured 2026-08-19 with a paired control, on a CLEAN tree (no local edits):

    clean tree, 3 consecutive runs, host loadavg 104-168:
      run 1  FAILED  574 passed, 2 failed
      run 2  FAILED  574 passed, 2 failed
      run 3  ok      576 passed, 0 failed

Same command, same commit, same binary. An earlier clean run at loadavg ~38 passed, so the
trigger is load, not a code change.

## The tests that flake are exactly the ones asserting determinism

Observed failures so far:

  - `tests::randomized_eigh_matches_full_eigh_on_low_rank` — fails at
    `assert_eq!(re.eigenvalues, repeat.eigenvalues)`, i.e. `randomized_eigh` called TWICE on
    the same input returned different values.
  - `toggle_ab_eigh_rank2_update::rank2_update_rewrite_is_bit_identical` — fails with
    "EIGH_RANK2_UPDATE_FORCE_SCALAR is documented BIT-IDENTICAL and is not: eigenvalues
    first differ at index Some(0)".

Both PASS in isolation and with `--test-threads=1`.

## The likely mechanism, and what would confirm or refute it

These paths use parallel reductions whose fold structure depends on the number of worker
threads actually available. Under concurrent test load, two calls in the same test see
different effective rayon occupancy, so they reassociate differently and produce different
bits. If that is right, the toggles are not "bit-identical" as documented — they are
bit-identical AT A FIXED THREAD COUNT, which is a weaker and different contract.

TO CONFIRM: pin the rayon pool to one thread for the duration of these tests (or assert the
observed worker count inside them) and re-run under load. If they stop flaking, the
thread-count dependence is established and the doc contracts need amending to say so. If
they still flake, the nondeterminism is elsewhere and this analysis is wrong.

## Why it matters more than a flaky test usually does

This crate uses bit-identity assertions as the PRIMARY safety net for its perf toggles —
`no_new_perf_toggle_may_ship_without_an_accuracy_contract` exists to enforce exactly that.
If those assertions are themselves load-dependent, then:
  - a REAL bit-identity regression can be dismissed as "the usual flake", and
  - a green suite on a quiet worker does not mean what it is being read to mean.

That is the masked-drift half of the known global-toggle hazard, arriving through thread
count rather than through a shared toggle.

## Scope note

NOT caused by the SYRK NC-blocking lever landed alongside this bead. That was the initial
suspicion and the paired clean-tree control above refuted it: the clean tree flakes at the
same rate. Recorded because a wrong attribution here would have sent someone hunting a
kernel bug that is not there.

Found 2026-08-19 by MistyBear.

title: [capability][linalg] eigh_tridiagonal has no subset selection -- scipy select/select_range has no equivalent
description:
Found and landed 2026-08-16 (RainyPrairie) while looking for capability gaps on eigh, the project's worst measured vs-incumbent ratio.

THE GAP. scipy.linalg.eigh_tridiagonal takes select and select_range; scipy.linalg.eigh takes subset_by_index and subset_by_value. fsci-linalg had NEITHER -- DecompOptions carries only { mode, check_finite }, and eigh_tridiagonal always computes the FULL eigenvector set through symmetric_tridiagonal_qr_eigen even when the caller wants three eigenpairs out of five hundred.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND PARITY. Eigenvector accumulation is what dominates the eigh deficit against LAPACK dsyevd. Restricting to k of n columns does not make the work faster, it skips it. This is the only lever found so far on that ratio that removes work rather than rescheduling it -- the blocked dsytrd reduction measured SLOWER (0.5-0.81x) and the clustering gate was refuted as the cause.

LANDED: eigh_tridiagonal_subset(d, e, select_range, eigvals_only, options), matching scipy's select='i' semantics -- select_range is INCLUSIVE at both ends and indexes the ascending spectrum. Eigenvalues come from eigh_tridiagonal(.., true, ..) so the d/e contract, check_finite and the hardened dimension policy are validated exactly once and the subset path cannot drift from the full path on validation. Eigenvectors are computed by inverse iteration for the selected indices only, with the ORIGINAL column index threaded through, so restricting the range does not change the numbers.

TWO CORRECTNESS FALLBACKS, both to the full solve: a cluster straddling the requested range would need neighbours outside the selection to re-orthogonalise against, and a failed inverse iteration is exactly the case QR exists for. Neither is slower than what callers had before this function existed.

TESTS: scipy golden for select_range=(1,3) on d=[1..5], e=[0.5;4] -> [1.9765560195969027, 2.9999999999999996, 4.023443980403098] with an n x 3 block; per-column residual T*v = lambda*v; BIT-IDENTITY of the selected columns against the unrestricted inverse iteration; eigvals_only returning None; a single-index range; and a must-miss arm asserting invalid ranges are REFUSED rather than silently clamped, which is the failure mode this campaign keeps finding elsewhere.

544 passed / 0 failed / 42 ignored, fsci-linalg lib, rch worker vmi1149989.

NOT DONE: subset_by_value (select='v'), and subset selection on the DENSE eigh entry point. Both are natural follow-ups on this foundation.
close_reason: Landed in this commit: eigh_tridiagonal_subset with scipy select=i semantics, inverse iteration over the selected indices only, two correctness fallbacks to the full solve, and tests covering the scipy golden, residual, bit-identity against the unrestricted inverse iteration, eigvals_only, a single-index range and refusal of invalid ranges. 544/0 on vmi1149989.

title: [test][sparse] 6 RED tests on main: PerfToggle load counter is process-global, so concurrent tests inflate it
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-15 (SandyFern), two-arm control on RCH worker vmi1227854.

Clean HEAD (--base HEAD --clean-overlay --no-overlay): cargo test -p fsci-sparse --lib => 442 passed, 6 FAILED.
Same command with unrelated working-tree changes: 448 passed, the SAME 6 failed. So these are RED on main, not caused by any in-flight work.

The 6:
  perf_toggle_tests::sparse_diagonal_force_serial_reads_the_toggle_and_preserves_output
  perf_toggle_tests::sparse_eliminate_zeros_force_serial_reads_the_toggle_and_preserves_output
  perf_toggle_tests::sparse_row_max_force_serial_reads_the_toggle_and_preserves_output
  perf_toggle_tests::sparse_row_sums_force_serial_reads_the_toggle_and_preserves_output
  tests::splu_periodic_cuboid_toggle_dispatches_and_rejects_a_changed_stencil
  tests::spsolve_periodic_cuboid_toggle_is_read_and_preserves_the_solution

ROOT CAUSE of the first four: PerfToggle::loads is a process-global AtomicUsize. Each test does store(true) / reset_load_count() / call kernel / assert_eq!(load_count(), 1). cargo test runs the crate's tests concurrently in ONE process, and every other test that calls a kernel reading the same toggle increments the same counter. sparse_row_max and sparse_row_sums even share SPARSE_ROW_MINMAX_FORCE_SERIAL, so they race each other by construction. Observed left: 7, right: 1.

Every toggle load site in linalg.rs is on the CALLER's thread (they gate a worker-count decision before any spawn), so a per-thread load count is both correct and sufficient for the anti-vacuity detector that qcuyy added these toggles for. Do NOT relax the assertion to a range -- the count is the gate that distinguishes a live A/B from an A/A over identical code.

The last two are a separate numeric failure (spectral vs native solution diverges beyond 1e-10); the spsolve one reports PoisonError from the shared cubic test lock, i.e. it is a cascade of the splu panic, not an independent defect.

NEGATIVE CASE a fix must still pass: perf_toggle_tests::dispatch_observed_is_false_when_the_probe_ignores_the_toggle must keep reporting a probe that never reads the toggle as vacuous.
close_reason: Fixed in d5eef9471 (per-thread PerfToggle load counts + load_counts_do_not_leak_between_threads regression test) and 1693edba2 (periodic-cuboid arms held to a 1e-8 relative-residual bound each, replacing an unachievable elementwise 1e-10 cross-solver bound; native arm's residual now asserted for the first time). EVIDENCE: RCH remote-only, cargo test -p fsci-sparse --lib = 455 passed / 0 failed (vmi1153651), against the clean-HEAD control (--base HEAD --clean-overlay --no-overlay) at 442 passed / 6 failed. Measured numbers behind the tolerance change: spectral residual 1.835e-12, native residual 2.958e-12, elementwise gap 5.043e-10. Negative control observed both arms: native bound tightened to 1e-14 fails and prints the real residual; at 1e-8 it passes. The originating commit 992770eb1 does not compile its lib test target (E0004/E0282), so the old bound never ran green.

title: [infra] rch scheduler ignores worker capability tags — ISA-aware selection is exclusion-only
description:
Split out of frankenscipy-hhr7j (closed 2026-08-08).

hhr7j is closed because the SIGILL vector is gone: ovh-b is 'enabled = false' in
~/.config/rch/workers.toml and is absent from rch's own pool (rch workers list -> 11
workers, ovh-b not among them). Verified by routing the exact command that SIGILLed
twice on 2026-07-22 (cargo clippy -p fsci-linalg): it landed on vmi1156319, exit=0.

What is NOT fixed is the underlying capability model. Fix option (b) from hhr7j --
tag ovh-b 'no-avx2' and have ISA-sensitive lanes exclude that tag -- WAS applied and
FAILED: on 2026-07-31 a strict Rust build was still auto-selected onto ovh-b despite
the recorded rust-tag removal, and SIGILLed in num-traits build-script-build. So rch
selection does not honor capability tags for admission; the only lever that works is
disabling the whole worker, which also throws away its Bun/Go capacity (3 slots).

This is an rch-side change, not a frankenscipy one. Recorded here so the knowledge is
not lost if ovh-b is ever re-enabled on health grounds (it has been twice before --
capability, not health, is why it must stay out of Rust lanes).

CLOSING EVIDENCE: a worker tagged as lacking an ISA is left ENABLED, and a Rust build
with -C target-feature=+avx2,+fma is submitted repeatedly (>=20 times) without ever
being scheduled onto it, while a Bun or Go job still is.

description:

ISOMORPHISM: bit-identical (each m[i][j] still accumulates k in 0..n order). Proof: test reordered==naive exactly. Same for the aligned=mtx2@rotation loop (rotation[k][j] column-strided). that "freqs_zpk lacks ZPK length/finite checks". In crates/fsci-signal/src/lib.rs:

Nothing was implemented.

DEDUP VERIFICATION -- COVERAGE: a sibling test
analog_frequency_responses_reject_non_finite_inputs already exists and covers a
non-finite zero, a non-finite frequency and a zeros length mismatch on
freqs_zpk, a non-finite numerator and frequency on freqs, and a non-finite
frequency on bode.

PROCESS NOTE: my first grep for rejection tests missed that sibling because it
searched for test names containing the function names, and this one does not
contain any. I only found it when the new test's name filter matched it during
the first run. I had by then written a broad test that duplicated roughly half
of it. Rather than commit the overlap I trimmed the new test down to the
genuinely uncovered guards -- committing duplicate coverage would have been the
conformance-metastasis pattern the suite rules name explicitly.

WHAT THE NEW TEST ACTUALLY ADDS (each is a distinct guard in the source that had
no test): EMPTY inputs on all three entry points (empty w on freqs_zpk; empty
b/a/w on freqs; empty num/den on bode); the POLES length mismatch, where only
the zeros side was checked; a non-finite GAIN across NaN/+inf/-inf; the
DENOMINATOR coefficient path on freqs; and BOTH coefficient paths on bode. It
also asserts up front that the valid fixture succeeds, so each rejection is
attributable to the single thing changed rather than to a broken fixture.

DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE, recorded in the test comment so it is not mistaken for
parity: these guards are STRICTER than SciPy. Measured on scipy 1.17.1, SciPy
has no fail-closed contract here -- with an explicit frequency grid it
propagates NaN rather than raising:
    scipy.signal.freqs([1,1],[1,1], worN=[nan,1]) -> [nan+nanj, 1+0j]
    scipy.signal.freqs_zpk([nan], [1], 1)         -> all nan+nanj
    scipy.signal.freqs_zpk([], [], k=nan)         -> all nan+nanj
Where SciPy does raise -- freqs([nan,1],[1,1]) and bode(([nan,1],[1,1])) give
LinAlgError "Array must not contain infs or NaNs" -- that is INCIDENTAL, thrown
by the automatic worN grid calling roots(), not a validation decision. This is
the same stricter-than-SciPy pattern recorded for the CZT family in
frankenscipy-drb0i, and it is the SECOND bead in this 2026-06-18
"reject non-finite" cohort whose premise conflicts with Strict-mode parity.
The tests pin fsci's chosen contract, not SciPy's behaviour; no behaviour was
changed here.

evidence without it):

      series implemented in the special crate — for a measured 9-40x (cdf) and
      38-102x (ppf). Verified the public path actually calls the kernel now:
      lib.rs:1815, :1831, :1848.

  cross_set_l1_pair_sum / within_set_l1_pair_sum
      These are the SORTING WRAPPERS, and the distinction is the whole answer:
      the kernels they delegate to (*_l1_pair_sum_sorted) are LIVE and carry
      energy_distance. 8de105e9b moved energy_distance to sort u and v once up
      front and call the sorted kernels directly (1.8-2x self), leaving only the
      sort-then-call convenience layer unreachable.

So there is a named, faster, live replacement in every case. NOTHING HERE IS A LOST CAPABILITY — the opposite of frankenscipy-1b85n, where the cluster bench keeps a private copy of a lever the library no longer ships and the dispatch is simply missing. Worth contrasting explicitly so the two are not treated as the same finding.

NOT DELETED, per the repo's no-deletion rule and on merit: the nct pair is the in-crate reference for the Lenth series, and the L1 wrappers document the naive-order semantics the sorted kernels have to match. Each now carries allow(dead_code) whose comment names the replacement AND the commit that made it, so nobody has to redo this archaeology.

title: [cluster] agglomerate_nnarray NN-array linkage lever is dead code — its call site is gone and the bench keeps a private copy
description:
Found by RusticCarp 2026-08-05 while reconciling fsci-cluster (frankenscipy-ecrbb).

crates/fsci-cluster/src/lib.rs defines agglomerate_nnarray (the nearest-neighbour-array linkage lever) plus its helpers agglo_idx and agglo_nearest. NOTHING CALLS agglomerate_nnarray. Verified: exactly one occurrence in the crate, the definition itself; agglo_idx/agglo_nearest are called only from inside it, so the whole cluster is unreachable.

This is NOT collateral from the bulk-deletion series. The occurrence counts are IDENTICAL in 1d999e235^ (the pre-deletion parent) and at HEAD after the reconciliation: transpose_rows 1, agglo_idx 7, agglo_nearest 3, agglomerate_nnarray 1. So it was already dead BEFORE that commit — a separate, earlier unwiring.

Corroborating: crates/fsci-cluster/benches/cluster_bench.rs carries its own private copy named legacy_agglomerate_nnarray and benchmarks THAT, not the library function. So the bench still measures the lever while the library no longer ships it — exactly the shape that lets a ledgered win drift away from shipped behaviour. Compare frankenscipy-ct8n2.

transpose_rows is dead the same way (1 occurrence, definition only).

DECIDE, and say which in the close reason:
 (a) Re-wire it. linkage() should dispatch to agglomerate_nnarray where the
     NN-array algorithm wins. That is a PERF change and needs the full protocol:
     live incumbent arm in the same invocation, A/A null, byte-identity or a
     stated tolerance. Do not re-land it on the strength of the old number.
 (b) Formally retire it. Then the bench's legacy_ copy is the only home and that
     should be said in a comment, so nobody mistakes the bench result for a
     library capability.

DO NOT simply delete the functions to silence the lint — they are a reference
implementation and deletion needs explicit permission.

INTERIM: ecrbb marks them #[allow(dead_code)] with a comment pointing here, so
the clippy gate is not left red. That allow should be removed by whichever branch
above is taken.

EVIDENCE TO CLOSE: either a measured A/B showing the re-wired dispatch (branch a),
or the retirement comment plus removal of the interim allow (branch b).
close_reason:
Closed 2026-08-08 (TopazOsprey). The bead asked for a decision -- re-wire or
formally retire -- and named a "full measured A/B" as the price of re-wiring.
The decision is now settled on CORRECTNESS evidence, which is cheaper and
stronger than a perf A/B: re-wiring is ruled out regardless of speed.

VERIFIED FIRST: still unwired at HEAD. Nothing in the library calls
agglomerate_nnarray; agglo_idx/agglo_nearest are reachable only from it. The
bead's recorded occurrence counts have since changed (it recorded
agglomerate_nnarray = 1, I measure 3) but the delta is only the explanatory
comments added by 02a7045cc, not a re-wiring.

WHY RE-WIRING IS RULED OUT. The shipped path is `linkage` -> `linkage_from_dm`,
which routes Single to an MST, Centroid/Median to the Müller heap, and the rest
to NN-chain -- asymptotically better routes than a plain nearest-neighbour
array. So agglomerate_nnarray is a SUPERSEDED intermediate, not a lost lever.
Cross-validating the two implementations bitwise on a 7-point fixture:
    Single, Complete, Average, Weighted -> BIT-IDENTICAL (0 ulp)
    Ward                                -> differs by exactly 1 ulp at row 2 col 2
                                           shipped 1.2909944487358056
                                           unwired 1.2909944487358058
And SciPy settles it:
    scipy.cluster.hierarchy.linkage(data, 'ward')[2][2] == 1.2909944487358056
i.e. SciPy agrees with the SHIPPED value and not the unwired one. Re-wiring this
lever would move Ward 1 ulp OFF SciPy parity. Under "stability outranks speed"
that ends the argument before any timing is needed.

RECOMMENDATION: formally RETIRE (delete agglomerate_nnarray, agglo_idx,
agglo_nearest and the bench's private legacy_agglomerate_nnarray copy). I did
NOT delete them -- removal is the owner's call, and the source comment
explicitly says "Preserved, not deleted" pending this bead. Everything needed to
execute that removal safely is now recorded.

FALSE CLAIM CORRECTED: the function's docstring asserted it was "byte-identical
... element-for-element" with the pairwise scan. That is false for Ward, as
measured above. Docstring updated to state the real result and cite the test,
so the next reader does not re-derive it or trust the wrong invariant.

LANDED: unwired_agglomerate_nnarray_is_bit_identical_to_the_shipped_linkage.
It asserts bit-equality for the four agreeing methods, pins the shipped Ward
value to SciPy's, asserts the unwired one still differs, and asserts the gap is
exactly 1 ulp. It also stops the code bit-rotting while it sits behind
#[allow(dead_code)]: an unwired function with no test can drift silently, and
drift is what makes the eventual removal expensive to justify.

SECONDARY CONCERN FROM THE BEAD, unresolved and left open on purpose: the bench
still measures its own private copy, and that copy has DIVERGED -- it takes
Vec<Vec<f64>> where the library version takes a flat Vec<f64>. So the bench is
not merely measuring an unshipped lever, it is measuring an older variant of it.
Retiring the library code should remove the bench copy in the same change;
noted here rather than split, since it is one removal.

EVIDENCE via RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec, with `Compiling fsci-cluster`
confirmed in every run log (per frankenscipy-eibro a remote green is not
evidence without it):
  - cargo test -p fsci-cluster --lib -> 150 tests, 150 passed, 0 failed, exit=0.
  - TWO-ARM CONTROL, observed twice. Naturally: the test FAILED on its first run
    with "Ward row 2 col 2: shipped 1.2909944487358056 vs unwired nnarray
    1.2909944487358058", which is how the divergence was found rather than
    assumed. Explicitly: swapping the SciPy golden to the unwired value makes
    the load-bearing assertion fail with "shipped Ward must stay bit-equal to
    scipy at the known divergence point". Restored, suite re-verified green.
  - cargo fmt -p fsci-cluster -- --check: clean. Two hunks: the docstring
    correction and the new test, 104 insertions.

title: [perf][io] mmread coordinate parser materializes a Vec<str> per entry; pull fields off the split iterator
close_reason:
Closed 2026-08-08 (TopazOsprey). The optimization is already implemented; what
landed is a regression test for a non-local safety property found while
verifying it.

DEDUP VERIFICATION: the bead (title only, no description) asks that the mmread
coordinate parser stop materializing a Vec<&str> per entry and pull fields off
the split iterator. That is already the code. All THREE mmread entry-parsing
paths use the iterator form -- crates/fsci-io/src/lib.rs:322 (dense coordinate),
:521 (array), :648 (sparse) -- each as `let mut fields = trimmed
.split_whitespace();` followed by `fields.next()`. Line 320 even carries a
comment describing the change as byte-identical. A sweep for per-entry
`.split(..).collect()` in the crate returns nothing; the remaining `Vec<&str>`
sites (:2642, :2886, :4188) collect LINES once per file, not fields per entry,
so they are not this lever. Nothing was implemented.

NO PERF CLAIM IS MADE. The lever is already in; I measured no ratio and none is
asserted here. Recording that explicitly because this bead is typed `perf` and a
closure without a number could otherwise be read as an unmeasured win.

WHAT THE VERIFICATION TURNED UP. A short entry line (fewer than two tokens) hits
a bare `continue`. Read locally that looks like silent data loss -- a truncated
file loading with entries quietly missing -- and SciPy rejects such a file
(ValueError "Line 4: Invalid integer value."), so a divergence looked likely.

I PROBED IT RATHER THAN INFERRING, and the inference was WRONG. fsci also
rejects:
    InvalidFormat("coordinate format expected 3 entries but found 2")
The declared-nnz count backstops the skip, so the entry cannot vanish silently.
Both implementations fail closed; there is no parity gap. Worth stating plainly
because I had drafted this as a defect before the probe corrected it -- the
third time this session that measuring first overturned a plausible-looking
conclusion.

LANDED: mmread_rejects_truncated_coordinate_entry_via_nnz_backstop. It pins the
rejection and its diagnostic, and includes an intact-file control so the failure
is attributable to the truncation rather than to the fixture. The test is
justified by the safety being NON-LOCAL: it lives in the nnz check, not at the
`continue`. Anyone relaxing or removing that count check would convert the skip
into real silent data loss, and nothing else in the suite would notice.

EVIDENCE via RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec, with `Compiling fsci-io` confirmed
in every run log (per frankenscipy-eibro a remote green is not evidence without
it):
  - cargo test -p fsci-io --lib -> 137 tests, 137 passed, 0 failed, exit=0.
  - TWO-ARM CONTROL: the probe form of this test was written to panic on BOTH
    branches, so it reported the real behaviour instead of confirming a guess --
    it printed "PROBE: mmread rejected with InvalidFormat(...)", which is how the
    draft defect was refuted. The shipped test then carries an intact-file
    control that must load.
  - cargo fmt -p fsci-io -- --check: clean. Diff is one purely additive hunk,
    43 insertions, 0 deletions.

title: Oracle capture coverage is incomplete across P2C packet families
description:
Review/testing sweep after DB recovery on 2026-04-28 compared packet fixtures, python_oracle scripts, and artifact captures. There are 17 packet fixtures (FSCI-P2C-001 through FSCI-P2C-017) and oracle scripts for many domains, but committed oracle_capture.json artifacts exist only for P2C-002, P2C-003, P2C-005, P2C-006, P2C-007, P2C-012, P2C-014, P2C-015, P2C-016, and P2C-017. No oracle_capture.json was found for P2C-001, P2C-004, P2C-008, P2C-009, P2C-010, P2C-011, or P2C-013.

Why this matters:
- README.md still frames real oracle capture and drift diffs as a core conformance workflow.
- The repo has scipy_sparse_oracle.py, scipy_cluster_oracle.py, scipy_spatial_oracle.py, scipy_signal_oracle.py, and scipy_integrate_oracle.py, so several missing capture families have an apparent oracle path.
- Without an explicit coverage matrix, it is unclear which packet families are genuinely differential, intentionally self-checking, or simply missing capture artifacts.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Add a machine-readable or test-enforced oracle-capture coverage matrix for all FSCI-P2C packet families.
2. Generate and commit oracle_capture.json for the missing families where a real SciPy oracle script exists and fixture semantics permit it.
3. For families that should not have oracle capture, document the reason in the matrix and ensure dashboard/report wording does not call them oracle-backed.
4. Add a regression test that fails when a packet fixture has an oracle script but neither an oracle capture artifact nor an explicit documented exemption.

title: Implement closed-form moments for Burr12, InvWeibull, TukeyLambda, GenHalfLogistic distributions
description:
## Context
Audit found 7 distribution moment methods returning f64::NAN as stubs where closed-form
formulas exist using only Gamma/Beta functions and harmonic numbers (already available in
fsci-special).

## Scope
All changes in crates/fsci-stats/src/lib.rs:

1. **Burr12::var()** (line ~3258) — Currently returns NaN with comment "Complex formula,
   return NaN for now". Formula: var = E[X²] - (E[X])², where E[X^r] =
   d·Γ(d-r/c)·Γ(1+r/c)/Γ(d+1) when c·d > r. Guard: return NaN when c·d ≤ 2.

2. **InvWeibull::var()** (line ~3712) — Formula: Γ(1-2/c) - Γ(1-1/c)² when c > 2.
   Guard: return NaN when c ≤ 2 (infinite variance).

3. **TukeyLambda::var()** (line ~3668) — Formula:
   var = 2·(1/(1+2λ) - Γ(λ+1)²/Γ(2λ+2))/λ² for λ ≠ 0.
   Special case λ=0: var = π²/3.

4. **GenHalfLogistic::mean()** (line ~3599) — Formula: mean = (1/c)·(H(1/c) + γ) where
   H is harmonic number and γ is Euler-Mascheroni. Alternatively:
   mean = (1-1/c)·∫₀¹ t^(1/c-1)·(-ln(1-t)) dt — use digamma: mean = (ψ(1/c+1) + γ)/c.

5. **GenHalfLogistic::var()** (line ~3604) — Formula: var = E[X²] - mean².
   E[X²] = (ψ₁(1/c+1) + (ψ(1/c+1)+γ)²)/c² where ψ₁ is trigamma.

## Testing Requirements
- Unit tests comparing each moment to SciPy reference values (≥3 parameter combos each)
- Test boundary cases (e.g., Burr12 with c·d near 2, InvWeibull with c near 2)
- Test that existing pdf/cdf/ppf behavior is unchanged
- Verify var() ≥ 0 for all valid parameters via property test
- Add to existing e2e_stats.rs as new scenario: e2e_011_closed_form_moments

## Validation
```
cargo test -p fsci-stats -- burr12
cargo test -p fsci-stats -- inv_weibull
cargo test -p fsci-stats -- tukey
cargo test -p fsci-stats -- gen_half_logistic
cargo test -p fsci-conformance --test e2e_stats
```
close_reason: Already implemented: Burr12::var(), InvWeibull::var(), TukeyLambda::var(), GenHalfLogistic::mean()/var() all have closed-form formulas in current code.

title: [measure][linalg] perf_chol_vs_scipy cannot certify n=1024 -- our own A/A null misses 1.0 at that size and no other, five times, including in a quiet window
description:
`perf_chol_vs_scipy` refuses every n=1024 cell because our own arm's A/A null misses 1.0 by
8-13%. It has never missed at any other size.

## The observations, five independent settings

| run | min_of | ambient | null_fsci | null_scipy1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 5  | ~20  | 1.112 | 1.013 |
| 2 | 9  | ~24  | 1.081 | 1.025 |
| 3 | 15 | ~22  | 1.111 | 1.022 |
| 4 | 9  | 21.21 | **1.078** | 1.014 |
| 5 | 7  | 50.03 | 1.178 | 1.023 |

The null is `max(f_a, f_b) / min(f_a, f_b)` for the two halves of an ABBA cell, each a
best-of-`min_of`. The SciPy arm's null in the SAME cells is 1.013-1.025 throughout.

## Why this is NOT contention, which is the whole point

Run 4 is decisive. It was taken in a QUIET window, ambient 21.21, and in the SAME invocation
n=256 and n=512 certified with nulls of 1.049 and 1.008. A contention-driven null would have
come in near 1.0 there alongside its neighbours. It did not.

Raising `min_of` from 5 to 9 to 15 also failed to move it. More repetitions drive a
contention-driven best-of toward the true minimum; a systematic asymmetry survives them,
which is what happened.

So this is a property of our n=1024 Cholesky path: the two halves of the cell run at
measurably different speed, reproducibly, and only at this size.

## Candidate mechanism, NOT established

The second half of the cell runs AFTER both SciPy arms have executed. At n=1024 the fixture
is 8 MB and the factor another 8 MB — small enough to sit in this Threadripper 5975WX's L3
(32 MB per CCD) and therefore vulnerable to being evicted by the 64-task `scipyN` arm between
the halves; at n=2048 (32 MB + 32 MB) both halves miss anyway, and at n=256/512 everything
stays resident. That story fits the size-specificity exactly and is UNTESTED.

## Verify

1. Run the fsci arm ALONE with no SciPy child in the invocation. If the null returns to ~1.0,
   the asymmetry is caused by the other arms and the mechanism is eviction; if it persists,
   it is internal to our factorisation at this size.
2. If it is eviction, an A-B-B-A ordering that interleaves at finer grain, or a cache-warming
   pass before each half, should collapse it — and that fix generalises to every harness in
   this repo that compares against a memory-hungry incumbent.
3. `perf stat -e LLC-load-misses` on the two halves at n=1024 against n=512 and n=2048 would
   settle it directly.

## Why it matters

n=1024 is the size where our certified vs-SciPy series has a hole: 256, 512 and 2048 are all
certified and 1024 cannot be. The uncertified readings there (scipy1/fsci 1.68-1.87x,
scipyN/fsci 1.27-1.51x) look like our best results, which is precisely why they must not be
quoted until the null behaves.

Split out of frankenscipy-8l8r1.151 on close, 2026-08-19 by MistyBear, so it does not hold
that bead open.
close_reason: done

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
2026-08-19 MistyBear — THIS BEAD'S PREMISE IS REFUTED BY REPLICATION. I filed it; it is wrong.

The premise was "our own A/A null misses 1.0 at n=1024 and at no other size, five times". The
five observations were real. The inference from them was not.

## The instrument that settled it

Added `FSCI_CHOL_NO_SCIPY` to `perf_chol_vs_scipy` (commit c4b6364f3): the identical cell —
same warmup, same ABBA halves, same best-of — with NO SciPy child in the process.

## Four mechanisms tested, all four dead

| hypothesis | verdict | what killed it |
|---|---|---|
| SciPy arm evicts our cache between halves (THIS BEAD'S OWN proposal) | REFUTED | fsci-only null is WORSE: 1.233 against 1.078-1.178 with SciPy present, while n=512 (1.014) and n=2048 (1.036) stayed clean in the same window |
| Systematic first-half warmup penalty | REFUTED | `f_a > f_b` in some replicates and `f_b > f_a` in others |
| Obtained rayon parallelism varies at the 64M-mac straddle | REFUTED | `RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1` made CV WORSE (14.61%), not better |
| Power-of-two row-stride aliasing (n=1024 → 8192 B) | REFUTED | n=1023 / 1024 / 1025 all 6.7-8.1%, no step at 1024 |

## And then the premise itself

Three consecutive repeats of the identical fsci-only measurement, same binary, same fixtures:

| repeat | host load | n=512 | n=1024 | n=2048 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| baseline | 27.8 | 1.11% | **17.64%** | 2.29% |
| a | 13.6 | **16.71%** | 6.89% | 2.27% |
| 1 | 16.2 | 3.62% | 9.15% | **21.99%** |
| 2 | ~60 | 18.53% | **28.45%** | 19.50% |
| 3 | 99.6 | 18.03% | **29.79%** | 20.13% |

The high-CV size MOVES — n=1024, then n=512, then n=2048 — and above load ~60 every size is
elevated. The variance tracks LOAD, not size. There is no n=1024 anomaly.

I had also published a six-size table whose CV peaked at 896-1024 as support for the straddle
mechanism. That was one draw from a distribution whose mode wanders, presented as a
replication. Retracted in commit 84b860aa3.

## What survives, and where it should live

1. `FSCI_CHOL_NO_SCIPY` stays — it separates "our arm" from "our arm plus the incumbent's
   footprint" in one flag, and it is what refuted this bead's own hypothesis.
2. REPLICATED: our Cholesky timing variance is large and load-sensitive at every size below
   n=2048 — CV 1% to 30%, max/min up to 2.8, same binary and fixture, no incumbent in the
   process. That is worth its own bead if anyone wants to chase it, and it is NOT this one.
3. The gate refusing n=1024 cells was never diagnosing a size; it was refusing windows, which
   is its job. Certified rows at n=256/512/2048 are unaffected.

CLOSING as refuted rather than leaving it open to attract more work on a premise that does not
replicate.

title: [perf][fsci-integrate] parallelize monte_carlo_integrate via LCG jump
description: monte_carlo_integrate drew each sample from a sequential LCG (d draws/sample) and accumulated sum/sum_sq inline. title: [parity-gap] missing scipy.special.eval_chebyc / eval_chebys (Chebyshev C, S)
description:
scipy.special.eval_chebyc(n, x) and eval_chebys(n, x) evaluate the Chebyshev polynomials of the first/second kind on the interval [-2, 2] (vs T_n, U_n on [-1, 1]). They satisfy the simple identities

  S_n(x) = U_n(x/2)

fsci ships eval_chebyt and eval_chebyu but not the C/S variants. Filing as P1 because the C/S forms appear in classical scattering and quantum-mechanical applications (dimer chain Green's functions, spectral methods on [-2, 2]).

title: [stats] VonMises.cdf uses trapezoidal integration; error grows with kappa (3.7e-6 at kappa=50)
