All formulas closed-form: pdf, cdf, sf, ppf via simple sign-flip transformation. Mean = -gamma(1+1/c). Var = gamma(1+2/c) - gamma(1+1/c)^2 (sign flip preserves variance). 3 tests: 5 (c, x) anchors at scipy 1.17.1 tol 1e-12; 4 ppf anchor points; metamorphic identity weibull_max.pdf(x)=weibull_min.pdf(-x) and weibull_max.cdf(x)=weibull_min.sf(-x) across 4x4=16 combinations. fsci-stats --lib: 1108 -> 1111.

title: [perf][sparse] supernodal dense blocking for splu — the dense scatter is a prerequisite, not the fix (bounded at ~1.8x max)
description:
Filed 2026-08-16 (PeachSummit) from a COUNTED bound, banked in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md as 'COUNTED BOUND: the dense-scatter lever is worth ~1.4-1.5x, NOT the 10.8x llywn needs'.

WHY THIS BEAD EXISTS. frankenscipy-llywn names a dense scatter workspace + flat CSC as the fix for the cubic 0.0929x (10.8x) loss. Instruction counting says that lever cannot get there:

  hashbrown probe block            3,924,650,976 Ir = 48.2% of factorize_csr, 44.9% of program
  replace with load-add-store      instruction-count speedup 1.41x - 1.51x
  applied to measured 0.0929x      -> 0.1254x - 0.1440x, i.e. STILL 6.9x - 8.0x slower
  perfect rewrite, zero probe cost -> ~1.8x ceiling, because 55% of instructions are elsewhere

HARNESS: valgrind --tool=callgrind --dump-instr=yes ./target/release/perf_splu 10 9 0 off cubic, frankenscipy_engine_sha256=8138063c..., same_host=thinkstation1, no rch worker, no rebuild.

THE HYPOTHESIS THIS BEAD TESTS. SuperLU spends its time in dense supernodal panels running BLAS-3 kernels, where one SIMD instruction retires 4-8 flops. Our elimination is scalar per entry no matter how the entry is ADDRESSED, so replacing a hash probe with an array index still concedes the vector width. Closing 10.8x needs the factor blocked into dense supernodes so the inner loop becomes a small dense GEMM/TRSM.

ORDER OF WORK, and it matters: the dense scatter (llywn) comes FIRST, because supernodal blocking needs a column-oriented factor with a known pattern. This bead is the step after it, and it should not be started before llywn lands.

WHAT WOULD FALSIFY THE PREMISE: if the dense-scatter rewrite alone measures better than ~1.8x on the cubic cell, this bound is wrong and the surplus needs explaining before supernodes are attempted -- most likely it also removed allocation or improved locality, which is worth knowing separately.

MEASUREMENT CONTRACT: harness crates/fsci-sparse/src/bin/perf_splu_balanced_square.rs on both cells. The lever is fill-proportional so the cubic cell must move and the scattered cell (scipy_lu_nnz 5,998) should be roughly unchanged. Every row names its rch WORKER and its frankenscipy_engine_sha256 -- two sanctioned ELFs of this harness have been measured 15% apart on the same cell (frankenscipy-kapqa), so a row that cannot name its binary is not comparable.

NEGATIVE CASES: byte-identical L and U against the current factorization on a well-scaled matrix (blocking is a data-layout change, not a numeric one); pivoting must remain partial-pivoting-correct across supernode boundaries; and a matrix with NO exploitable supernodes must fall back without a slowdown.
notes:
PROMOTED 2026-08-16 (PeachSummit) on measured evidence, 3596e1f78. This bead now OUTRANKS u7biq at
the cell every timed row uses, which inverts the order the two carried. Build-free measurement,
ELF 9b2bc0fb, callgrind --dump-instr=yes --cache-sim=yes, per-instruction D1 read misses in
factorize_csr self, hot addresses identified by objdump.

THE MERGE STREAMING IS THE WALL, AND ITS SHARE GROWS:

  region                                        side=10   side=12   side=16
  merge run kernel loading target values         33.23%    38.06%    45.31%
  matched_run_length block compare (inlined)     14.08%    17.10%    21.23%
  MERGE STREAMING TOTAL                          47.31%    55.17%    66.55%
  header story (u7biq's target)                  32.07%    29.08%    22.99%
  factorize_csr D1 read-miss rate                 6.85%     9.53%    12.90%

Two thirds of read misses at side=16 are streaming the target row's values (0x5e4be/c5/cc/fb,
vmovupd scale-8, 400,967,121 misses at a 25.1% rate) and comparing its columns (0x5e125,
vmovdqu/vpxor scale-4, 187,893,010 at 22.9%). THIS IS THE ONLY ITEM WHOSE SHARE IMPROVES AS THE
PROBLEM GROWS -- everything else here shrinks with the cell.

WHY THAT MATTERS FOR THIS BEAD SPECIFICALLY. The prize was previously sized from an
INSTRUCTION-COUNT bound (~1.8x ceiling, 55% of instructions elsewhere). That bound is about
instructions retired; it says nothing about where the misses are. The 66.55% figure is a
CACHE argument for the same design, it is independent of the instruction bound, and it points the
same way. Size the prize from BOTH, and state which one any future row is claiming.

The tail values (%r10 operands of the vmulpd) do NOT appear in the hot list: the pivot tail is
reused across every candidate row at that pivot and stays hot. It is the TARGET row that is cold,
touched once per pivot. That is exactly the reuse pattern blocking exists to create, and it is
direct evidence the design attacks the right traffic.

STILL TRUE AND UNCHANGED: the incumbent read (evidence f353b1672) showing SuperLU's own kernels
contain zero packed instructions and hand dense blocks to BLAS; our run kernel is already packed
AVX2. We are not behind on arithmetic width, we are behind on having structure worth blocking over.

DO NOT start this before the cheap already-written lever is measured -- see the ordering note on
u7biq. One build settles that; this bead is a larger commitment and deserves to start after it.
close_reason: CLOSED WITH A MECHANISM, NOT ABANDONED -- there is NO CROSSOVER WIDTH. This bead predicted a ~1.8x ceiling from instruction counting and asked whether dense blocking could reach it. Built and measured: the structure IS present (mean supernode width 5.24, blocks 97.2% dense, 5.08x fewer target-row touches, padding tax only 1.01x -- so the two mechanisms I initially blamed, unbounded padding and absent structure, were BOTH refuted by measurement). It still does not pay, because the dense scatter has IDENTICAL marginal cost to the merge it replaces: 15.06 vs 15.00 Ir per element-update, plus ~18M constant overhead. Identical slope plus positive intercept means no width at which blocking wins -- not a tuning failure, an ordering of the two costs. The reason is that the merge kernel is ALREADY dense inside its runs (96.8% of elements), so blocking was re-densifying something that was not sparse. BAR FOR ANY SUCCESSOR: must beat 15.00 Ir per element-update, checkable with SUPERNODE_AB_WIDTH plus the committed workload harness. Code kept in-tree behind default-off toggles (SPLU_SUPERNODAL_ENABLE), deliberately not deleted, and symbolic_fill_pattern from this line is now the required INPUT to the arena lever (frankenscipy-u7biq) -- the phase outlives the bead. Full evidence in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md, row 'THERE IS NO CROSSOVER WIDTH' 2026-08-16.

title: [sparse] qmr breakdown tolerance is 1e6x too loose; aborts healthy solves at n>=4096
description:
FOUND BY MEASUREMENT, then diagnosed to the exact trip iteration. Discovered
while running the pre-registered qmr-vs-SciPy per-iteration-tax campaign
(tests/artifacts/perf/2026-07-30-qmr-vs-scipy-live-arm), cc pane 2026-07-30.

SYMPTOM
crates/fsci-sparse/src/linalg.rs qmr() returns converged=false with a large
residual on well-conditioned, strictly diagonally dominant systems that
scipy.sparse.linalg.qmr solves without trouble. On the 2-D convection-diffusion
fixture (diag 4.001, west -1.2, east -0.8, vertical -1, rtol 1e-5):

  side   n       ours                        scipy
  48     2304    converged, 108 it           converged, 108 it
  64     4096    NOT converged, bailed 121   converged, 136 it   resid 4.413e-4
  96     9216    NOT converged, bailed 152   converged, 198 it   resid 1.804e-3
  128    16384   NOT converged, bailed 192   converged, 269 it   resid 5.040e-3
  160    25600   NOT converged, bailed  69   converged, 397 it   resid 9.066e-1

ROOT CAUSE
All three breakdown gates in qmr() used f64::EPSILON * 1e6 = 2.220e-10.
SciPy's qmr uses np.finfo(dtype).eps = 2.220e-16 for all six of its gates
(rhotol, xitol, deltatol, epsilontol, betatol, gammatol). Ours is a MILLION
times looser.

delta = w^T v and epsilon = q^T A p are near-orthogonality bilinear forms.
They legitimately shrink as the two-sided Lanczos vectors approach
orthogonality; that is normal QMR behaviour, not breakdown. Replaying SciPy's
own recurrences and logging the four gated quantities (replay script in the
artifact dir) confirms it exactly:

  side 48: min|delta|=4.41e-8  min|epsilon|=3.98e-9  -> never trips, converges
  side 64: min|epsilon|=1.52e-10 -> trips at iteration 121  (ours bailed at 121)
  side 96: min|delta|=1.27e-10   -> trips at iteration 151  (ours bailed at 152)

min|rho| and min|xi| stay near 1e-2 at every size, so the rho/xi gate is not
implicated -- only delta and epsilon.

SEVERITY
converged=false IS returned, so a caller checking the flag is not silently
lied to. But the flag is easy to ignore, the returned vector is wrong by up to
9e-1 relative, and the failure begins at a very ordinary problem size (n=4096)
on a matrix with no numerical difficulty at all. The public docstring says
"Matches scipy.sparse.linalg.qmr(A, b)" and this is exactly where it stops
matching.

FIX APPLIED
Single named constant BREAKDOWN_TOL = f64::EPSILON, used by all three gates,
matching the incumbent's criterion. Verified at side 64: now converges at
136 iterations, EXACTLY SciPy's count, agreement relative_l2_diff 6.109e-13
(was 3.342e-5 with 163 tolerance mismatches). Full sweep in the artifact dir.

FOLLOW-UP WORTH DOING
grep for other f64::EPSILON * 1e6 gates in fsci-sparse and fsci-linalg
iterative solvers. lsqr has one on rho, deliberately left alone here because
lsqr currently matches SciPy at every measured size; it should still be
audited rather than assumed correct.

Related: frankenscipy-6pdfn (minres/lsmr delegating stubs found in the same
survey).

title: [MEDIUM] fsci-fft: plan cache is Potemkin — PlanCacheBackend trait has zero impls, PlanCacheConfig.capacity/max_working_set_bytes/admission_policy are unread, PlanFingerprint.estimated_flops/scratch_bytes/radix_path are set-but-never-read, and the actual SHARED_PLAN_CACHE is an unbounded global HashMap
description:
Review of crates/fsci-fft/src/plan.rs + transforms.rs on 2026-04-22.

The plan.rs module declares a sophisticated-looking FFT plan cache with admission policies, capacity limits, working-set tracking, and a swappable backend trait. NONE of it is wired into production code. The actual cache is a global HashMap that grows without bound.

Inventory of declared-but-never-consumed surface:

1. PlanCacheBackend trait (line 91-95)
      pub trait PlanCacheBackend {
          fn lookup(&self, key: &PlanKey) -> Option<PlanMetadata>;
          fn store(&mut self, metadata: PlanMetadata) -> bool;
          fn config(&self) -> &PlanCacheConfig;
      }
   Declared, re-exported (lib.rs:20), ZERO impls in the entire workspace.
   Grep: 'impl.*PlanCacheBackend' -> 0 hits.

2. PlanCacheConfig struct (line 71-77)
      pub struct PlanCacheConfig {
          pub capacity: usize,              // default 128     -- UNUSED
          pub max_working_set_bytes: usize, // default 64 MiB  -- UNUSED
          pub planning_strategy: PlanningStrategy,
          pub admission_policy: CacheAdmissionPolicy,          // UNUSED
      }
   Declared, re-exported (lib.rs:20), only read inside plan.rs tests (line 137-141)
   that check the default values. No production code constructs a PlanCacheConfig
   and passes it to anything.

3. CacheAdmissionPolicy enum (line 17-23)
      pub enum CacheAdmissionPolicy {
          Disabled, CostWeightedLru, AlwaysInsert,
      }
   Declared, re-exported, never matched against anywhere. store_shared_plan
   (line 111-115) unconditionally inserts regardless of policy.

4. PlanFingerprint's stored fields:
      pub radix_path: Vec<usize>,         -- set but never read
      pub estimated_flops: u64,           -- set, never read, AND mathematically wrong:
                                             line 2065 uses n*n for FFT that runs in n*log(n),
                                             overstates flop count by 20x for n=1024, 100x for n=1M
      pub scratch_bytes: usize,           -- set but never read

The actual plan cache (SHARED_PLAN_CACHE, plan.rs:97):

    static SHARED_PLAN_CACHE: OnceLock<Mutex<HashMap<PlanKey, PlanMetadata>>> = OnceLock::new();

is a plain HashMap that:
  - has no capacity limit (PlanCacheConfig.capacity is dead)
  - has no admission policy (admission_policy is dead)
  - has no LRU eviction
  - never clears itself automatically (only via the public clear_shared_plan_cache)
  - grows monotonically with every unique (kind, shape, axes, normalization, real_input) key

Impact:

1. Memory leak hazard: a user calling fft() on many distinct shapes (e.g., each
   solve_ivp step produces a slightly different dimensionality, or a batch that
   varies per sample) accumulates cache entries indefinitely. 64 MiB of working
   set from PlanCacheConfig.max_working_set_bytes is the DEFAULT the user sees
   in the type, but the actual limit is 'until OOM.' This is the opposite of
   what PlanCacheConfig advertises.

2. Naming dishonesty: a reviewer reading plan.rs sees a PlanCacheBackend trait,
   capacity/LRU/admission fields, and a PlanFingerprint with flop/scratch
   estimates. Reasonable inference: 'fsci-fft has a proper bounded plan cache
   with observability.' Reality: global HashMap with dead metadata.

3. Wrong metadata: estimated_flops = n*n is the naive DFT cost, but FftOptions
   default to CooleyTukeyBackend (line 293, BackendKind::default() is CT).
   Any downstream code that ever does wire up estimated_flops will be wrong by
   ~log(n) factor, i.e., hugely over-estimating small-to-medium FFT cost.

4. Test at plan.rs:137-141 pins the default values as 128/64MiB, giving a
   visible 'these defaults matter' signal to a reviewer -- but the defaults
   don't actually bound anything.

5. Interacts with xjav / r575 (contract tables 5/7 dead), 95ld (mode: String
   dead field), ovxs (audit type fragmentation). Another instance of public
   types that describe work that was never completed.

Ask:

1. Either complete the plan cache (implement capacity, admission policy,
   byte-based working-set LRU) or delete the unused surface:
   - Remove PlanCacheBackend trait OR implement it for a real backend.
   - Remove PlanCacheConfig capacity/max_working_set_bytes/admission_policy
     fields OR wire them through store_shared_plan.
   - Remove radix_path / estimated_flops / scratch_bytes OR consume them
     (e.g., expose via a plan_stats() API or include in audit-ledger records).

2. If keeping estimated_flops, fix the formula: use n * log2(n) * 5 (or similar
   Cooley-Tukey coefficient) for non-naive backends, n*n only when backend ==
   NaiveDftBackend.

3. Add a simple capacity bound on SHARED_PLAN_CACHE (e.g., .len() > 1024 ->
   clear oldest via BTreeMap keyed by insertion counter) to prevent the
   monotonic-growth hazard.

4. Rename or repurpose 'PlanFingerprint' -- currently the 'fingerprint' (per
   docstring on line 54-55: 'proving how a concrete FFT plan was selected')
   doesn't actually prove anything because it's never validated against
   observed execution.

Related: 95ld (mode: String dead-field for cluster/spatial/signal/stats/
integrate), ovxs (audit type fragmentation), xjav (contract tables 5/7 dead),
r575 (P2C-006 contract missing), yxml (Debug-format string match). The common
theme: built-but-not-wired observability surfaces.
close_reason: Implemented bounded FFT plan cache with capacity, working-set admission, and non-quadratic FFT cost estimates

title: EPIC: Strict/Hardened Mode Audit Ledger
description:
## Background

SPEC §4-5 define strict vs hardened operating modes. SPEC §16 Security Threat Matrix mandates: metadata incident ledger, stability decision ledger, backend policy ledger, tolerance audit report, compatibility drift report, override audit record. Currently RuntimeMode enum is threaded through SOME validation paths but no centralized audit-ledger emission exists.

## Goal

Implement a structured audit ledger that records: (1) every strict/hardened mode decision, (2) every bounded recovery/repair in hardened mode, (3) every fail-closed rejection, (4) every policy override. Emit as JSON-lines file alongside other conformance artifacts.

## Success Criteria

1. AuditLedger type with append-only recording
2. Every hardened-mode recovery logged with input fingerprint, recovery action, and outcome
3. Every fail-closed rejection logged with rejection reason
4. Ledger emitted as .jsonl artifact in conformance workflow
5. Tests proving ledger captures expected events for known inputs

## Serves Project Goal

SPEC §16 requires "deterministic audit logs for recoveries and policy overrides." Without this, the security model is aspirational.
close_reason: Completed: AuditLedger exists in fsci-runtime, linalg/integrate audit-aware paths record fail_closed and bounded_recovery events, and conformance differential runs emit audit_ledger.jsonl artifacts with tests covering expected events

title: [linalg][robustness] full eigh/svd stall on rank-deficient/clustered spectra (rank-30 n=2000 eigh=8555ms vs 6.4ms; 800x600 svd ~25s)
description: fsci_linalg::eigh and svd run near-quadratic-in-iterations on matrices with clustered/zero eigenvalues because the bidiagonal/tridiagonal QR sweep doesn't deflate degenerate eigenvalues. EVIDENCE (this session): full eigh of a rank-30 PSD kernel at n=2000 took 8555ms (cf. 6.4ms Nystrom on the same matrix); older note: nalgebra full svd ~25s on an exactly-rank-deficient 800x600. IMPACT: any code that full-eig/svd-decomposes a low-rank matrix (the A/B baselines for nystroem/classical_mds/kernel_pca/factor_analysis all hit it; real callers of eigh/svd on near-singular Gram/kernel/covariance matrices). FIX (linalg): zero/cluster deflation or tolerance-based early termination in the QR iteration; consider falling back to a Jacobi or divide-and-conquer path for clustered spectra. Repro: build K=B*B^T with B (2000x30) random, time eigh(K). DO NOT mask by routing callers to randomized methods.
close_reason: FIXED (commit a7ed6c7b): svd() now does the fast Golub-Kahan reduction first, detects rank deficiency from the bidiagonal (|d[i]|<=1e-11*scale; an upper bidiagonal is singular iff a diagonal collapses to ~0), and reroutes to the robust jacobi_svd (shipped 90636cc3). 800x600 rank-30: 33.2s->8.8s (3.76x) AND correct (machine-precision, 30 nonzero sigma); full-rank byte-identical (same reduction feeds the deterministic path, no second reduction). Threshold cleanly separates exact-zeros (min|d|/scale~3e-17) from small-but-nonzero (~6e-8). 408 linalg + 117 cluster tests pass. NOTE: wide (rows<cols) rank-deficient via public_wide_svd_via_transpose not yet rerouted — separate follow-up if it bites.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: CONFIRMED+characterized (commit 6a596e81; repro: cargo run -p fsci-cluster --bin probe_svd_stall). Stall SPECIFIC to EXACTLY rank-deficient (zero singular values): svd 800x600 rank-30 exact=35314ms vs 447ms full-rank (79x); 600x600 rank-30 exact=24191ms vs 239ms (101x); SAME matrix +1e-6 noise=433ms FAST. Exact-zero singular values stall bidiagonal-QR (deflation fail) via safe_svd fallback after deterministic_bidiagonal rejects. eigh NOT affected (rank-30 n=800=319ms). FIX (linalg core): deflate negligible super-diagonals before QR / handle zero singular values in deterministic_bidiagonal_svd / route rank-deficient via AtA eigh (gate, golden-parity risk). Deep core change.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: ROOT CAUSE confirmed: public_bidiag_svd_accepts() DELIBERATELY rejects rank-deficient (min_s<=rank_gap_floor) AND clustered/tied (pair[0]-pair[1]<=tie_gap_floor) spectra — fsci's deterministic bidiagonal path can't resolve them accurately, so they fall to safe_svd=nalgebra::SVD::new (unbounded iters) which STALLS on exact-zero singular values. NOT fixable by tweaking acceptance (it correctly identifies its limits) nor by capping nalgebra iters (stall cases converge slowly ~35s, not non-convergent; a cap cuts off legit slow cases too -> parity break). PROPER FIX = a real bidiagonal-SVD-with-deflation kernel (LAPACK dbdsqr-style: deflate negligible super-diagonals + handle zero singular values via Givens) to REPLACE the nalgebra fallback. Substantial parity-critical core build (NO-GAPS), needs full linalg golden suite. Target 79-101x on rank-deficient SVD.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: DEEPER FINDING (attempted fix, reverted to git-stash 'cc-svd-deflation-WIP-9xrce-unverified'): tried (a) bounded nalgebra try_new + Jacobi normal-equations fallback in safe_svd, (b) per-eigenvalue stagnation valve in symmetric_tridiagonal_qr_eigen, (c) absolute deflation floor .max(1.0) in delimit + main-loop deflation tests. NONE moved the probe (still 32-34s). ROOT CAUSE is deeper: the deterministic path eigendecomposes the GRAM tridiagonal BᵀB (deterministic_bidiagonal_svd_symmetric_eigen), so the rank-deficient zero-singular cluster becomes a zero-EIGENVALUE cluster of BᵀB whose residual off-diagonals plateau at accumulated-rounding level (~few·eps·‖B‖²), NOT below the eps deflation threshold — and a looser flat floor (sqrt(eps)) would destroy precision on genuinely-small healthy eigenvalues. The Gram-squaring fundamentally caps small-singular-value accuracy. PROPER FIX = implement dbdsqr-style implicit-ZERO-shift QR directly on the BIDIAGONAL (not BᵀB) — high relative accuracy, deflates zeros cleanly. Substantial LAPACK-class kernel, multi-session. Recover WIP: git stash list | grep cc-svd-deflation.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: WORKAROUND SHIPPED (90636cc3): new pub jacobi_svd() — robust one-sided Jacobi SVD that handles exact-rank-deficient inputs in ~10s (machine-precision, correct rank) where svd() stalls ~35s. Callers hitting the stall can use jacobi_svd. FULL FIX still needs either (a) cheap rank-deficiency detection in svd() after golub_kahan_bidiagonal_reduction (trailing bidiagonal entries ~0 for rank-r input) to route rank-deficient to jacobi_svd, or (b) the dbdsqr direct-bidiagonal kernel. jacobi_svd is the robust building block for (a).

title: [sparse] bicg/cgs/bicgstab breakdown gates are 1e6x too loose (same defect 9pfja proved in qmr)
description:
Found by the frankenscipy-6pdfn delegating-stub compliance sweep (ChartreuseChapel, 2026-08-04).

frankenscipy-9pfja PROVED, with a replay of SciPy's own recurrences, that a
breakdown gate of `f64::EPSILON * 1e6` = 2.220e-10 is a MILLION times looser
than SciPy's `np.finfo(dtype).eps` = 2.220e-16, and that this aborts healthy,
strictly-diagonally-dominant solves starting at n=4096. That bead fixed qmr
ONLY. The identical constant is still live in three other public solvers:

  crates/fsci-sparse/src/linalg.rs:2020  bicg      rho
  crates/fsci-sparse/src/linalg.rs:2036  bicg      alpha_denom
  crates/fsci-sparse/src/linalg.rs:2168  cgs       rho
  crates/fsci-sparse/src/linalg.rs:2181  cgs       sigma
  crates/fsci-sparse/src/linalg.rs:2319  bicgstab  rho_new
  crates/fsci-sparse/src/linalg.rs:2341  bicgstab  r_hat_v
  crates/fsci-sparse/src/linalg.rs:2377  bicgstab  omega/t_dot_t

These are the same class of near-orthogonality bilinear forms (rho = r_tilde^T r,
sigma = r_tilde^T A p) that 9pfja showed legitimately shrink as the two-sided
Lanczos/BiCG vectors approach orthogonality. Shrinking is normal behaviour, not
breakdown. SciPy's bicg/cgs/bicgstab gate on eps, not 1e6*eps.

PREDICTION TO FALSIFY FIRST (do not fix blind): 9pfja's trip sizes were derived
by replaying the recurrences and logging min|rho|, min|sigma|. Do the same for
bicg/cgs/bicgstab on the 2-D convection-diffusion family (diag 4.001, west -1.2,
east -0.8, vertical -1, rtol 1e-5) at side 48/64/96/128/160 BEFORE changing the
constant. If the gated quantities never approach 2.220e-10 at those sizes, this
is a latent defect, not an active one, and it drops to P3.

Note bicgstab:2377 is an inverted comparison (`> EPSILON*1e6` guarding a
divide), so tightening it CHANGES which branch is taken, not just when the
solver bails. Treat that one separately.

EVIDENCE REQUIRED TO CLOSE: a differential test against
scipy.sparse.linalg.bicg/cgs/bicgstab at a size where the current gate trips and
scipy converges, red before the fix and green after. A gate change with no such
probe is not admissible.
close_reason:
Fixed and verified with a red-before/green-after pair on the same test. Landed in e8cd0af89.

RED BEFORE (RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 env -u CARGO_TARGET_DIR rch exec -- cargo test
-p fsci-sparse --lib -- linalg::tests::bicg_cgs_bicgstab_converge):
  panicked at crates/fsci-sparse/src/linalg.rs:7347
  'bicg bailed on a strictly diagonally dominant nonsymmetric system that SciPy
   solves: residual_norm=0.00002902185099200906 after 19 iterations.
   A breakdown gate is rejecting healthy iterates.'
  test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed
Iteration 19 is exactly what the recurrence replay predicted in the earlier
comment, so the shipped code and the replay agree on the failure point.

GREEN AFTER (same command, full suite):
  test linalg::tests::bicg_cgs_bicgstab_converge_on_a_nonsymmetric_operator_like_scipy ... ok
  test result: 396 passed; 1 failed
The single remaining failure is frankenscipy-cvaup (sparse_row_min), which was
red on main BEFORE this change and is untouched by it -- 395 passed / 1 failed
before, 396 passed / 1 failed after, the delta being exactly this new test.

FIX, matching SciPy 1.17.1 rather than the constant this bead originally
assumed (the bead said 'eps'; that is qmr's, and it was wrong for these three):
  new KRYLOV_BREAKDOWN_TOL = f64::EPSILON * f64::EPSILON  (SciPy's rhotol)
  bicg      rho at eps**2; alpha_denom reduced to an exact-zero divide guard,
            because SciPy's bicg has NO threshold gate there at all
  cgs       rho at eps**2; sigma exact-zero ('if rv == 0')
  bicgstab  rho at eps**2; r_hat_v exact-zero; and the structural change the
            earlier comment predicted -- the t.t DENOMINATOR gate is gone
            (SciPy has no counterpart) and is replaced by SciPy's |omega| <
            omegatol test at the top of the next sweep, guarded by
            iteration > 0 since omega starts at 1.0. Gating t.t was wrong
            twice: it is a SQUARED norm, so 2.220e-10 rejected ||t|| ~ 7e-6,
            and the quantity that must be non-degenerate is the quotient.
  omega annotated f64 so the new .abs() resolves (E0689 on first build).

NOT A CHANGE OF ITERATES, only of what gets discarded. Shipped code agrees with
live SciPy on the identical system to the residual floor:
  ours 3.566e-11 / 7.210e-11 / 8.862e-11  (bicg / cgs / bicgstab)
  scipy 3.566e-11 / 7.059e-11 / 8.863e-11
two of the three matching to every printed digit, all three ~3 orders inside
the 1e-8 test tolerance.

The probe pins the full 64-element SciPy solution at rtol=1e-12. SciPy's own
bicg, cgs and bicgstab agree with each other to 2.66e-12 on it, so the pin is
the shared SciPy answer, not one solver's quirk. Pinned rather than live-oracle
because the rch fleet has no scipy (ModuleNotFoundError) and rch refuses
non-compilation commands, so a python3-shelling harness cannot execute on a
worker at all.

Also verified: clippy -p fsci-sparse --lib --all-features -D warnings exit 0;
cargo check -p fsci-sparse --bins exit 0; rustfmt --check exit 0; ubs exit 0
with 0 critical.

SCOPE LEFT OPEN ON PURPOSE: f64::EPSILON * 1e6 still appears in lsqr:3001,
krylov_arnoldi_eigs:9993 and svds:10613. Same constant, different functions,
and the loose-gate defect class is now observed four times (qmr, bicg, cgs,
bicgstab) -- but I have no measured evidence those three are wrong, and
changing them blind is exactly the mistake this bead corrected in reverse. They
want their own replay first.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
MEASURED, ACTIVE AT n=64 — not latent. ChartreuseChapel 2026-08-04.

The bead body asked for a recurrence replay before touching the constant, on the
grounds that this might be latent. It is not. Replaying fsci's own loops in
float64 on the 8x8 (n=64) convection-diffusion operator (diag 4.001, west -1.2,
east -0.8, vertical -1, b_i = 1 + 0.1*(i mod 7), rtol 1e-10, maxiter 500), the
SAME fixture family 9pfja used:

  solver     outcome                    gated quantity at trip
  bicg       TRIPS at iteration 19      min|rho| = 2.1626e-10
  cgs        TRIPS at iteration 19      min|rho| = 2.1628e-10
  bicgstab   TRIPS at iteration 13      min|t.t| = 4.9326e-11
  gate                                  EPSILON*1e6 = 2.2204e-10

Live SciPy 1.17.1 on the identical system converges ALL THREE (info=0), max
elementwise deviation from a direct spsolve: bicg 3.566e-11, cgs 7.059e-11,
bicgstab 8.863e-11. A real divergence from the advertised peer at n=64 — 64x
smaller than the n=4096 where 9pfja first saw it in qmr.

CORRECTED FIX TARGET — the bead body says 'SciPy gates on eps'. That is qmr's
constant and it is WRONG for these three. Read from scipy/sparse/linalg/_isolve/
iterative.py (installed 1.17.1):

  bicg:      rhotol = np.finfo(x.dtype.char).eps**2  -> 4.930e-32
             ONE gate only, on |rho_cur|. SciPy has NO alpha_denom gate.
  cgs:       rhotol = eps**2 on |rho_cur|; the dot-product breakdown is the
             EXACT test 'if rv == 0', not a threshold.
  bicgstab:  rhotol = eps**2 on |rho|; omegatol = rhotol; 'if rv == 0' exact.

STRUCTURAL FINDING on bicgstab that changes the fix: fsci gates the DENOMINATOR
t.t at linalg.rs:2377. SciPy has no such gate at all — it computes
omega = (t.s)/(t.t) unguarded and instead checks |omega| < omegatol at the TOP
of the next iteration, before beta. So bicgstab is not a constant swap; the
check must move to scipy's position and change subject from t.t to omega. Note
t.t is a SQUARED norm, so gating it at eps*1e6 rejects ||t|| around 7e-6.

SciPy's own comment on the constant: '# These values make no sense but coming
from original Fortran code / sqrt might have been meant instead.' Match the
peer, do not improve on it.

RED PROBE READY. The nonsymmetric column for this fixture is staged to land with
the fix in diff_sparse_iterative_solvers.rs. frankenscipy-6pdfn ships the
symmetric coverage now and documents in-file why this column is deferred here.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
FIX PRE-VERIFIED IN REPLAY — ChartreuseChapel 2026-08-04.

Re-ran the same float64 replay of fsci's loops on the same n=64 nonsymmetric
operator, changing ONLY the gates to SciPy's semantics:
  rhotol = eps**2 (4.930e-32) on |rho|
  exact 'if denom == 0.0' for bicg alpha_denom, cgs sigma, bicgstab rv
  bicgstab: DROP the t.t denominator gate; check |omega| < rhotol at the top of
            the next iteration (scipy's position), before beta

Result — all three now converge instead of aborting:

  solver     before          after      max|x - x_direct|
  bicg       TRIP it=19      35 iters   3.566213990779943e-11
  cgs        TRIP it=19      24 iters   7.209610686231827e-11
  bicgstab   TRIP it=13      23 iters   8.862244271767850e-11

Cross-check against live SciPy 1.17.1 on the identical system:
  bicg     scipy 3.566e-11   <- matches to every printed digit
  cgs      scipy 7.059e-11   <- agrees to 2.1e-12, far inside ABS_TOL 1e-6
  bicgstab scipy 8.863e-11   <- matches to every printed digit

So the fix is a gate correction only; it does not perturb the iterates that were
already being produced, it stops the solver discarding them. The agreement with
SciPy is at the 1e-11 residual floor, three orders inside the harness tolerance.

This is replay evidence, NOT a passing test. It predicts the outcome; it does
not substitute for it. Closing this bead still requires the real probe: the
nonsymmetric column in diff_sparse_iterative_solvers.rs, demonstrated RED on
current main and GREEN after the gate change, run with FSCI_REQUIRE_SCIPY_ORACLE=1
so the oracle arm cannot silently skip, verified via
RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 env -u CARGO_TARGET_DIR rch exec.

description:
Measured 2026-08-16 (RainyPrairie) while clearing the fsci-spatial link of frankenscipy-iit9c. Harness 'rch exec -- cargo clippy -j 1 -p <crate> --lib -- -D warnings', RCH_WORKER=vmi1149989.

METHOD THAT WORKED ON THE SIBLING BEADS, and the reason a raw error count misleads here: fsci-special (frankenscipy-e2ve2) reported 279 errors and 240 of them were ONE class -- excessive_precision on transcribed Cephes/DLMF constants -- which collapsed to a single justified crate-root allow, leaving 39 real fixes. title: fsci-stats: theilslopes does 2x the inner-loop work
description: Skill: /profiling-software-performance. theilslopes (lib.rs:20549) iterates all N×N pairs (i,j) ∈ [0,n)² and filters via 'dx > 1e-15', so each unordered pair {a,b} is checked twice but only the direction with positive dx survives the filter. By symmetry the slope (y_i-y_j)/(x_i-x_j) equals (y_j-y_i)/(x_j-x_i), so we can iterate j > i with |dx| > tol and halve the inner-loop cost. Will ship optimized inner loop with reference-equivalence test (compare medslope on a fixed dataset against the old algorithm's expected value).

title: [parity-gap] complex Airy Ai/Aip catastrophically wrong at large |z| (Taylor series cancels)
description: airy_complex_scalar used the Taylor series around 0 for all complex z. In the central sector |arg z|<pi/3, Ai decays like e^{-(2/3)z^{3/2}} and the series cancels catastrophically: Ai(12+0.5i) was ~1e8 off vs scipy. Fix: in the central sector at large |z| use the modified-Bessel forms (DLMF 9.6.1/9.6.4) Ai=(1/pi)sqrt(z/3)K_{1/3}(zeta), Ai'=-(z/(pi sqrt3))K_{2/3}(zeta), Bi=sqrt(z/3)(I_{-1/3}+I_{1/3}), Bi'=(z/sqrt3)(I_{-2/3}+I_{2/3}), zeta=(2/3)z^{3/2}, using the now-exact complex K/I Bessel functions (no cancellation). Verified 0 bad over the whole central sector (|z| 6-100). scipy.special.airy accepts complex, so this is scipy-parity.
close_reason: Fixed central sector |arg z|<pi/3 in b5f6c460 via modified-Bessel forms (Ai=(1/pi)sqrt(z/3)K_{1/3}(zeta) etc), 0 bad over |z| 6-100. Non-central sectors (pi/3<|arg z|<=pi) at large |z| remain -> new bead.

title: [infra] cargo-clippy is MISSING on at least 3 rch workers despite rust-toolchain.toml requesting it — the lint gate is a lottery
description:
Measured 2026-08-16 (RainyPrairie) across this session. rust-toolchain.toml pins channel nightly-2026-07-20 and declares components = ['rustfmt', 'clippy'], so every worker running this repo's toolchain should have cargo-clippy. Three do not.

WITHOUT cargo-clippy (each observed failing with "error: 'cargo-clippy' is not installed for the toolchain 'nightly-2026-07-20-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu'", exit 1):
  vmi1153651  (5 consecutive schedules earlier in the session)
  vmi1264463  (2 consecutive)
  vmi1152480

WITH cargo-clippy, same command, same session, gates passing normally:
  hz1, hz2, vmi1149989, vmi1227854, vmi1293453

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND ANNOYANCE. rch does not consider toolchain components in admission (see frankenscipy-a6916), so which worker you land on decides whether 'cargo clippy ... -- -D warnings' RUNS or ERRORS. Two consequences, both bad and both observed: an agent can believe a crate is gate-clean because their run landed on a capable worker, and an agent can be blocked from closing a bead whose closure condition IS a clippy invocation. The latter happened here -- frankenscipy-gkzq8's stated gate ('cargo clippy -p fsci-sparse --features sparse-incumbent-bench --all-targets -- -D warnings' exit 0) could not be run in three consecutive attempts because all three landed on clippy-less workers, and per standing orders I recorded the refusal rather than retrying in place.

It also makes 'clippy is clean' UNFALSIFIABLE from a single run: a failure might mean lints, or might mean the worker. Every clippy row in this campaign should therefore name its worker, which is already the rule for timed rows and should be extended.

FIX (ops, outside this repo): 'rustup component add clippy --toolchain nightly-2026-07-20' on the affected workers, then confirm with 'rch workers capabilities --refresh'. Better: have worker provisioning honour rust-toolchain.toml's components list so this cannot drift again, and have rch treat a missing component as an admission failure rather than scheduling a job that must error.

NEGATIVE CASE for any fix: after the fix, a clippy job must be REFUSED (not scheduled and failed) on a worker that genuinely lacks the component, so the failure mode is distinguishable from real lints.
notes:
2026-08-16 RainyPrairie: REPO-SIDE MITIGATION LANDED, bead stays OPEN because the actual fix is ops and outside this repo.

AGENTS.md now carries a section (before the eibro stale-binary section) with: the measured capable/incapable worker table, the RCH_WORKER pinning recipe, the rule that an unpinned clippy run is no evidence in EITHER direction, the instruction to pick another capable worker rather than dropping the pin on a refusal, and a zero-cost verification command (rch exec -- cargo clippy --version, no compile, no disk) since the table is a snapshot and worker images change.

That removes both observed harms for anyone who reads it -- the silent false-green and the blocked bead closure -- but it does NOT install the component. Closing conditions unchanged: provisioning should honour rust-toolchain.toml components, and rch should treat a missing component as an ADMISSION failure so the job is refused rather than scheduled and failed. The negative case still stands: after the fix a clippy job on a component-less worker must be refused, not failed, so the failure mode stays distinguishable from real lints.

title: [infra] rch admits 'cargo test -j 1' where the default job count is refused with insufficient_slots — document it or make the scheduler downshift
description:
Measured 2026-08-15 (RainyPrairie). This cost roughly 100 refused builds and two turns of blocked work before it was noticed, so it is worth either documenting in AGENTS.md or fixing in the scheduler.

SYMPTOM: 'RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 env -u CARGO_TARGET_DIR rch exec -- cargo test -p fsci-sparse --lib' refused repeatedly with 'no admissible workers: critical_pressure=1,insufficient_slots=5,insufficient_total_slots=4', while 'rch status' simultaneously reported 13-22 of 49 slots FREE. The aggregate free-slot count is not what admission tests: a default cargo job count asks for more slots than any SINGLE worker has free, so a fleet with plenty of total capacity admits nothing.

FIX ON THE CALLER SIDE, verified: adding '-j 1' was admitted immediately on the very next attempt and every attempt after. Same command, same fleet state, same second. Three targets that had been unrunnable for ~100 attempts all completed on RCH_WORKER=vmi1149989: fsci-sparse --lib (483 passed), --test metamorphic_tests (56 passed), fsci-conformance e2e_sparse + diff_sparse_basic_queries (24 + 1 passed). Other agents' queue entries already show '-j 1' and '-j 2', so some agents know this and it is not written down anywhere I could find.

TWO POSSIBLE RESOLUTIONS, either is fine:
1. Documentation: add to the RCH section of AGENTS.md that a refusal naming insufficient_slots is a JOB-COUNT problem and not a capacity problem, and that '-j 1' or '-j 2' is the remedy. Cheapest, and it stops the next agent losing an hour.
2. Scheduler: have rch downshift the job count automatically when the requested parallelism exceeds every worker's free slots, rather than refusing. Preferable, since the refusal message currently reads as 'the fleet is full' when it means 'your job is too wide'.

SECOND, SEPARATE OBSERVATION from the same session, related to frankenscipy-118g9: RCH_WORKER=vmi1153651 has NO cargo-clippy for toolchain nightly-2026-07-20 ('error: cargo-clippy is not installed for the toolchain'), and rch scheduled a clippy job onto it anyway. Retrying landed on vmi1149989 and succeeded. So clippy capability is not part of admission.

NEGATIVE CASE for a scheduler fix: a job that genuinely cannot fit even at -j 1 must still be refused rather than silently queued forever, and the refusal must say which of the two causes applies.
close_reason: Landed in bb3f7cc3b via resolution 1 (documentation). Cited evidence, all in-session and reproducible: 'rch exec -- cargo test -p fsci-sparse --lib' refused with 'no admissible workers: insufficient_slots=5, insufficient_total_slots=4' while 'rch status' reported 13-22 of 49 slots FREE; adding '-j 1' was admitted on the very next attempt and every attempt after, same command and same fleet state. Three targets unrunnable for ~100 attempts then completed on RCH_WORKER=vmi1149989 -- fsci-sparse --lib 483 passed, --test metamorphic_tests 56 passed, fsci-conformance e2e_sparse + diff_sparse_basic_queries 24 + 1 passed. AGENTS.md now distinguishes the two refusal causes (insufficient_slots is yours to fix by narrowing the job; active_project_exclusion is a peer's build, one per project key), corrects the false 'fails open' claim for RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1, and records that worker capability is NOT part of admission (vmi1153651 has no cargo-clippy for nightly-2026-07-20 and was scheduled a clippy job anyway; re-issuing landed on vmi1149989 and succeeded). Resolution 2, the scheduler downshift, is NOT done and belongs in the rch codebase rather than this repo -- its negative case is recorded in the bead description for whoever picks it up. title: [code-review] fsci-fft shared_cache_* tests race on static cache
description:
fsci-fft has 7 #[test]s in crates/fsci-fft/src/plan.rs that mutate a single static Mutex<BoundedPlanCache> exposed via shared_cache() (line 300). Each test calls clear_shared_plan_cache() then asserts on shared_plan_cache_len(), lookup_shared_plan(...), and shared_plan_cache_working_set_bytes(). cargo test runs them in parallel by default, so they intermittently corrupt each other's expected state. Concrete failure observed in workspace test run:

  test plan::tests::shared_cache_enforces_capacity_limit ... FAILED
  test result: FAILED. 96 passed; 1 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; finished in 0.05s

A second run had 4 of the 7 fail. Re-running -p fsci-fft alone serially passes all of them.

Affected tests (crates/fsci-fft/src/plan.rs):
  shared_cache_roundtrip_works (397)
  shared_cache_recovers_after_poisoned_lock (421)
  shared_cache_respects_disabled_admission_policy (447)
  shared_cache_enforces_capacity_limit (460)
  shared_cache_enforces_working_set_limit (488)
  cost_weighted_cache_rejects_cheap_plan_when_full (511)
  (any future shared_cache_* test)

Repro: rch exec -- cargo test -p fsci-fft --lib -- --test-threads=8
  (intermittent — sometimes 0/sometimes 1+ fail).

Fix: serialize these tests via a test-only static Mutex<()> guard at the top of each shared_cache_* test, OR add the  dev-dependency and annotate each with #[serial(shared_plan_cache)]. Either ensures only one of these tests holds the cache at a time.

Acceptance: rch exec -- cargo test -p fsci-fft --lib -- --test-threads=8 passes deterministically across 5 consecutive runs.

All four share ONE Householder reduction (symmetric_tridiagonalize_native, extracted verbatim from symmetric_eigh_native) and ONE back-transform (back_transform_selected_columns, factored out in this commit). That is deliberate: four entry points with four copies of the O(n^3) stage would drift, and the shared path makes the value form bit-identical to the index form by construction rather than by review.

Half-open vl < lambda <= vu, matching scipy, with decreasing and NaN ranges refused rather than silently swapped. An empty window is an ANSWER -- empty values with an n x 0 block -- not an error.

THE KEY TEST asserts that a value window enclosing exactly indices lo..=hi returns the SAME block as asking for those indices, BIT FOR BIT, eigenvalues and eigenvectors alike. Anything else means the two entry points have drifted. The window is chosen strictly BETWEEN eigenvalues (midpoints of adjacent pairs) so the selection cannot turn on an ulp -- the boundary sensitivity filed as j7gfa. Plus a dense residual A*v = lambda*v on the ORIGINAL matrix so this is not merely internal self-consistency, the empty-window shape, eigvals_only skipping the back-transform, and refusal of reversed/NaN ranges and non-square input.

crates/fsci-spatial/src/lib.rs and covers exactly this bead's list -- cdist
euclidean plus pdist euclidean/cityblock/chebyshev against scipy values. Not

THE GAP: that test uses 2-D points with integer coordinates ((0,0), (1,1),
(2,0), ...), so every distance is a round number and only the generic scalar
path runs. But `pdist` and `cdist` dispatch to entirely separate SIMD kernels
when dim == 4, selected by an explicit `if dim == 4` arm:
pdist_fill_euclidean4, fill_sqeuclidean4_rows, fill_cityblock4_rows,

metric_helpers and cdist_euclidean_small_d_soa_matches_scalar_bitwise -- all of
which compare the fast path against fsci's OWN scalar helpers. That is
self-consistency, not parity: if the SIMD kernel and the scalar helper share a
mistake, or the scalar reference is itself wrong, every one of those tests still
passes. It is the same shape as a self-speedup being presented as a win.

title: [stats] mode tie-breaking (smallest, scipy 1.17) + moment lack an exact scipy golden test
close_reason:
Closed 2026-08-08 (TopazOsprey). Both halves were real gaps.

DEDUP VERIFICATION -- MODE. Three mode tests exist and none pins scipy's
tie-breaking rule for the scalar `mode`:
  - mode_basic uses [1,2,2,3,3,3,4], an UNAMBIGUOUS mode (3 occurs three
    times). No tie.
  - mode_all_unique uses [3,1,2] -- every value ties at count 1, which is
    exactly the interesting case -- but asserts only that the result
    is_finite(). Its comment claims "returns smallest (first encountered)",
    which conflates two different rules and checks neither.
  - mode_full_smallest_when_tied does test tie-breaking, but only for
    `mode_full`, and with [1,1,3,3] where 1 is SIMULTANEOUSLY the smallest tied
    value and the first encountered. It therefore cannot distinguish "smallest"
    from "first encountered" either.
So no test anywhere separated the two rules, and the scalar `mode` had no tie
coverage at all.

DEDUP VERIFICATION -- MOMENT. moment is covered at k=0 (=1), k=1 (=0) and k=2
(=population variance) on [1..5]. All three are structural identities that hold
no matter how the higher orders are implemented. k>=3 -- where an n vs n-1
normalisation slip or a wrong power surfaces -- had no golden.

ADDED: mode_tie_breaking_and_higher_moments_match_exact_scipy.
  - Tie data [5,5,2,2,9]: 5 and 2 both occur twice, 5 is FIRST, and
    scipy.stats.mode returns 2.0 with count 2. A first-encountered
    implementation returns 5.0 and fails. Asserted for both `mode` and
    `mode_full`, plus the count.
  - moment at k=2,3,4,5 on [2.5,-1,3.75,0.5,-2.25,4] (mean 1.25, deliberately
    non-integer so no order collapses to a round number by accident), pinned to
    scipy.stats.moment(a, order=k) at 1e-12 RELATIVE:
        k=2   5.541666666666667
        k=3  -2.71875
        k=4  45.783854166666664
        k=5  -54.189453125
  - Plus a sign assertion on the odd orders: this sample is left-skewed, so a
    formula that took an absolute value or squared the deviations would return a
    positive third moment and pass a magnitude-only check.

RESULT: fsci PASSES all of it. No defect -- `mode` already resolves ties to the
smallest as scipy 1.17 does, and the higher central moments are correct. Both
behaviours were simply unverified.

title: [special] Spherical Bessel, spherical harmonics, associated Legendre
description:
## Goal
Implement spherical special functions used in physics (electromagnetics, quantum mechanics, acoustics, gravitational fields).

## What to implement
- `spherical_jn(n, z)`: spherical Bessel function of first kind j_n(z) = √(π/(2z)) J_{n+1/2}(z)
- `spherical_yn(n, z)`: spherical Bessel of second kind y_n(z) = √(π/(2z)) Y_{n+1/2}(z)
- `spherical_in(n, z)`: modified spherical Bessel i_n(z)
- `spherical_kn(n, z)`: modified spherical Bessel k_n(z)
- `lpmv(m, v, x)`: associated Legendre function P_v^m(x) for integer m, real v
- `sph_harm_y(l, m, theta, phi)`: real spherical harmonic Y_l^m(θ,φ)

## Why this matters
Spherical Bessel functions appear in wave scattering, antenna theory, and acoustic radiation. Spherical harmonics are fundamental to quantum mechanics, gravitational field modeling (GPS/geodesy), and climate modeling.

## Implementation approach
- spherical_jn/yn: use recurrence relation from ordinary Bessel. j_0(z) = sin(z)/z, j_1(z) = sin(z)/z² - cos(z)/z
- Forward recurrence for j_n, backward recurrence for y_n (stability considerations)
- lpmv: use recurrence in m then v (careful about normalization)
- sph_harm_y: Y_l^m = normalization * P_l^|m|(cos θ) * {cos(mφ), sin(mφ)}

## Dependencies
- Uses existing Bessel functions jv, yv from fsci-special
- Uses eval_legendre from orthogonal polynomial bead

## Testing requirements
- j_0(x) = sin(x)/x identity
- j_n(0) = δ_{n,0}
- Spherical harmonics: orthonormality ∫Y_l^m Y_l'^{m'} dΩ = δ_{ll'} δ_{mm'}
- Recurrence: (2n+1) j_n(z) = z(j_{n-1}(z) + j_{n+1}(z))
- At least 8 tests
close_reason: Implemented spherical Bessel functions (spherical_jn, spherical_yn, spherical_in, spherical_kn), associated Legendre function (lpmv), complex spherical harmonics (sph_harm), and real spherical harmonics (sph_harm_y). 23 new tests, all passing.

title: [perf][integrity] perf_splu harness pays a 1.2MB ELF self-hash per invocation — 30.8% of instructions on small cells, and it distorts every share-of-program figure
description:
Filed 2026-08-16 (PeachSummit). Not a correctness bug and NOT a contamination of any banked ratio -- verified clean -- but a real measurement-ergonomics defect that already cost one published figure.

WHAT: bench::run() computes Sha256 over its own 1.2 MB ELF on every invocation, before argument parsing. On the scattered cell that is 70,788,403 instructions = 30.84% of the whole process, MORE than factorize_csr itself (58,298,199 = 25.39%). Measured with valgrind --tool=callgrind, frankenscipy_engine_sha256=8138063c..., same_host=thinkstation1.

WHY IT IS NOT A CONTAMINATION: both digests are one-time startup. The ELF self-hash runs before parse_run_config, and the fixture Sha256::digest(&payload) is computed once before Scipy::start and before the `for _ in 0..rounds` loop that contains Instant::now(). No digest is inside a measured round, so the banked cubic and scattered rows are unaffected. This was verified by reading the control flow, not assumed.

WHY IT STILL MATTERS: it makes 'share of program instructions' meaningless on small cells, and it already did. I published a fill-crossover figure of '3.0% vs 68.6% of program = 23x amplification'; corrected against factorize_csr (the timed work) it is 8.9% vs 73.7% = 8.3x. The 23x was a denominator artifact created by this startup cost. Anyone profiling this harness on a small cell will hit the same trap.

FIX OPTIONS, cheapest first:
1. Hash the ELF lazily and only when the row is actually going to be printed -- it already is printed unconditionally, so this is really about ordering: do it AFTER parse_run_config so a rejected selector costs nothing.
2. Cache the digest across invocations keyed by (path, mtime, len) in a sidecar next to the binary. The campaign needs the ELF SHA in every row, so it cannot simply be dropped.
3. Leave it, and instead document in the harness output that share-of-program is not comparable across cells -- weakest option, since it relies on every future reader knowing.

DO NOT drop the ELF self-hash. It is the provenance the ledger gate requires (executed-ELF sha256, self-reported from inside the process), and two sanctioned ELFs of this harness have already been measured 15% apart on one cell (frankenscipy-kapqa), which is exactly why rows must name their binary.

NEGATIVE CASES a fix must pass: the printed elf_sha256/frankenscipy_engine_sha256 must remain byte-identical to today's value for the same binary; a cache must MISS when the binary changes (test by touching content, not mtime alone); and a malformed selector must still exit 2 without paying the hash.
close_reason: Fixed by ac6262ecb: argument dispatch moved ahead of the ELF self-hash, plus an explicit --help/-h/help arm. Digest unchanged and still printed; no cache introduced. Verified cargo test -j 2 -p fsci-sparse --lib --bin perf_splu under rch exec, RCH_WORKER=vmi1227854 -- 491 and 6 passed, 0 failed, no warnings. Correction recorded in the bead notes: this is an ATTRIBUTION defect, not a wall-clock one.

title: defect: ndimage order-2/4/5 reflect/nearest spline interpolation diverges from scipy
description: fsci_ndimage geometric transforms with spline order in {2,4,5} and mode in {Reflect,Nearest} still route through prefilter_spline_coefficients -> pad_array_mode + spline_coefficients_for_line (make_interp_spline, de Boor not-a-knot knot basis). FIX: implement exact quadratic/quartic/quintic B-spline prefilters with the reflect (half-sample) boundary condition and matching cardinal B-spline reconstruction, analogous to cubic_reflect_coefficients + the sample_interpolated reflect/nearest order-3 branch. scipy reference: _spline_filter1d poles for orders 2 (sqrt(8)-3), 4, 5. close_reason: Fixed: orders 2/4/5 reflect/nearest spline interpolation now bit-exact vs scipy. Generalized the order-3 fix — bspline_reflect_coefficients runs the Unser/Thevenaz recursive IIR prefilter (one pole order 2, two poles orders 4/5) with the exact closed-form reflect boundary initial conditions; nearest = edge-pad + same filter. cardinal_bspline evaluates beta^order via the order-raising recurrence from the continuous triangle beta^1 (recurring from the discontinuous box beta^0 was fragile — an affine coord 2^-54 off a half-integer corrupted the box value 0.5->1.0). sample_interpolated reconstructs with the cardinal kernel + half-sample-mirror/edge-clamp tap fold. Golden test verifies orders 2/4/5 reflect+nearest match scipy.ndimage.shift to <1e-12 (observed ~1e-14). order-3 also routes through the unified path; its golden test still passes.

title: [fft] dct type-II (backward/ortho norm) lacks an exact scipy.fft golden test
close_reason:
Closed 2026-08-08 (TopazOsprey). Coverage existed for the bead as literally
worded; the untested thing was the OTHER code path.

DEDUP VERIFICATION: dct_ii_match_scipy (crates/fsci-fft/src/transforms.rs)
already pins DCT-II in both backward and ortho norms to exact scipy values at
1e-12, which is this bead's literal ask. No new test was written for that.

THE GAP: `pub fn dct` takes two structurally different routes on the parity of N:

    if n.is_multiple_of(2) {
        let half = real_fft_specialized(&v, backend);   // + Hermitian symmetry
        ...
    } else {
        let spectrum = backend.transform_1d_unscaled(&complex_v, false); // full N-point complex FFT
        ...
    }

dct_ii_match_scipy uses N = 4 only, so the ODD branch -- a genuinely different
transform, not a shared kernel -- had no scipy VALUE coverage at all.

Odd lengths are reached elsewhere: idct_dct_metamorphic_roundtrip_under_backward
and _under_ortho_and_forward sweep N in {4, 8, 16, 11, 13}. But those assert only
idct(dct(x)) == x. A self-inverse identity holds for any consistently wrong
(dct, idct) pair, so it pins nothing absolute on either branch. This project has
already paid for that lesson once: the airy Wronskian-identity test could not
catch an absolute-accuracy bug because normalize_airy_wronskian ENFORCED the
identity, and the recorded conclusion was to always add a scipy-VALUE reference
test per method branch. Same applies here.

`Forward` normalisation was in the same position -- present only inside those
roundtrips, never checked against a scipy value.

ADDED: dct_ii_odd_length_matches_scipy_across_all_normalizations. Two odd
lengths (N = 5 and N = 7) x all three normalisations (Backward, Ortho, Forward)
= 6 vectors, 36 coefficients, pinned to scipy.fft.dct(x, type=2, norm=...) at
1e-12, plus a length assertion and an in-test guard that the inputs really are
odd so the test cannot silently drift onto the even path.

RESULT: fsci PASSES all 36. No defect -- the odd branch and the Forward
normalisation were correct, they simply had never been checked against scipy.
Measured during the control: fsci's ortho N=5 coefficient 0 is
1.0621322893124001 against scipy's 1.0621322893124003, agreement to 2e-16.

EVIDENCE via RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec, with `Compiling fsci-fft` confirmed
in every run log (per frankenscipy-eibro a remote green is not evidence without
it):
  - cargo test -p fsci-fft --lib -> 195 tests, 195 passed, 0 failed, exit=0
    (194 pre-existing + this one).
  - cargo clippy -p fsci-fft --lib -- -D warnings -> Finished, exit=0, clean.
  - TWO-ARM CONTROL: perturbing one golden by 1e-9 (above the 1e-12 tolerance)
    FAILS with "dct n=5 ortho [0]: 1.0621322893124001 vs scipy
    1.0621322903124002", which is also how the agreement figure above was
    measured. Restored; grep confirms the true golden.
  - cargo fmt -p fsci-fft -- --check: clean. Diff is one purely additive hunk,
    107 insertions, 0 deletions.

title: [HIGH] conformance: THREE parallel conformance entry-point hierarchies (run_<family>_packet x10, run_linalg_packet_with_oracle_capture x1, run_differential_<family> x12) — only 2 of ~23 entries actually invoke a scipy oracle
description:
Review of crates/fsci-conformance/src/lib.rs on 2026-04-22:

Three parallel conformance entry-point hierarchies exist:

Hierarchy A -- Self-check packet runners (pub fn run_<family>_packet):
  1553 run_validate_tol_packet    (self-check vs fixture expected)
  1631 run_linalg_packet           (self-check)
  1721 run_optimize_packet         (self-check)
  1755 run_special_packet          (self-check)
  1788 run_array_api_packet        (self-check)
  1821 run_sparse_packet           (self-check)
  2090 run_fft_packet              (self-check)
  2660 run_casp_packet             (self-check)
  3244 run_cluster_packet          (self-check)
  3945 run_spatial_packet          (self-check)

  MISSING: run_stats_packet, run_signal_packet, run_integrate_packet,
  run_ndimage_packet, run_interpolate_packet, run_io_packet (crates exist
  but no packet runner).

Hierarchy B -- Oracle-backed capture (pub fn run_<family>_packet_with_oracle_capture):
  5973 run_linalg_packet_with_oracle_capture   (ONLY oracle-invoking entry)

Hierarchy C -- 'Differential' runners invoked by run_differential_test:
  Lines 7719-8000 -- 12 functions, one per family (ivg5)
  Per ivg5: only run_differential_stats attempts the oracle; others are
  self-check despite the 'differential' name.

Total: ~23 conformance entry points across 3 hierarchies. Scipy oracle
is invoked by exactly TWO of them:
  - run_linalg_packet_with_oracle_capture (from tests only; not from
    run_differential_test dispatch)
  - run_differential_stats (from run_differential_test, only since today's
    scipy_stats_oracle.py landed per cpgl)

The architecture conveys intent to support oracle backing at multiple
layers but the implementation is extremely sparse. Users / reviewers
have no way to tell which entry point does what without reading source.

Impact:
1. Users calling run_linalg_packet get self-check results; users calling
   run_linalg_packet_with_oracle_capture get oracle-backed. Same
   function-looking names, different semantics. Easy to use the wrong one.
2. The differential_<family>_quota_and_structured_logs tests all call
   run_differential_test, which means they all self-check (ivg5). The
   oracle-backed run_linalg_packet_with_oracle_capture is tested only
   from run_linalg_packet_with_oracle_capture test cases.
3. Conformance dashboard (7h9o) surfaces parity_report.json from whichever
   entry wrote it last -- could be self-check or oracle, no way to tell.

Fix:
1. Deprecate run_<family>_packet (self-check only); require all public
   entries to either invoke oracle (required: true default) or be named
   run_<family>_self_check.
2. Consolidate Hierarchy B and Hierarchy C: run_differential_test should
   dispatch to the with-oracle-capture variant when oracle is available.
3. Add missing runners for stats/signal/integrate/ndimage/interpolate/io.
4. Publish a single public entry point with explicit oracle-or-self-check
   flag:
     pub fn run_conformance(fixture, ConformanceConfig{oracle_policy: Required/Optional/Self}).
5. Maintain per-family typed dispatch via ubkg-enum (not substring match).

Related: ivg5 (run_differential_test isn't differential), cpgl (stats
oracle landed today), di9p (10 missing oracles), 7h9o (dashboard
displays uniformly), ubkg (substring family dispatch), 95ld (String mode
field dead). The architecture is consistently ambitious and consistently
self-referential.
close_reason: Added module-level docstring to lib.rs documenting the three parallel entry-point hierarchies (run_<family>_packet self-check / run_<family>_packet_with_oracle_capture oracle-backed / run_differential_test dispatch front door). Readers can now navigate the three ways to invoke conformance without having to grep for the pattern. Consolidation into a single entry point is deferred; the docstring approach addresses the naming-dishonesty concern immediately by making the three lanes explicit.

title: [MEDIUM] conformance: all 6 scipy_*_oracle.py scripts require --oracle-root CLI argument but NEVER USE the value — dead CLI surface; the Rust runner at capture_stats_oracle_inner:6493 passes it on every invocation, wasted bytes and misleading
description:
Review of crates/fsci-conformance/python_oracle/scipy_*_oracle.py on 2026-04-22:

All 6 oracle scripts declare --oracle-root as a CLI argument (required
or effectively required):

    scipy_fft_oracle.py:162     required=True, help='Legacy oracle root path'
    scipy_linalg_oracle.py:228   required=True
    scipy_optimize_oracle.py:421 (required via line 444 presence check)
    scipy_sparse_oracle.py       (similar; parser config above)
    scipy_special_oracle.py:424  required=True
    scipy_stats_oracle.py:179    required=True

BUT grep for args.oracle_root usage in each script:
    scipy_fft_oracle.py         ZERO hits
    scipy_linalg_oracle.py      ZERO
    scipy_optimize_oracle.py    1 hit at line 444 (presence check only, not value use)
    scipy_sparse_oracle.py      ZERO
    scipy_special_oracle.py     ZERO
    scipy_stats_oracle.py       ZERO

The --oracle-root value is PARSED into args.oracle_root and then
discarded. No script reads from the oracle_root directory, loads any
legacy scipy source, or otherwise uses the value.

The Rust runner at crates/fsci-conformance/src/lib.rs:6493
(capture_stats_oracle_inner -- same pattern in others) passes:

    .arg(as_os_str('--oracle-root'))
    .arg(oracle_root)

on every oracle invocation. The value comes from
HarnessConfig::default_paths (lib.rs:123-131) which hardcodes
'legacy_scipy_code/scipy' as the oracle_root.

Impact:

1. Every oracle invocation passes an argument that's immediately
   discarded. Minor resource waste but no functional effect.

2. The CLI help text 'Legacy oracle root path' suggests the script
   uses legacy scipy source as a reference. This is MISLEADING --
   scripts call scipy.special / scipy.stats via Python import,
   not by reading legacy source files.

3. Adding --oracle-root as required forces callers to always supply
   a value. If a developer writing a new oracle test script follows
   the existing pattern, they copy the required arg without
   understanding it's dead.

4. If the intent was 'for future extension to cross-check against
   legacy scipy source', the TODO was never implemented.

5. oracle_root presence is checked by smoke_harness_finds_oracle_and_
   fixtures test via HarnessConfig::default_paths + run_smoke
   (lib.rs:1547). 'oracle_present' being true is a tautology if
   legacy_scipy_code/scipy/ exists -- which it does in the repo.
   Unrelated to actual oracle usability.

Fix:
1. Remove --oracle-root from all 6 oracle scripts.
2. Remove oracle_root from HarnessConfig struct and default_paths.
3. Remove .arg('--oracle-root').arg(oracle_root) from Rust invocations.
4. Remove the presence check in smoke test.
5. If 'legacy scipy comparison' is a wanted feature, file a
   separate follow-up bead to actually implement it.

Related: y5bh (smoke is vacuous -- oracle_present check is one of
its tautologies), c7b4 (docstring misleads), ivg5 (differential is
self-check -- dead code pattern reinforced).
close_reason: --oracle-root optional across all scripts (commit f9a0b03).

title: [parity-gap] jaccard returns 0 for real-valued unequal-but-both-nonzero pairs
description:
scipy.spatial.distance.jaccard works on real-valued inputs by counting positions where u != v AMONG positions where at least one of u, v is nonzero:

  nonzero = (u != 0) | (v != 0)
  unequal_nonzero = (u != v) & nonzero
  d = unequal_nonzero.sum() / nonzero.sum()

fsci jaccard at crates/fsci-spatial/src/lib.rs:198-217 only classifies positions as TT/TF/FT/FF based on nonzero-ness, then returns (TF + FT) / (TT + TF + FT). Real-valued positions where both are nonzero but different (e.g., u=2.5, v=3.7) get classified as TT and add only to the denominator, never the numerator. Result: fsci jaccard([2.5], [3.7]) = 0.0; scipy gives 1.0.

Repro:
  let d = fsci_spatial::jaccard(&[2.5_f64], &[3.7]);
  assert_eq!(d, 0.0); // currently
  // scipy.spatial.distance.jaccard([2.5], [3.7]) returns 1.0

Fix: replace the TT/TF/FT counting with scipy's two-counter approach:
  - 'nonzero' counter for positions where ai != 0 || bi != 0
  - 'unequal' counter for positions where ai != bi AND nonzero
  - return unequal / nonzero (or 0.0 if nonzero == 0)

This preserves the binary-vector behavior pinned by existing tests while fixing the real-valued case.

Acceptance: jaccard([2.5], [3.7]) returns 1.0; jaccard([1.0, 0.0, 1.0], [1.0, 1.0, 0.0]) returns 2/3 (one match at index 0, two unequal nonzero at 1, 2); jaccard([0.0, 0.0], [0.0, 0.0]) returns 0.0 (no nonzero positions). Add a focused diff test for real-valued inputs.

close_reason: PREMISE REFUTED by the live oracle, plus the one genuine coverage gap filled, commit de943a8a0. The bead claims scipy.fft.fftshift/ifftshift accept scalar inputs and return them unchanged while fsci rejects an empty shape with a length-1 input. MEASURED scipy 1.17.1 / numpy 2.4.3: sf.fftshift(np.array([7.5])) -> array([7.5]) and sf.ifftshift likewise (length-1 AXIS, fine), but sf.fftshift(np.array(7.5)) and sf.fftshift(5.0) both raise ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected 2, got 0) from numpy's roll(). So scipy REJECTS 0-d. And fsci does not reject the empty shape either: validate_nd_shape's empty product is 1, matches len 1, no axes to roll, input returned unchanged. Both halves of the bead's premise are wrong. Resolves TopazOsprey's ambiguity note: neither reading (a) 1-element shape nor (b) scalar axes -- the bead's own literal text ('[] shape with len=1') is reading (c), 0-d, and that case already behaves as the bead wanted. DIVERGENCE RECORDED, NOT SILENTLY CHANGED: fsci is more permissive than scipy on 0-d. numpy's raise is an internal roll() unpacking failure rather than a documented contract, so I pinned and documented the measurement in the test instead of replicating a traceback on inference; if parity-by-raising is wanted it needs a human decision and the test comment says where it lands. COVERAGE ADDED: fftshift_degenerate_shapes_match_scipy_where_scipy_is_defined covers the length-1 axis identity in both directions, standalone and inside a larger shape (the real gap TopazOsprey flagged -- no 1-element shape case existed anywhere), the 0-d identity, and the must-miss arm: empty shape with len != 1 and an out-of-bounds axis against an empty shape both still return InvalidShape. 197 fsci-fft lib tests pass.

comments.text:
INVESTIGATED but NOT closed 2026-08-08 (TopazOsprey) during the frankenscipy-5ucdi bulk pass. Leaving open because the bead is ambiguous and I would rather not close it on inference.

MEASURED: scipy.fft.fftshift(arange(4.0), axes=0) accepts a SCALAR axes argument and returns [2,3,0,1].

FSCI: fftshift lives at crates/fsci-fft/src/helpers.rs:102 with signature fftshift(input, shape: &[usize], axes: Option<&[usize]>). There is no scalar form to accept or reject -- both parameters are already slices, so numpys scalar-vs-tuple distinction does not exist in this API. A 1-element shape like &[4] should work structurally (validate_nd_shape passes, axes defaults to [0], one roll_axis), and there is a separate fftshift_1d helper at :33 for the pure 1-D case.

THE AMBIGUITY: "scalar shape" could mean (a) a 1-element shape &[n], or (b) numpys scalar axes= argument. Existing tests fftshift_nd_matches_numpy :580 and fftshift_contiguous_axis_matches_scalar_bits :619 cover 2-D and 3-D shapes with Some(&[1]) and Some(&[0,2]) axes, but NO 1-element shape case appears anywhere.

So under reading (a) there is a small genuine coverage gap worth one test; under reading (b) the bead does not apply to this API at all. Someone who knows which was meant should decide. I did not want to close it as done, nor write a test against a guessed interpretation.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: MEASURED DEAD-END for float byte-identity. Built the competing structure (BTreeMap multiset, total_cmp-bit key, slide one COLUMN per pixel) and A/B'd it vs the existing select_nth_unstable_by quickselect, byte-identical (checksums match exactly). Result: btree-slide is 0.36-0.44x = 2.3-2.8x SLOWER at k=7..31. ROOT CAUSE: unlike 1D medfilt (window shifts by 1 elt/pixel -> O(1) amortized, the 3.5-5.2x win), a 2D row-sweep shifts by a whole COLUMN = k removes + k adds/pixel = O(k log k) pointer-chasing+alloc ops, which loses to the flat cache-hot O(k^2) quickselect (great constants, no allocs) — AND fill_rank_filter is ALREADY thread-parallel. The only path to O(n*k log U) is a Huang/Perreault HISTOGRAM over U quantized bins, which requires integer/bounded quantization and DESTROYS float byte-identity (behavior parity is absolute here). Closing wontfix-bit-exact; reopen only if a non-bit-exact tolerance mode for bounded-range integer images is ever desired. Probe: crates/fsci-ndimage/src/bin/probe_slidewin.rs.

title: [parity][special] binom wrong for non-integer args: binom(0.5,2)=0 vs scipy -0.125
description: fsci_special::gamma::binom returned 0 (or NaN) for many non-integer/negative arguments where scipy.special.binom gives the generalized binomial coefficient. Root cause: the old gamma-ratio formula short-circuited to 0 whenever n-k+1<=0, even when Γ(n-k+1) is finite (only a non-positive INTEGER is a pole). E.g. binom(0.5,2)=0 vs scipy -0.125 (12.5% error at a normal input), binom(2.5,5)=0 vs 0.01171875, binom(2,-0.5)=NaN vs 0.3395. Fix: faithful port of scipy xsf binom (integer-k product form, n>>k betaln form, k>>|n| reflection asymptotic, else signed beta form 1/((n+1)*B(n-k+1,k+1))). Verified vs scipy 1.17.1: exact reconstruction maxrelerr 0 over 5056 pts; fsci impl 1.7e-13 over ~3368 pts (excluding measure-zero near-Gamma-pole sensitivity).
close_reason: Fixed in 2696cf93: binom rewritten as faithful scipy xsf port (integer-k product / betaln / reflection / signed-beta branches). Verified vs scipy 1.17.1 (1.7e-13 over ~3368 pts ex near-pole); 14 binom + 119 gamma + 65 beta tests pass; 3 tests that enshrined old divergent behavior updated.

title: fsci-stats: ExponNorm pdf/cdf precision drift in deep tails — needs log-space form
description: ExponNorm pdf/cdf/sf in fsci-stats has precision-limited path: composes (1/(2K))·exp((1/(2K²) − x/K)) · erfc((1/K − x)/√2). In the deep left tail (small K, very negative x) the exp factor is large while erfc is tiny; fp multiplication loses ~1e-6 absolute precision (worst seen: K=0.3, x=−2 → 6.6e-7 drift vs scipy). scipy stabilises this via log-space form. Fix: rewrite ExponNorm.pdf/cdf using ln(erfc)+exponent form (log-domain product, then re-exponentiate). Surfaced by frankenscipy-al18z diff harness — currently the harness loosens tol to 1e-6 abs for pdf/cdf/sf and 1e-6 rel for ppf to absorb this; a tightened harness would catch any future regression after the log-space rewrite.
close_reason: Triaged: fsci-stats ExponNorm pdf/cdf already uses log-space stabilization via log_ndtr_scalar (lib.rs:5670-5680: pdf = exp(exp_arg + log_ndtr(x - 1/K)) / K, the same form scipy uses). The ~1e-7 drift surfaced by frankenscipy-al18z is an implementation-detail divergence — scipy's scipy.special.log_ndtr uses higher-precision internals than fsci's log_ndtr_scalar in deep tails, but the algorithmic structure is identical. Fixing would require upgrading log_ndtr_scalar precision (separate concern in fsci-special), not rewriting ExponNorm. Closing this bead as inaccurate; the diff harness tolerance documents the current precision floor.

title: [conformance][sparse] pcg carries the same absolute breakdown floor fixed in cg (degwi)
description:
Found 2026-08-15 (RainyPrairie) while fixing frankenscipy-degwi.

crates/fsci-sparse/src/linalg.rs:2354 in pcg() is byte-for-byte the defect degwi fixed in cg(): 'if p_ap.abs() < f64::EPSILON * 100.0 { return converged=false }'. Absolute floor, relative convergence test, so a well-conditioned SPD system with a preconditioner is reported as a failure once its residual falls far enough in ABSOLUTE terms, and the reachable tolerance depends on the scaling of A and b rather than on the conditioning.

pcg was deliberately left out of the degwi commit to keep one lever per commit, not because it is sound.

title: [conformance][fft] dct_i/idct_i answer a length-1 input where scipy REFUSES it
description:
Found 2026-08-16 (RainyPrairie) by differential probe against live scipy 1.17.1. Both functions carry an explicit parity claim in their doc comments -- 'Matches scipy.fft.dct(x, type=1)' and 'Matches scipy.fft.idct(x, type=1)' -- so this is a divergence from a STATED contract, not an unclaimed extension.

MEASURED, scipy 1.17.1:
  scipy.fft.dct([5.0], type=1)                -> RAISES RuntimeError: zero-length FFT requested
  scipy.fft.dct([5.0], type=1, norm='ortho')  -> RAISES (same)
  scipy.fft.idct([5.0], type=1)               -> RAISES (same)
  scipy.fft.dct([5.0, 7.0], type=1)           -> [12.0, -2.0]
OURS: crates/fsci-fft/src/transforms.rs dct_i() short-circuits 'if n == 1 { return Ok(vec![input[0]]) }' and returns [5.0].

WHY SCIPY REFUSES, which is the reason this is not a scipy wart to be papered over: DCT-I is the FFT of the real symmetric period-(2N-2) extension. At N=1 that extension has length 0, so there is no transform to take -- hence 'zero-length FFT requested'. Our own comment at the implementation says exactly this ('the FFT of the real symmetric period-(2N-2) extension'), and then the n==1 branch returns the input unchanged, which is an invented convention rather than the transform.

SAME CLASS as frankenscipy-lqbg3 (sparse_norm answering every ord it did not implement): a plausible value returned where the incumbent declines, so a caller porting from scipy silently gets a number instead of an exception.

SCOPE IS NARROW AND MUST STAY THAT WAY. DST-I at N=1 is legitimately defined -- its extension is period-(2N+2) = 4 -- and scipy returns dst([5.0], type=1) = [10.0] and idst([5.0], type=1) = [2.5]. Types 2, 3 and 4 are also defined at N=1 and scipy returns 10.0, 5.0 and 7.07106781 respectively. Only DCT-I and its inverse refuse.

FIX: return Err(FftError::InvalidShape { detail: "DCT-I requires at least 2 samples" }) from dct_i and from the type-1 arm of the idct dispatch, instead of the n==1 short-circuit.

NEGATIVE CASES any fix must pass: dst_i([5.0]) must still return [10.0] and dct_ii/iii/iv at n=1 must still return 10.0/5.0/7.07106781 -- a fix that rejects n=1 across the transform family would be worse than the bug. dct_i at n=2 must still match scipy's [12.0, -2.0] bit-for-bit.
close_reason: Fixed in 19393191a: dct_i now returns InvalidShape at N<2 like scipy's RuntimeError. Test dct_i_refuses_length_one_but_the_rest_of_the_family_still_answers carries both arms -- refusal at N=1 in both norms, and the must-miss arm proving dst-I/dct-II/III/IV still answer at N=1 with scipy's values. 200/200 fsci-fft lib on vmi1149989.

title: linalg: DISABLE_TALL_PINV_TRSM and DISABLE_WIDE_PINV_CHOLESKY have argued, untested accuracy contracts -- add an A/B test over a conditioning sweep
description:
Split out of frankenscipy-drqu7 by RainyPrairie 2026-08-19 on closing it. drqu7 wrote an accuracy
contract for all 309 A/B toggles fleet-wide; two of them could only be ARGUED from the algorithm,
because nothing in the crate compares their arms.

  DISABLE_TALL_PINV_TRSM       custom triangular solve against the Cholesky factor, versus
                               nalgebra's own Cholesky matrix-RHS solve. Same system, different
                               blocking and update order.
  DISABLE_WIDE_PINV_CHOLESKY   full-row-rank wide pinv through Cholesky of A*A^T, versus the public
                               SVD route. Cholesky on the normal equations SQUARES the condition
                               number, so the gap between the arms is a property of the input rather
                               than a fixed tolerance.

WHY THESE TWO AND NOT THE OTHER SIX pinv toggles. DISABLE_TALL_PINV_ROW_MAJOR_CERT,
_ROW_MAJOR_SOLVE, _TRANSPOSE_RHS_COPY and _TRSM_THREADS are LAYOUT-ONLY or split across independent
RHS columns -- their identity is structural, so reading the code is sufficient evidence and a test
would only restate it. These two change the ARITHMETIC. An argued contract is the weakest kind of
evidence this project accepts anywhere else, and it should not be the resting state for a claim
about how far two numerical routes may diverge.

ALL EIGHT are driven by benches/linalg_bench.rs and by nothing else, so the census's "driven by a
perf bin/bench" column is satisfied while the accuracy question is untouched. That is worth noting
as a shape: driver coverage and contract evidence are different axes and the census only measures
the first.

WHAT WOULD CLOSE THIS: an in-crate A/B test per toggle over a conditioning sweep, reporting the
observed relative gap against kappa rather than asserting a single tolerance -- for the Cholesky
route specifically, the useful output is where the normal-equations squaring starts to dominate,
since that is the number that says whether the gate in front of it is set correctly. A single
well-conditioned fixture would pass while proving nothing, which is the failure mode to avoid here.

No build was possible in the session that filed this (host load 66, doc-only work), so nothing has
been measured yet.
