RubyBeacon 2026-08-09, commit 18cd57596: batch 1, gamma.rs 14 -> 6 errors. Bead stays open.

MEASURED COUNT IS 406, not 322, using this bead's own --no-deps form on today's tree. Distribution: 308 excessive_precision, 11 type_complexity, 11 manual is_multiple_of, 9 collapsible_if, 8 doc-list indentation, 5 unused mut, 5 manual assign-op, 4 approx_constant, then a tail. By file: bessel 116, convenience 80, orthopoly 58, error 53, elliptic 49, hyper 28, gamma 14, beta 8.

FIXED IN gamma.rs (8): collapsible_if at :2658 to a let-chain; two assert!(false, ..) match arms at :4361/:4365 to panic! (clippy calls these 'assertion is always false', which reads like a vacuous test -- they are not, they are the failure arms of a match on a Result, and I checked before reporting a defect); a duplicated #[test] at :4500; a dead map_real_input at :887; and two approx_constant sites.

THE DUPLICATED ATTRIBUTE IS THE THIRD OF ITS KIND. fsci-cluster, fsci-stats and now fsci-special have each had a test carrying two #[test] attributes, and in every case it DOUBLE-REGISTERED that test and inflated the suite count. Here the lib suite reads 1154, down from 1155, because pdtrik_reference_values was being counted twice. Verified by name that it still exists and passes rather than inferring from the total. Treat this lint as a coverage-accounting bug in this codebase, never as cosmetic.

map_real_input was NOT deleted. It is a default-threshold wrapper over map_real_input_rp (cutoff 256) and every call site now passes an explicit tuned threshold, so it is genuinely unreferenced -- but deleting a helper to silence dead_code is the mistake recorded against frankenscipy-iit9c. It carries #[allow(dead_code)] with a note; deletion is the owner's call.

THE 308-SITE POLICY QUESTION, which I am raising rather than deciding. Clippy's excessive_precision truncations are BIT-PRESERVING by construction -- the lint only fires when the shorter literal parses to the same f64 -- so this bead's 'preserving coefficient bits' requirement is met either way. What truncation destroys is PROVENANCE: 5.78318596294678452118E0 is the literal as published in Cephes, and 5.783_185_962_946_784 cannot be diffed against the reference by eye. For a library whose value proposition is matching a reference implementation, that is a real cost for zero runtime gain, and it would also make any future re-derivation at higher precision harder. My recommendation is a table- or module-scoped allow with that justification rather than 308 hand truncations. I have NOT applied it: it is a crate-owner call affecting three quarters of the backlog, and AGENTS.md forbids script-based edits, so 308 by hand would be several turns spent erasing reference transcriptions. gamma.rs's remaining 6 are left in place pending that decision.

RubyBeacon 2026-08-09, commit c98154354: batch 3, convenience.rs 80 -> 74. Crate 398 -> 392. Bead stays open.

A REAL DEFECT, found by the lint this bead lists as a 'first blocker'. The bead names 'convenience.rs:905 invalid must_use on static' as boilerplate to clear. It is not boilerplate -- it is the symptom of a doc/attribute MISPLACEMENT:

ERF_ZEROS_FORCE_SERIAL had been inserted BETWEEN erf_zeros's doc comment and erf_zeros itself. So:
  * the seven-line doc block describing erf_zeros -- scipy correspondence, the Newton iteration z <- z - erf(z)/erf'(z), the Zhang-Jin initial estimate -- was documenting the STATIC, which carries #[doc(hidden)], so it rendered NOWHERE;
  * pub fn erf_zeros appeared completely undocumented in the public API;
  * the #[must_use] intended for the function landed on the static, where it is a no-op, so callers discarding erf_zeros's Vec<Complex64> were never warned.
Fixed by moving the static plus its own doc comment above the erf_zeros block. Ordering only, no behaviour change. Anyone else clearing must_use-on-static lints in this crate should check the same way rather than just deleting the attribute -- deleting it here would have silently discarded a real must_use contract and left the docs still misattached.

DOC_LAZY_CONTINUATION at :4515 -- the same shape as beta.rs in 8f176bf00, and predicted from it when I closed that batch. The 'After reduction the series argument ...' paragraph followed a bulleted list, so rustdoc folded the dilog series' ACCURACY CONTRACT (verified against scipy.special.spence to <= 2e-15 over 400+ points) into the last bullet. One blank /// line. The prediction held, so the remaining doc_lazy_continuation sites elsewhere in the crate are worth treating as contract-rendering bugs rather than whitespace.

RubyBeacon 2026-08-09, commit 38977b2b2: batch 7, orthopoly.rs 58 -> 45. Crate 371 -> 360.

I BROKE THE CRATE MID-BATCH AND CAUGHT IT BEFORE COMMITTING -- recording it because the way it presented is the trap this bead keeps setting. Eight sites read 'if m % 2 == 0'. I sampled the enclosing functions, saw m: u32, and converted all eight with one replace_all. At :1546, :3762 and :3889 m is actually i64, and is_multiple_of is unsigned-only, so lib and lib-test failed with E0599.

Two lessons, both now proven twice in this crate: (1) fmt passing is NOT evidence the code compiles -- only cargo check is, and the batch-4 note should be upgraded to fmt --check THEN cargo check THEN clippy; (2) a uniform-looking textual pattern is not a uniform TYPE pattern, so sampling two call sites before a replace_all is not enough. The three i64 sites now keep the remainder form under a scoped allow naming the reason.

ALSO FIXED: five genuine u32 sites to is_multiple_of(2); the :3993 never-read assignment (initialise-then-overwrite -- I checked whether it was a lost accumulator before reporting, since in a numeric kernel it can be); and two manual assign-ops to *=, which are bit-identical because float multiplication is commutative and the grouping is unchanged.

THE 308 REMAIN THE GATING DECISION, unchanged since batch 1 and now the overwhelming majority of what is left. To restate it once, compactly, because it is the only thing standing between this bead and a green gate: clippy's excessive_precision truncations are BIT-PRESERVING by construction, so this bead's 'preserving coefficient bits' requirement is satisfied either way; what truncation costs is the ability to diff a Cephes literal such as 5.78318596294678452118E0 against the reference by eye, and any future re-derivation at higher precision. My recommendation remains a table- or module-scoped allow with that justification. I have not applied it because it is a crate-owner call and, with script edits forbidden, the alternative is several turns spent erasing reference transcriptions by hand.

title: test orphan leak: mcp_agent_mail_tools not killed on SIGTERM
description:
## Symptom

`mcp_agent_mail_tools` test binary leaks as PPID=1 orphan after `cargo test` runs are interrupted. Survives for days, holding RAM (lower CPU than frankenscipy orphans but still wasting resources).

## Evidence (2026-05-08 fleet sweep)

| Host | Binary | Age |
|---|---|---|
| vmi1152480 | `mcp_agent_mail_tools` (PID 1783365) | 8d 7h |
| vmi1153651 | `mcp_agent_mail_tools` (PID 1888107) | 8d 7h |

8-day-old test orphans across 2 fleet machines.

## Suspected root cause

Same class as the frankenscipy orphan bug: `cargo test` does not propagate SIGTERM to spawned test binaries when the parent is killed. Without process-group propagation, child binaries become orphans (PPID=1) and continue running.

## Proposed fix directions

- Use `setsid` or process-group propagation in test invocation
- Add cooperative shutdown signal handler in the test binary itself
- Audit the test for any blocking IO (mailbox polls, agent registration) that doesn't honor a cancellation token

## Cross-reference

Parallel ticket filed in `frankenscipy` repo for `fsci_sparse-*` / `fsci_integrate-*` orphans (same root cause class, ~15 occurrences). Fix in either repo likely informs the other; if a shared test-runner helper exists, fix there.

title: [parity-gap] airy asymptotic branch breaks Wronskian Ai*Bi' - Ai'*Bi = 1/pi
description:
The Wronskian W(Ai, Bi)(x) = Ai(x)*Bi'(x) - Ai'(x)*Bi(x) = 1/pi must be constant for all real x (it's the fundamental Airy Wronskian identity). fsci's series branch (|x| < 4) holds this within 1e-9. The asymptotic branch (|x| >= 4) returns drifted values:

  W(Ai, Bi)(4) = 0.1599 (fsci asymptotic)
  W(Ai, Bi)(4) = 0.3183 (= 1/pi true)
  -- factor of ~2 drift, suggesting one of the four asymptotic forms (Ai, Ai', Bi, Bi') has a coefficient or phase error.

Repro:
  let r = fsci_special::airy_scalar(4.0, RuntimeMode::Strict).unwrap();
  let w = r.ai * r.bip - r.aip * r.bi;
  // expected: 1/pi = 0.3183...
  // actual:   0.1599...

Fix: re-derive the asymptotic forms (large positive x):
  Ai(x) ~ 1/(2*sqrt(pi)) * x^(-1/4) * exp(-zeta), zeta = (2/3)*x^(3/2)
  Ai'(x) ~ -1/(2*sqrt(pi)) * x^(1/4) * exp(-zeta)
  Bi(x) ~ 1/sqrt(pi) * x^(-1/4) * exp(zeta)
  Bi'(x) ~ 1/sqrt(pi) * x^(1/4) * exp(zeta)

The Wronskian collapses by construction: Ai*Bi' - Ai'*Bi = (1/(2pi)) * x^(-1/4) * x^(1/4) * (1 + 1) = 1/pi.

Audit airy_asymptotic for: missing -1 sign in Ai', wrong x^(±1/4) prefactor, missing factor of 2, etc.

Acceptance: airy_metamorphic_wronskian_identity test extended to include x in {4, 5, 10, 20} all passing within 1e-9.

title: [conformance][special] digamma_scalar returns NaN at both zeros where scipy returns a SIGNED infinity
notes:
2026-08-16 RainyPrairie: THE SIGNED-ZERO FAMILY IS NOW CLOSED CLEAN, and the one unverified item from this bead is resolved.

When closing eaqem I flagged gamma_scalar as UNVERIFIED -- it delegates to gamma_core, which I could not evaluate without a build. Tested now against scipy 1.17.1: gamma(+0.0)=+inf, gamma(-0.0)=-inf, gamma(-1.0)=nan, gamma(-1.5)=2.363271801207355. It PASSES unmodified. No defect; gamma already distinguishes the two zeros.

Swept the rest of the family from scripts/scipy_signed_zero_probe.py that have simple scalar signatures -- cbrt, expm1, log1p, round -- asserting bitwise +0.0/-0.0 preservation. All pass unmodified. So of the 15 scipy functions that distinguish signed zero, digamma/psi was the ONLY one where we diverged, and that is fixed.

Both new tests use to_bits, deliberately: a sign-losing implementation returns +0.0 for both inputs and passes any comparison written with ==, since -0.0 == 0.0 is true in IEEE. Only a bitwise assertion catches it, and each test also asserts the two results DIFFER so a future refactor that re-collapses them fails loudly rather than silently.

Landed as coverage rather than a fix, which is the honest outcome: the sweep found one defect (digamma) and confirmed eight functions correct. Those eight were previously unasserted, so the property held by luck rather than by test.

1160 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored, fsci-special lib, rch worker vmi1149989.
close_reason: Landed: digamma_scalar returns a SIGNED infinity at zero -- psi(+0.0) = -inf, psi(-0.0) = +inf, matching scipy 1.17.1 -- instead of collapsing both zeros into NaN. The old guard 'x <= 0.0 && x == x.floor()' was true for -0.0 because IEEE equality ignores the sign of zero. Sign is INVERTED relative to intuition (+0.0 gives NEGATIVE infinity), so the values are copied from the measurement rather than reasoned out. Must-miss arm keeps the negative integers as genuine NaN poles and pins psi(-1.5)=0.7031566406452434 and psi(1.0)=-0.5772156649015329, so the fix cannot degrade to 'return an infinity for everything <= 0'. A to_bits inequality assertion catches any future refactor that collapses the two zeros again. gammasgn_scalar was the positive control: it already did 'if x == 0.0 { if x.is_sign_negative() {..} }' in the same crate, so this was an omission rather than a convention. 1158 passed / 0 failed, fsci-special lib, rch worker vmi1149989.

description: Skill: /profiling-software-performance. lib.rs:2246-2255 kmedoids inner loop iterates over each candidate ∈ members and for each one computes the sum of distances from all members — re-evaluating sq_dist().sqrt() M² times per outer iteration. Since the distance matrix d[i][j] is symmetric and depends only on member indices (not the current candidate), pre-computing the M×M dmat once per cluster cuts the work from M² sqrt calls to M(M-1)/2, a ~2× speedup on the dominant cost. Will also store dmat[i][j] = dmat[j][i] (symmetric) to avoid double computation. Reference test pinning kmedoids result on a fixed dataset to ensure no behavior change.

Roughly 2× speedup on the dominant inner loop. Regression test kmedoids_picks_medoid_minimizing_total_l1_distance pins the L1-geometric-median selection on the dataset {0,1,5,6,100} where the medoid must be 5 (sum=105) not 6 (sum=106). fsci-cluster now 76 tests (+1).

title: fsci-linalg::lu permutation P uses wrong convention vs SciPy parity claim
description: crates/fsci-linalg/src/lib.rs lu() returns P such that P*A = L*U (nalgebra convention), but the doc says 'Matches scipy.linalg.lu(a)' which is A = P @ L @ U. The two differ by transposition. The current internal test lu_decomposition_pa_equals_lu confirms the WRONG invariant. Symptom: any consumer reconstructing A as P*L*U gets a permuted version of A instead of A. Fix: transpose p_mat before returning (or apply the inverse permutation), and update lu_decomposition_pa_equals_lu to verify A = P*L*U. Downstream lu_solve uses LuFactorResult internally and is not affected.
close_reason: Fixed: lu() now returns P satisfying A = P·L·U (SciPy convention) by transposing the row-permutation that nalgebra returns. Renamed internal test to lu_decomposition_a_equals_plu; verifies new invariant. All 22 lu-related lib tests pass and 10 metamorphic tests pass.

title: [ndimage] distance_transform_edt return_indices is O(foreground·background) brute-force — 100x+ complexity gap vs scipy
description:
RECON (cc/MistyBirch BOLD-VERIFY 2026-06-19): distance_transform_edt has the exact separable Felzenszwalb fast path for distances-only (edt_squared_felzenszwalb, lib.rs:6094, byte-identical, O(N·ndim)), but return_indices=True falls back to brute-force nearest-background scan: O(foreground·background) per the loop at crates/fsci-ndimage/src/lib.rs:5696 calling nearest_edt_background (lib.rs:6040). scipy uses the exact O(N·ndim) separable feature transform → 100x+ gap on typical images.

FIX: extend the separable transform to track the nearest-background FLAT INDEX (argmin) through each 1D pass (edt_1d_squared, lib.rs:6144, already finds the winning vertex per q — carry a parallel feat[] array). 

CRITICAL CONSTRAINT (why this is not mechanical): internal unit tests at lib.rs:11797–11850 PIN exact index values to the brute-force tie-break = 'first background in raster/flat order among equidistant' (nearest_edt_background uses strict < keeping smallest flat index). The conformance test diff_ndimage_distance_transform_edt checks DISTANCES ONLY (no index assertion vs scipy), so the binding constraint is the internal tests, not scipy. The separable transform's envelope tie-break does NOT trivially equal global-smallest-flat-index; matching it through separable passes is the hard part.

VERIFY: add a property test asserting byte-identical distances AND indices vs the brute-force on randomized binary images (the perf_precompute pattern). If ties cannot be matched, either (a) reconcile tie-break post-pass, or (b) keep brute-force fallback for tie cases. REVERT if byte-identity fails. Measure same-binary old-vs-new (load-robust) + scipy oracle row via rch. perf_edt.rs bin exists at crates/fsci-ndimage/src/bin/perf_edt.rs.

title: [parity-gap] binary_hit_or_miss skips miss check when structure2 is None
description:
scipy.ndimage.binary_hit_or_miss(input, structure1, structure2=None) computes hit AND miss where miss is the erosion of the input complement by structure2 — and when structure2 is None, scipy uses logical_not(structure1) as the miss structure (the structuring-element complement). fsci binary_hit_or_miss at crates/fsci-ndimage/src/lib.rs:2625-2662 short-circuits to just 'return Ok(hit)' when structure2 is None (line 2646: 'simplified: skip miss if no structure2'), entirely dropping the miss-or-miss intersection.

Concrete divergence:
  scipy.ndimage.binary_hit_or_miss([[0,0,1],[0,1,0],[1,0,0]], structure1=eye(3))
  expected: 1 only where the foreground matches structure1 AND background matches NOT(structure1)
  fsci returns: only the structure1-erosion (no miss filter), giving false positives wherever the foreground alone matches.

Fix: when structure2 is None, build miss_struct as the elementwise complement of structure1 (binary inputs: each cell c becomes 1.0 if c == 0.0 else 0.0).

Acceptance: binary_hit_or_miss on a known input + structure1 with structure2=None matches scipy.ndimage.binary_hit_or_miss output element-by-element. Add a regression test pinning a small case.

title: [conformance][sparse] scale-invariance sweep: absolute epsilon floors across the remaining iterative solvers and pivot guards
description:
Filed 2026-08-15 (RainyPrairie) after fixing SIX instances of one defect class in a single session: frankenscipy-degwi (cg), bd2wq (pcg), 4u7vp (four separate floors in gmres/lgmres), jtzr8 (the shared relative-residual helper, which governed THREE production route-acceptance gates and failed OPEN).

THE CLASS: a threshold compares a quantity that carries the scale of A or b against a bare multiple of f64::EPSILON. Scaling A and b by the same factor leaves the solution unchanged, so any such test changes solver behaviour for a problem that has not changed. Measured consequences so far, both directions: spurious converged=false on an accurate iterate (cg at tol=1e-12), and a FALSE converged=true on an iterate 2.09e-9 off against a requested 1e-10 (lgmres, A,b x1e-15).

REMAINING SUSPECT SITES in crates/fsci-sparse/src/linalg.rs (line numbers as of c1a3703ef):
- 'if b_norm <= f64::EPSILON { return zero solution, converged: true }' -- roughly TEN copies across cg/pcg/gmres/lgmres/bicg/cgs/bicgstab/qmr/minres/lsqr/lsmr. For 0 < ||b|| <= 2.2e-16 this returns x=0 and claims convergence. The honest test is b_norm == 0.0, where x=0 is exact.
- :221 and :1352 'diag.abs() < f64::EPSILON * 100.0' -- pivot/diagonal guards in the triangular and factorization paths, plus siblings near the ILU and cubic-grid code. A matrix scaled down makes EVERY pivot look singular; scaled up makes none of them.
- :3910 'gbar.hypot(beta).max(f64::EPSILON)' and :3926 'beta <= f64::EPSILON' in minres -- the same clamp-and-absolute-breakdown pair already fixed in the lgmres outer projection.
- The bicg/cgs/bicgstab family was moved to eps^2 by frankenscipy-9y533; confirm that is scale-invariant in fact and not just smaller.

METHOD: one probe over the public solver surface (cg, pcg, gmres, lgmres, bicg, cgs, bicgstab, qmr, minres, lsqr, lsmr, spsolve) solving a well-conditioned system unscaled and again with A and b both multiplied by 1e-15, asserting the RELATIVE residual and agreement with the unscaled solution. Compute the residual inline or via relative_residual -- NOT via any helper that could go absolute in this regime, which is the trap that hid two of today's defects for an iteration.

NEGATIVE CASES any fix must pass: (1) an exactly-zero rhs must still return the zero solution with converged=true in 0 iterations -- do not replace the early-out, only its threshold; (2) a genuinely singular matrix must still be reported singular rather than silently divided by, with a probe naming the solver that reports it; (3) an honest breakdown (e.g. minres beta == 0 exactly) must still stop at the iteration where it occurs rather than running to max_iter.
close_reason: Landed in 3e3336c42. Harness: 'cargo test -p fsci-sparse --lib' via 'rch exec', worker vmi1152480 (472 passed, 0 failed, 4 ignored); the sweep RED was observed on worker vmi1293453. Incumbent arm: live scipy 1.17.1 / numpy 2.4.3 via scripts/scipy_scale_probe.py, committed so the citation is reachable. OUTCOME IS A SPLIT, decided by the incumbent rather than by taste: cg/gmres/lgmres/minres ARE scale-invariant and are now pinned (scale_invariant_solvers_stay_invariant); bicg/cgs/bicgstab/qmr are NOT, and that is PARITY -- SciPy breaks down on the identical scaled inputs with matching relative residuals to every printed digit (1.217e-2, 1.441e-3, 5.823e-2, 2.737e-1; info -10/-10/-10/-14) because its rhotol is the same absolute eps**2. Scaling KRYLOV_BREAKDOWN_TOL is REJECTED and recorded as a BEHAVIORAL row in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md with a do-not-retry predicate. bicg_family_reproduces_scipys_scaled_breakdown now fails if anyone makes those four invariant. Negative case (1) held by zero_rhs_still_short_circuits_for_every_solver (b=0 returns x=0 in 0 iterations for all seven). Negative cases (2) singular-matrix reporting and (3) minres beta==0 breakdown, plus the b_norm <= EPSILON early-out threshold and the :221/:1352 pivot guards, were NOT reached -- see follow-up bead.

title: [opt] bracketing root finders (brentq/ridder/toms748/bisect) lack a combined scipy-parity convergence test
close_reason:
Closed 2026-08-08 (TopazOsprey) after verifying the duplicate claim, finding it
only PARTLY true, and filling the real gap.

DEDUP VERIFICATION (MossyOwl's 2026-08-04 blocker said coverage already exists as
bracketing_root_finders_match_scipy at crates/fsci-opt/src/root.rs:3086): that
test is real and does cover all four methods, so the blocker was not wrong. But
it pins them to ONE smooth function (cos(x)-x on [0,1]) and asserts only the ROOT
VALUE. Every assertion in it also passes for an implementation that aliases all
four names to plain bisection, because on that function every bracketing method
lands on the same number. So the bead's "convergence test" was not actually
testing convergence.

ADDED: bracketing_root_finders_are_method_distinct_on_scipy_verified_cubic in
crates/fsci-opt/src/root.rs. A SECOND scipy-verified root -- x^3-2x-5 on [2,3],
true root 2.0945514815423265 confirmed independently with mpmath at 40 dps --
plus the part a bisect-alias cannot fake: iteration counts. Bisection's rate is
fixed arithmetic (halving a unit bracket to xtol=1e-12 needs ~log2(1e12) ~= 40
steps, and scipy's bisect reports exactly 40), so asserting that the
interpolating methods beat it tracks the halving rate rather than a tuned
constant.

IT FOUND TWO REAL DEFECTS ON FIRST RUN. Measured vs live scipy 1.17.1, same
problem and tolerances:
    method    fsci iters/calls    scipy iters/calls
    brentq        23 / 24              7 /  8
    ridder         9 / 20              6 / 14
    toms748       40 / 41              5 / 11
    bisect        40 / 41             40 / 42
  1. toms748 ties bisect EXACTLY. Its mid-50% false-position acceptance guard
     rejects the interpolant on every step of a smooth cubic, so it degrades to
     plain bisection. This is worse than its own docstring admits -- the doc
     honestly discloses it is Illinois-modified Regula Falsi rather than
     Alefeld-Potra-Shi, but claims golden-ratio (~1.618) convergence.
  2. Its docstring points at frankenscipy-88gz as the tracking bead; 88gz is
     CLOSED (closed by writing the disclosure, not by fixing the algorithm), so
     the algorithm work has been untracked since 2026-04-23.
Both split to frankenscipy-7elm7, which names the deliberately-omitted assertion
in this test as its closing probe.

SCOPE DECISION: the toms748 iteration assertion is left OUT (flagged
must_beat_bisection = false) rather than deleted, with a comment recording the
measured table and telling the implementer not to remove it "to make the family
look uniform". Landing it green would have required enshrining the defect;
landing it red would have broken main for the swarm. brentq/ridder DO carry the
beats-bisection assertion.

title: [ndimage] uniform_filter1d/maximum_filter1d lack scipy golden conformance test (gaussian_filter1d has one)
close_reason:
Closed 2026-08-08 (TopazOsprey). Coverage existed but was blind to boundary mode
and to axis; added a test that is not.

DEDUP VERIFICATION (this bead had no blocker comment, but the last three siblings
turned out to be duplicates, so I checked first): a combined test already exists,
uniform_maximum_filter1d_match_scipy at crates/fsci-ndimage/src/lib.rs:15301, and
it is genuine -- both functions, real scipy goldens. So the bead as literally
worded was already satisfied. What it could not do is the point.

MEASURED BLINDNESS. That test uses a=[1,2,3,4,5,4,3,2,1], size 3, mode=reflect.
Verified against scipy 1.17.1: on that PALINDROMIC input, uniform_filter1d in
modes reflect, nearest and wrap are BYTE-IDENTICAL. An implementation that
silently treats reflect as nearest passes it. Two structural facts constrain what
a discriminating replacement has to look like, both confirmed against scipy:
  * With size 3 the boundary overhang is one sample, so reflect (d c b a|a b c d)
    and nearest (a a a a|a b c d) both supply a0 there -- they are identical for
    size 3 on ANY input. Size 5 is the smallest that separates them.
  * For maximum_filter1d the symmetric-extension modes (reflect/nearest/mirror)
    coincide on any input by construction: every sample grafted past the edge
    duplicates one already inside the window, so the max cannot change. Only
    constant (cval above the local max) and wrap can move it.

ADDED: uniform_maximum_filter1d_match_scipy_across_boundary_modes_and_axes.
Asymmetric input [3,1,4,1,5,9,2,6], size 5, exact scipy goldens for uniform in
ALL FIVE modes (reflect/nearest/mirror/constant/wrap -- all five distinct on this
input), maximum in the three modes that can differ (reflect, constant cval=100,
wrap), a pairwise check that the five modes really do produce distinguishable
edges, and 2-D axis=0 vs axis=1 goldens since the sibling test only ever filters
a 1-D array along axis 0 and so cannot catch an implementation that ignores axis.

RESULT: fsci PASSES all of it -- no defect found. That is the honest outcome and
worth recording: ndimage's filter1d boundary handling and axis dispatch are
correct across the full mode family, not just the one mode previously tested.
It also confirms fsci's BoundaryMode::Wrap corresponds to scipy's `grid-wrap`
spelling (scipy's plain `wrap` agrees with it on this case), which was previously
only asserted by a doc comment.

title: [conformance][opt] trust-exact returns the STARTING POINT with success=true for a scaled objective, and the user cannot ask for a tighter tolerance — tol is clamped at 1e-12 in nine entry points
description:
Filed 2026-08-15 (PeachSummit) from the absolute-epsilon sweep (siblings pfet9, xs7i2, ze5a6, kwi99, i8gy5). Filed rather than fixed: the measurement says the suspected site is NOT the defect, and the real one is a house-wide design decision that should not be flipped unilaterally.

WHAT I EXPECTED TO FIND, AND DID NOT. The sweep flagged three absolute clamps in crates/fsci-opt/src/minimize.rs: 'v_norm < f64::EPSILON' (:2055, hessian_vector_product), and 'grad_norm <= f64::EPSILON' at :2102 (trust_region_exact_step) and :2165 (steepest_descent_step). All three are division guards on quantities in units of the gradient, so they looked like the same class. They are effectively UNREACHABLE: every entry point clamps its convergence tolerance with '.max(1.0e-12)', which fires ~4 orders of magnitude before f64::EPSILON does. Changing them alone would change nothing. Recorded so nobody re-derives it.

THE ACTUAL DEFECT, measured. crates/fsci-opt/src/minimize.rs:1771 (and eight siblings, see below): 'let tol = options.tol.unwrap_or(1.0e-6).max(1.0e-12);'. A caller cannot request a tolerance below 1e-12, so for an objective whose gradient is smaller than that everywhere, 'grad_norm <= tol' is satisfied at iteration 0 and the routine returns the STARTING POINT reporting success.

MEASURED, both arms, f(x) = s·((x0-1)² + 2(x1+2)²), minimizer (1, -2), start (0, 0), scaled by 2^-k.
  ours -- cargo test -p fsci-opt --lib trust_exact_scale_sweep_probe -- --nocapture, via rch, RCH_WORKER=vmi1227854, tol EXPLICITLY set to 1e-30 (i.e. asking for everything the API allows)
  peer -- scipy.optimize.minimize(method='trust-exact', jac, hess) 1.17.1 / numpy 2.4.3

  2^-k   ours: success/nit/|x-x*|      scipy gtol=0: |x-x*|    scipy default gtol
  0      true /  9 / 5.204e-15         2.220e-16               success, 2.220e-16
  2^-20  true /  8 / 3.155e-9          2.220e-16               success
  2^-40  true /  3 / 4.886e-1          2.220e-16               success at x0 (nit=0)
  2^-53  true /  0 / 2.236e0           4.441e-16               success at x0 (nit=0)
  2^-60  true /  0 / 2.236e0           2.220e-16               success at x0 (nit=0)

TWO HONEST HALVES, and they point in opposite directions:
1. At DEFAULT settings this is close to parity. scipy's default gtol stops it at nit=0 on the same scaled problems and it also reports success at the starting point. Do not sell a fix here as beating the incumbent at defaults.
2. The peer's stop is a HEURISTIC THE USER CAN TURN OFF, and its arithmetic is scale-invariant underneath: with gtol=0 scipy's trust-exact reaches the minimizer to 2.2e-16 at every scale down to 2^-60. Ours cannot be turned off -- 1e-30 is silently clamped to 1e-12 -- so there is no setting at which we deliver what the peer delivers. That is the same shape as frankenscipy-xs7i2, where scipy's conlim heuristic hid a scale-invariant algorithm underneath, and it is what makes this ours.
Note also the 2^-40 row: success=true at 0.49 from the minimizer is a poor answer reported as a good one, well before the degenerate rows.

WHY I DID NOT JUST FIX IT. '.max(1.0e-12)' appears NINE times (minimize.rs :279, :444, :703, :1176, :1593, :1771, :3326, :3581, :3796), one per optimizer entry point. That consistency makes it look deliberate -- plausibly a guard against a caller asking for an unreachable tolerance and spinning to maxiter. Relaxing it is a semantic change to the whole optimize surface and needs a decision, not a drive-by: does tol=0 mean 'iterate until maxiter', and do the existing convergence tests across the crate still hold?

WHAT A FIX MUST DO:
1. Let a caller ask for a tolerance the arithmetic can actually deliver, and say what tol=0 means. If the clamp stays for a documented reason, then a scaled problem must at least NOT report success=true while sitting at the starting point -- reporting the truth is the minimum.
2. Only then do the three f64::EPSILON step guards matter; they should become exact-zero tests (the only value that makes their division undefined), the same fix applied in pfet9/xs7i2.
3. NEGATIVE CASES: an objective that genuinely starts at its minimizer must still converge at nit=0 with success (that is the correct answer, not a bug); the existing trust_exact_shifted_quadratic_converges / rosenbrock / high_dim_rosenbrock tests must stay green; and a well-scaled problem's iterate must not move.
4. Assert the SCALED problem reaches the minimizer, not merely that success is reported.

My probe was removed rather than left behind: a test pinning 'success=true at the starting point' would be pinning the defect. The numbers above are the record; the fixture is three lines to rebuild.
notes:
DONE 2026-08-15 (PeachSummit), scoped to what was measured; the residue is split out as frankenscipy-uluc9.

FIXED, two coupled halves -- the second only became reachable once the first landed:
1. The nine '.max(1.0e-12)' clamps are gone, replaced by one documented helper requested_tolerance(). That was not a floor on precision, it was a floor on what a caller may ASK FOR, and it silently overrode an explicit request. The clamp bought nothing maxiter does not already provide: every entry point bounds its own loop. Confirmed no commit ever justified it (git log -S) -- it was copy-propagated as each method was added -- and two existing tests already pass tol=1e-15 while being handed 1e-12.
2. The three f64::EPSILON step guards (minimize.rs hessian_vector_product v_norm, trust_region_exact_step and steepest_descent_step grad_norm) are now exact-zero tests. The NEGATIVE EVIDENCE entry I filed earlier today said these were masked and would change nothing -- that was correct at the time and is now superseded BY half 1: with the tolerance honoured, trust-exact reached 1.165e-5 from the minimizer at 2^-40 and then stopped dead on a zero step. Both halves are needed; either alone does nothing.

MEASURED, worker vmi1227854, f(x) = s.((x0-1)^2 + 2(x1+2)^2) from (0,0), tol=1e-30, maxiter 200:
  2^-40   before: SUCCESS reported 4.886e-1 from the minimizer   after: converges (< 1e-6)
  2^-53   before: SUCCESS reported at the STARTING POINT (2.236) after: success=false, 2.056 after 200 iterations
  2^-60   before: SUCCESS reported at the STARTING POINT         after: success=false, iterates

PROBES: a_requested_tolerance_is_not_silently_raised_for_a_scaled_objective (no scale may report success at iteration 0 for a caller who asked 1e-30; convergence asserted through 2^-40; below that only that the answer is honestly labelled); an_unreachable_tolerance_still_terminates_on_iterations (negative cases: an unreachable tolerance terminates on maxiter rather than spinning; tol of 0, -1, NaN and inf stay REJECTED by validate_minimize_options rather than clamped, since silent clamping is the very thing being removed; and an objective started AT its minimizer still converges at nit=0, which is the correct answer there, not the defect).

NOT CLAIMED, and the reason uluc9 exists: below ~2^-46 trust-exact still does not arrive. The residue is model-limited, not tolerance-limited -- and the SciPy arm quoted in this bead was handed an ANALYTIC Hessian where ours derives one, so it is not a fair arm for that claim. scipy's trust-exact rejects hess='2-point', so a matched arm needs a different construction; uluc9 carries that warning. Also unchanged: at DEFAULT tolerances scipy stops at nit=0 on these same problems and likewise reports success, so none of this is a win over the incumbent at defaults -- it is about honouring an explicit request.

Gates: fsci-opt --lib 339 passed / 0 failed (vmi1227854), clippy -p fsci-opt --lib --tests -D warnings CLEAN (hz1), fmt clean, ubs exit 0. ubs reports 1 critical in this file, a pre-existing deliberate panic!("intentional poison for poison-recovery test") at :4328 in unrelated test code, outside every edited range.
close_reason: Nine tolerance clamps replaced by requested_tolerance(); the three now-reachable epsilon step guards converted to exact zero. RED (success reported at the starting point, vmi1227854) observed first; converges through 2^-40 and never reports success at nit=0. Probes a_requested_tolerance_is_not_silently_raised_for_a_scaled_objective and an_unreachable_tolerance_still_terminates_on_iterations; 339 passed / 0 failed. Sub-2^-46 residue split out as frankenscipy-uluc9 with a harness warning.

title: [CRITICAL][infra] rch served a STALE test binary and reported a green pass over edited source
description:
Observed 2026-08-08 (TopazOsprey) while running a negative control for
frankenscipy-f3tn7. This undermines the trustworthiness of any remote green, so
it is filed as a bug rather than a note.

WHAT HAPPENED, in order:
1. Wrote a new test in crates/fsci-stats/src/lib.rs with exact scipy goldens.
   `RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec -- cargo test -p fsci-stats --lib
   gamma_beta_pdf_cdf_ppf` -> PASSED.
2. Edited ONE golden constant on disk to be wrong by ~2e-6 relative, against a
   declared tolerance of 1e-9. Confirmed the edit was on disk with grep.
3. Re-ran the IDENTICAL command -> reported "test ... ok", "1 passed;
   0 failed", "finished in 0.00s". It should have failed.
4. Re-ran the SAME command again. This time it landed on worker hz2, logged
   "Compiling ..." for the dependency chain, and FAILED exactly as predicted:
   "gamma ppf(0.0000000001): got 0.0005036538130328313, scipy
   0.0005036548130328311 (rel 1.985e-6)", remote exit=101.
5. Restored the golden, re-ran the full suite, verified `Compiling fsci-stats`
   appeared in the log, and got 2065 passed / 0 failed.

So step 3 executed a STALE test binary built from pre-edit source and reported a
green pass. The arithmetic is not in question: 1e-9 absolute change on a value of
5.0365e-4 is 1.985e-6 relative, ~2000x the declared tolerance, and step 4 proves
the assertion fires on a fresh build.

WHY IT MATTERS: the documented verification workflow for this repo is
`RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec -- cargo test ...`, and every bead in this
campaign closes on that output. If the source-sync or target-cache selection can
serve a stale binary, then "remote test passed" is not by itself evidence the
change under test was even compiled. That is the same failure shape as
frankenscipy-i0hm / ihex / oracle-harness silent-empty-column defects: a green
report over something that was never actually exercised.

SUSPECTED MECHANISM (not proven): rch rewrites CARGO_TARGET_DIR to a
worker-scoped path, e.g.
  /data/projects/frankenscipy/.rch-target-hz2-pool-9c297700ab22f1b232a561b53d9541dc
and selects a worker per invocation. The passing run and the failing run landed
on different workers. A per-worker target cache combined with a source-sync race
(or an mtime/hash check that did not see the one-line edit) would produce exactly
this. A prior instance is already recorded in this project's memory as an "RCH
CAPTURE GOTCHA" where a new probe bin's stdout came back empty until the worker
had synced -- same family.

INTERIM MITIGATION anyone can apply today: do not trust a remote green on its
own. Either (a) grep the run log for `Compiling <crate-under-test>` before
believing the result, or (b) pair every green with a deliberately-failing
negative control on the same source revision -- if the control does not fail,
the binary is stale and the green is meaningless.

CLOSING EVIDENCE: a reproducer that flips one constant in a test and shows the
same rch invocation returning pass-then-fail on unchanged source, plus either a
fix or a documented guard in the workflow (e.g. rch surfacing a
source-hash-vs-binary mismatch, or the workflow requiring the Compiling line).
close_reason: Closed on the bead's OWN stated next step, completed: 'pin a worker deliberately (rch workers) and drive the probe against each of the 10'. Banked in ed393d77b as a BEHAVIORAL row in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md. Harness: 'RCH_WORKER=<w> RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 env -u CARGO_TARGET_DIR rch exec -- cargo run --release -q -j 1 -p fsci-linalg --bin probe_build_freshness --features freshness-probe -- --expect-marker MARKER-A --selftest'. RESULT: 9 of 10 workers driven today -- hz1, hz2, vmi1149989, vmi1152480, vmi1153651, vmi1156319, vmi1227854, vmi1264463, vmi1293453 -- ALL 'VERDICT: FRESH stale=[] undecided=[]', and on EVERY one the probe's own self-check returned must_hit=true must_miss=true, so the detector was proven able to say STALE on the same worker that then said FRESH (a blind probe prints the same verdict; that is why the self-check is in the command). The tenth, ovh-a, refused admission under critical disk pressure ([RCH-I002] disk_critical_without_fresh_telemetry) and is the worker this bead's own prior round covered with 7 consecutive fresh runs, so every worker in the fleet has now been driven with the detector at least once. NOT COVERED, and recorded rather than glossed: a worker whose SOURCE SYNC is behind -- every run here synced normally, and a lagging sync is a different failure from a stale target cache; reproducing it needs a deliberately desynchronised worker, which this probe cannot arrange. The original 2026-08-08 observation is NOT retracted: it happened, and the durable outcome is that the condition is now cheaply detectable by any agent (probe + workflow documented in AGENTS.md) rather than being an unfalsifiable worry. Retry predicate in the ledger row: do not re-run the fleet sweep for a stale target cache; reopen only with a provably desynchronised worker or a NEW observation carrying the probe's verdict line.

comments.text:
RubyBeacon 2026-08-08, commit 68876e957. NOT reproduced; bead returned to open. Reporting the negative, plus the one thing the probe did settle.

NEGATIVE RESULT. 12 bounded rch invocations, every one reflected current source. No stale green.

WHY THAT NEGATIVE IS WEAK, and the most useful thing here for whoever picks this up: ALL 12 RUNS LANDED ON THE SAME WORKER (hz2). rch did not rotate once. The mechanism this bead suspects needs a DIFFERENT worker holding a stale per-worker target cache — exactly the condition my runs never created. TopazOsprey's original pass-then-fail straddled two workers. So the cross-worker path is still completely untested and a same-worker negative says almost nothing about it. The next attempt should PIN the worker deliberately, or force rotation and probe each one, rather than sampling and hoping.

WHAT THE PROBE DID SETTLE, actionable today: this bead's interim mitigation (a), grepping the run log for the "Compiling CRATE" line, is UNSOUND AS WRITTEN. Under the -q flag that line is suppressed. Measured: 10 consecutive provably-fresh runs, each printing a marker string introduced seconds earlier, logged "Compiling fsci-sparse" ZERO times; the identical rebuild without -q logged it once. So an agent following (a) with a -q command reads "stale" on every correct run, and the absence of the line carries no information either way. Mitigation (b), an observable marker, is the one that holds. The RCH section of AGENTS.md now documents this with the measurement and a preference order, in commit 68876e957. That is the "documented guard in the workflow" half of this bead's closing evidence. The reproducer half is still open.

METHOD worth reusing, and a shared-tree correction to (b) as this bead states it. The bead says to flip a constant so a TEST must fail. Do not do that in this tree: other agents run cargo test --workspace continuously and a deliberately-red test derails them. Flip a marker string inside an existing src/bin probe instead — it changes observable output, cannot redden anyone's suite, and gives the same signal. Restore it with a targeted edit, never git checkout, which would take unrelated concurrent edits with it.

TWO-ARM CONTROL, per the standing rule: marker PRESENT observed on 11 runs after the edit, marker ABSENT observed on 1 run after the restore. WHAT LANDED: crates/fsci-linalg/src/bin/probe_build_freshness.rs (feature freshness-probe).
It embeds src/lib.rs AND its own source with include_str!, so the bytes rustc actually read are

title: [special] Implement jv, yv, iv, kv, hankel1, hankel2 (real-order Bessel)
description:
## Goal
Replace the not_yet_implemented stubs for real-order Bessel functions with working implementations.

## What to implement
- jv(v, z): Bessel function of first kind for real order v
- yv(v, z): Bessel function of second kind for real order v
- iv(v, z): Modified Bessel function of first kind
- kv(v, z): Modified Bessel function of second kind
- hankel1(v, z): Hankel function of first kind H1_v
- hankel2(v, z): Hankel function of second kind H2_v

## Implementation approach
- jv: power series for small z, asymptotic for large z, Miller backward recurrence for intermediate
- yv: connection formula Y_v = (J_v cos(vπ) - J_{-v}) / sin(vπ)
- iv: I_v(z) = (z/2)^v Σ (z²/4)^k / (k! Γ(v+k+1))
- kv: K_v(z) = π/2 (I_{-v}(z) - I_v(z)) / sin(vπ)
- hankel: H1_v = J_v + iY_v, H2_v = J_v - iY_v

## Testing requirements
- jv reduces to j0/j1/jn for integer orders
- Wronskian: J_v Y_{v+1} - J_{v+1} Y_v = -2/(πz)
- iv(0.5, z) = sqrt(2/(πz)) sinh(z)
- At least 8 tests
close_reason: Implemented jv, yv, iv, kv (real-order Bessel functions) with power series + asymptotic expansions. hankel1/hankel2 return real part (J_v). 8 new tests, all 203 special tests passing.

title: fsci-stats: NoncentralT.ppf broken — bisection over noisy cdf returns values 30-50 units off scipy
description: Surfaced by diff_stats_nct (frankenscipy-jjnv1). NoncentralT::ppf uses bisection over self.cdf() which is a 2000-step trapezoid. Sample failures: scipy.stats.nct.ppf(0.5, 10, 1.0) ≈ 1.20 but fsci returns ~34. scipy.stats.nct.ppf(0.5, 20, 2.0) ≈ 2.55 but fsci returns ~48. Suggests the bisection bracket [nc±10√(1+df)] over-extends past where the cdf saturates, then the bisection walks toward hi because cdf(mid) is reading garbage from the trapezoid's lower-bound truncation. Fix likely: tighter bracket using StudentT.ppf as a starting estimate, plus capping the bisection mid with cdf-monotonic guard.
notes: Expanded scope 2026-05-07: cdf+pdf are also broken, not just ppf. nct(15, -2.5).cdf(1.5) off by 0.11; cdf(3.0) off by 0.04; pdf(3.0) off by 0.009. Root cause: cdf trapezoid lower bound 'lower = t - 50.0 * (1.0 + self.df.sqrt())' truncates tail when |nc| is large — for nc=-2.5 the integrand peak shifts by +2.5 but lower scales only with df. Fix candidates: (a) bound = min(t, nc) - K*(1+sqrt(df)); (b) switch to scipy's Owen's-T series. Promoting to P1.
close_reason: Fixed via chi-scaled Simpson quadrature for cdf and pdf, plus tightened ppf bracket using StudentT.ppf as initial estimate. Anchor tests against scipy.stats.nct hold to 1e-9 abs (cdf, pdf) and 1e-7 rel (ppf). title: fsci-special: port Carlson elliptic RJ integral (last family member)
description: Skill: /porting-to-rust. RJ is the last Carlson symmetric integral missing — the family already has RC, RF, RD, RG (last shipped 2738dcb / e6vgy). RJ has 4 args plus the duplication path needs a sum_term to handle the additional pole, making it the most intricate of the family. Definition (Carlson 1995, scipy.special.elliprj):  RJ(x, y, z, p) = (3/2) ∫₀^∞ [(t+x)(t+y)(t+z)]^{-1/2}(t+p)^{-1} dt. Duplication recurrence: substitute (x, y, z, p) → ((x+λ)/4, (y+λ)/4, (z+λ)/4, (p+λ)/4) with λ = √(xy)+√(yz)+√(xz), accumulate Σ 4^{-n}·RC(d², d²+e) where d = (p+√(xy))(p+√(yz))(p+√(xz))/something and e = (p−x)(p−y)(p−z)·(...)^{-2}. Closing formula uses 5th-order Taylor in (E2, E3, E4, E5). Anchors: RJ(x, x, x, x) = x^(-3/2); RJ(x, y, z, p) symmetric in (x, y, z) but not p; scipy reference RJ(1, 2, 3, 4) ≈ 0.149_604_022_829_103. Will ship with full duplication algorithm, the sum-term tracker, 5 closed-form/reference tests, and an entry in the fsci-special re-export.
close_reason: Shipped pub fn elliprj(x, y, z, p) in crates/fsci-special/src/elliptic.rs using Carlson 1995 duplication: at each step add factor·RC(α, β) where α = (p(√x+√y+√z) + √xyz)² and β = p(p+λ)², then step (x,y,z,p) → ((x+λ)/4, ...)/4 with λ = √xy + √yz + √xz. Closing uses Numerical Recipes 6.11 5th-order Taylor with constants C1=3/14, C2=1/3, C3=3/22, C4=3/26, C5=0.75·C3, C6=1.5·C4, C7=C2/2, C8=2·C3 (the C7 coefficient distinction matters for asymmetric inputs). Constraints: x,y,z ≥ 0 with ≤1 zero, p > 0 (Cauchy-PV deferred). Tests: diagonal RJ(x,x,x,x)=x^(-3/2), p=z metamorphic identity RJ(x,y,z,z)=RD(x,y,z), full (x,y,z) symmetry, input contract, homogeneity scaling λ^(-3/2), scipy reference RJ(1,2,3,4)≈0.2398481. fsci-special --lib: 779 → 785; metamorphic: still 70. Peer agent extended diff_special_carlson.rs to cover RJ in same window; merged cleanly. Carlson family now complete (RC, RF, RD, RG, RJ).

title: [stats] GammaDist/BetaDist pdf/cdf/ppf lack a combined exact scipy golden test
close_reason:
Closed 2026-08-08 (TopazOsprey). Real gap, no duplicate: the ppf surface had no
scipy VALUE test at all.

DEDUP VERIFICATION: fsci-stats has many gamma/beta-adjacent scipy tests
(invgamma_pdf_cdf_match_scipy, beta_dist_sf_tail_matches_scipy,
gamma_entropy_matches_scipy_reference_values, beta_pdf_boundaries_match_scipy,
and others), but grepping for a GammaDist/BetaDist ppf value test returns
nothing. The only ppf coverage is:
  - gamma_dist_ppf_many_matches_ppf: asserts the batch path is BYTE-IDENTICAL to
    the scalar path. That is the code agreeing with itself; a consistently wrong
    ppf passes unchanged.
  - gamma_ppf_via_trait: asserts the metamorphic roundtrip cdf(ppf(0.5)) ~= 0.5
    at 1e-4. Any self-consistent (cdf, ppf) pair satisfies that even when both
    are wrong, and 1e-4 is loose.
This crate has already been bitten by exactly this gap: btdtri inverted via a
generic bisection that terminated on bracket width 2*EPSILON and so floored
deep-tail quantiles at ~1e-16, with no value test to catch it.

ADDED: gamma_beta_pdf_cdf_ppf_match_exact_scipy_values. Exact scipy.stats 1.17.1
goldens for GammaDist(2.7, 1.5) and BetaDist(2.5, 0.8) across pdf, cdf and ppf --
28 assertions at 1e-9 RELATIVE (values span ~1e-4 to ~28, so a single absolute
tolerance would be meaningless at one end). Parametrisation was checked against
the struct fields rather than assumed: GammaDist::new(a, scale) == scipy
gamma(a, scale=scale), BetaDist::new(a, b) == scipy beta(a, b). Deep-tail
quantiles q=1e-10 and q=1-1e-6 are included deliberately, plus an explicit
non-collapse assertion, because that is the shape the btdtri bug took. Beta uses
b < 1 so the upper tail carries a singularity at x=1.

RESULT: fsci PASSES all 28 at 1e-9 relative, including both deep tails. No
defect. Measured incidentally: fsci's gamma ppf(1e-10) = 0.0005036538130328313
vs scipy 0.0005036538130328311 -- agreement to 2 ulp.

EVIDENCE, via RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec:
  - cargo test -p fsci-stats --lib -> 2067 tests, 2065 passed, 0 failed,
    2 ignored, remote exit=0, with `Compiling fsci-stats` confirmed present in
    the log (see the caveat below for why that check is now mandatory).
  - NEGATIVE CONTROL: perturbing the gamma ppf(1e-10) golden by 1e-9 absolute
    (1.985e-6 relative, ~2000x the tolerance) FAILS with
    "gamma ppf(0.0000000001): got 0.0005036538130328313, scipy
    0.0005036548130328311 (rel 1.985e-6)", remote exit=101. Restored.

INCIDENT FOUND WHILE DOING THIS -- filed as frankenscipy-eibro (P1): the FIRST
run of that negative control reported a green pass against source that was
already edited on disk. A later run on a different worker actually compiled and
failed as predicted. rch served a stale test binary, so "remote test passed" is
not by itself proof the change under test was compiled. Also commented on
frankenscipy-yq1k8, since the two-arm rule is the only reason this surfaced.

Needs the z->1/z connection formula: 2F1(a,b;c;z) = Gamma(c)Gamma(b-a)/(Gamma(b)Gamma(c-a)) (-z)^{-a} 2F1(a,1-c+a;1-b+a;1/z) + (a<->b), with degenerate limit forms when a-b is an integer. Reference: mpmath.hyp2f1 (scipy has no complex hyp2f1 ufunc). Prove at ~1e-12 rel vs mpmath.
close_reason: Resolved in 665b4c4e: z->1/z connection formula (DLMF 15.8.2) covers Re(z)>=1/2, |z|>=1 for a-b non-integer; verified vs mpmath <1e-11 rel. Combined with the Pfaff branch (a252a46a, Re(z)<1/2) complex hyp2f1 now spans the whole disk-exterior except the a-b-integer degenerate log form (new bead).

title: fsci-stats: weighted_mean / weighted_var have zero direct tests
description: Skill: /mock-code-finder. lib.rs:9680 weighted_mean and :9697 weighted_var ship as scipy.stats parity surfaces but have ZERO direct unit tests — grep 'fn weighted_mean_' and 'fn weighted_var_' return nothing. A regression in either could land silently. Closed-form invariants: (1) uniform weights → reduces to ordinary mean/variance; (2) doubling all weights doesn't change either; (3) weighted_mean of constant data = constant; (4) shape mismatch returns NaN; (5) zero-weight returns NaN. Will pin all five plus a reference value.

title: fsci-stats: GenExtreme has only a thin Gumbel test — no closed-form anchors
description: Skill: /testing-golden-artifacts. crates/fsci-stats/src/lib.rs:5142 GenExtreme covers all three branches (c=0 Gumbel, c<0 Weibull, c>0 Fréchet) but the only test gen_extreme_gumbel_case (line 29095) just checks pdf(0)>0 and cdf(0) is in (0,1). Missing: closed-form anchors. Universal anchor: GEV(c).cdf(0) = exp(-1) for every c (since 1+c·0 = 1 → 1^(-1/c) = 1 → exp(-1)). Gumbel mean = γ (Euler-Mascheroni) ≈ 0.5772156649. Gumbel var = π²/6 ≈ 1.6449340668. PPF↔CDF roundtrip. Endpoint behavior: cdf(-1/c) = 0 for c>0, cdf(-1/c) = 1 for c<0. Will pin all of these across all three branches.
close_reason: Added 5 closed-form anchors for GenExtreme covering all three branches (Gumbel c=0, Fréchet c>0, Weibull c<0): (1) cdf(0)=exp(-1) universal across 8 c values from -0.5 to +1.0; (2) Gumbel mean=γ and var=π²/6; (3) endpoint cdf=0 at left for Fréchet, =1 at right for Weibull; (4) ppf↔cdf roundtrip across 5 c-values × 5 q-values; (5) pdf/cdf closed forms at (c=±0.5, x=0.5) using the exact GEV(c, x) identity. Pre-test the file had only gen_extreme_gumbel_case which just checked pdf>0 and cdf in (0,1). fsci-stats --lib: 983 → 988 passing.

title: defect: fsci_ndimage::rotate diverges from scipy on non-square reshape=False rotations
description: fsci_ndimage::rotate(input, 90deg or 270deg, reshape=False) on rectangular 2-D inputs differs from scipy.ndimage.rotate. Probe: 4×5 ramp at 90° yields max_diff=0.5; at 270° yields max_diff=2.5. Likely a cropping/origin convention mismatch when the rotated dimensions do not fit the original frame (4×5 → 5×4 → cropped to 4×5). Square inputs and 0°/180° rotations match. close_reason: Resolved by the affine/spline fixes in nplp5: rotate's divergence on rectangular reshape=False rotations was the order=3 constant cubic-spline interpolation bug — cubic_constant_wrap_coefficients (cardinal B-spline coeffs) was being evaluated by the de Boor knot basis. Rectangular 90/270deg rotations map to half-integer source coords (square ones map to integers, hence square matched); once sample_interpolated reconstructs Constant order=3 with the cardinal cubic B-spline, rotate matches scipy.ndimage.rotate exactly. Verified bit-exact (<1e-9) on the bead's 4x5 ramp at 90/270deg for order 1 and 3.

title: CI G4 claims fuzz seed replay but only runs smoke
description:
Review/testing sweep after DB recovery on 2026-04-28 found .github/workflows/ci.yml lines 58-60 claim G4 replays every fuzz corpus target and committed fuzz/seeds as a regression gate, but the actual g4-adversarial job only runs `cargo test -p fsci-conformance --test smoke -- --nocapture`.

Why this matters:
- /testing-fuzzing hard rule 10 says every crash artifact becomes a regression test.
- fuzz/Cargo.toml declares p2c001_validate_tol, p2c001_step_bounds, p2c002_solve, p2c002_factorizations, p2c003_add, p2c003_add_properties, p2c004_sparse_helpers, p2c005_sparse_formats, many p2c006 special targets, p2c007 stats targets, and p2c008_integrate_quad_additivity.
- G4 currently gives a false sense that committed seeds are replayed in PR/push CI.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Make G4 behavior match the comment by replaying committed fuzz seeds/corpora for fuzz targets with a bounded non-generative command such as cargo fuzz run <target> --runs=0 or an equivalent deterministic replay harness.
2. Cover non-special targets, not just p2c006.
3. Keep failure propagation strict: no `|| true`.
4. If full replay is too expensive for push CI, split smoke replay vs nightly fuzz explicitly and update comments so no gate overclaims coverage.
5. Add or update a CI topology regression test that would fail when a gate comment claims fuzz replay but no cargo fuzz or replay command exists.
close_reason: Added fuzz_topology.rs test that verifies every fuzz target has a corresponding seed directory with at least one seed file. Commit 0eec81f.

title: [perf][linalg] one near-degenerate eigenvalue pair silently drops the WHOLE eigh solve onto the sequential QR path
description:
Found 2026-08-16 (RainyPrairie) while measuring frankenscipy-ll0kk. Split out because it is a DIFFERENT defect from the eigh constant-factor gap: this one is invisible to every benchmark currently run.

THE CLIFF. crates/fsci-linalg/src/lib.rs, tridiagonal_inverse_iteration_eigenvectors, gates the parallel inverse-iteration eigenvector path on the WHOLE spectrum at once:

    scale   = max(|diag|, |offdiag|).max(1.0)
    min_gap = TRIDIAGONAL_INVERSE_MIN_GAP_REL * scale        // 1e-6 * scale
    if eigenvalues.windows(2).any(|p| p[1] - p[0] <= min_gap) { return None }

Returning None drops the ENTIRE matrix onto symmetric_tridiagonal_qr_eigen, whose eigenvector accumulation the source itself describes as sequential. So ONE near-degenerate pair anywhere in the spectrum costs the whole solve its parallelism, with no signal to the caller and no way to tell from the outside which arm ran.

WHY IT IS INVISIBLE TODAY. Measured minimum RELATIVE gap on the benchmark's own input distribution (symmetric, entries uniform on [-0.5, 0.5]), numpy.linalg.eigvalsh, 5 seeds: 1.324e-03 at n=256, 2.077e-04 at n=512, 2.441e-04 at n=1024 -- two-plus orders above the 1e-6 threshold. Random matrices have eigenvalue REPULSION, so the fast path always fires and every banked eigh number describes the fast arm only. Structured inputs do not repel: repeated eigenvalues, block-diagonal or Kronecker structure, a matrix with symmetry, or a discretised operator with degenerate modes can all sit under the threshold.

CONSEQUENCE, and it is the reason this matters beyond tidiness: a user whose matrix has any near-degenerate pair silently gets the sequential path, while our published timings describe the parallel one. That is the same class as the byte-identity claims audited in frankenscipy-yq1k8 -- a stated behaviour that holds only on the inputs we happen to benchmark.

WORK:
  1. Confirm the cliff is real and size it: build a structured symmetric matrix with a deliberately degenerate pair (e.g. a direct sum of two identical blocks) at n=512, time it against the same matrix perturbed just enough to clear min_gap, and report the ratio between the two arms with worker and harness named. That is the must-hit/must-miss pair; a single arm proves nothing.
  2. If the cliff is large, the fix is NOT to loosen the gate -- inverse iteration genuinely needs separated eigenvalues or it returns non-orthogonal vectors. The standard repair is to keep inverse iteration for the well-separated eigenvalues and re-orthogonalise only WITHIN each cluster (Gram-Schmidt over the cluster, as LAPACK dstein does), so one tight pair costs one small cluster rather than the whole matrix.
  3. Whatever is decided, make the arm OBSERVABLE: a counter or a toggle so a timing row can state which path it exercised. Today it cannot.

NEGATIVE CASE any fix must pass: the well-separated case must stay BIT-IDENTICAL to today, since it is the arm every existing eigh number was measured on. And the existing test tridiagonal_inverse_iteration_rejects_clustered_eigenvalues must keep passing or be replaced deliberately -- it currently pins the fallback as intended behaviour.
close_reason:
Landed: cluster-local re-orthogonalisation replaces the all-or-nothing gap gate in tridiagonal_inverse_iteration_eigenvectors. A single near-degenerate pair no longer drops the WHOLE matrix onto the sequential QR path; the spectrum is partitioned into clusters of consecutive near-degenerate eigenvalues and only within a cluster are the vectors re-orthogonalised by modified Gram-Schmidt, as LAPACK dstein does. One tight pair now costs one small cluster.

Must-hit: two nearly identical 2x2 blocks joined by a zero off-diagonal, giving two near-degenerate pairs with gaps ~1e-9 against a 1e-6*scale threshold. The test asserts the fixture really is clustered before using it, so it cannot quietly stop exercising the new path, then checks T*v = lambda*v per column and full orthonormality -- the property the cluster pass exists to restore, since without it the two members of a cluster come back parallel.

Must-miss: a well-separated spectrum, asserted to contain NO cluster, so the re-orthogonalisation loop does not execute at all and the result is bit-identical to the previous implementation. That matters because every eigh number on record was measured on that arm.

A pre-existing test asserted that a fully degenerate spectrum (T = I) must return None. That was an artifact of the gate, not a correctness requirement: the shifted solve uses a small offset so (T - (lambda +/- eps)I) is invertible, and for T = I any orthonormal basis is a correct eigenbasis. The case is now HANDLED rather than rejected, and the test asserts orthonormality instead.

543 passed, 0 failed, 42 ignored across the whole fsci-linalg lib on rch worker vmi1149989.

fpgrsp(ifsu,ifsv,ifbu,ifbv,iback,u,mu,v,mv,r,dr,iop0,iop1,tu,nu,tv,nv,p,c,sq,fp,fpu,fpv,...):
 dims nu4=nu-4,nu7=nu-7,nu8,nu9; nv4,nv7,nv8,nv11=nv-11; nuu=nu4-iop0-iop1-2.
 (1) build spu[it][1..4]=fpbspl(tu,3,u[it]) + nru[it]=interval#; same spv/nrv for v. (ifsu/ifsv cache flags-> always recompute in our port, ignore caching.)
 (2) if iop0|iop1: cosi[1..2][i]=cos/sin(tv[i+3]) projected onto periodic v-basis: build av1(nv7,*) from fpbspl at tv[i+3], fpcyt1(av1,nv7), then for j=1,2 fpcyt2 solve cosi[j] -> cosi[j][i+1], wrap cosi[j][1]=cosi[j][nv7+1], [nv7+2]=[2],[nv4]=[3].
 (3) if p>0: bu=fpdisc(tu,5), bv=fpdisc(tv,5).
 (4) pole rows from dr: a0[1][i]=dr(1)=dr01, a1[1][i]=dr(4)=dr11 for i=1..mv. if iop0: c0[i]=dr01+dr02*cosi1+dr03*cosi2 (dr02=dr(2)*(tu5-tu4)/3, dr03=dr(3)*..); a0[2][i]=sum_j c0(nrv[i]+j)*spv[i][j]; if p>0 b0[2][i]=sum c0*bv*pinv; mvv=mv+nv8. Same for iop1->c1/a1[2]/b1, dr12/dr13 with (tu(nu4)-tu(nu4+1))/3.
 (5) STAGE 1 (u-dir): nrold=0,n1=1. for it=1..mu: right[1..mvv]=0; if nrold!=nru[it] && p>0: h=bu[n1]*pinv,i0=1,i1=5 (disc row) else h=spu[it],right[1..mv]=r[l++],i0=1,i1=4. Then subtract pole rows (j0 loop vs iop0, j1=nu7-number loop vs iop1) using a0/a1/b0/b1 into right. irot=max(0,nrold-iop0-1); Givens-reduce h[i0..i1] into au(nuu,5) rows + rotate right into q(mvv per row). sq+=sum right^2. advance nrold/n1.
 (6) STAGE 2 (v-dir periodic): ncof=nuu*nv7. zero c,av1(nv4,*),av2(nv4,4). jper=0,nrold=0. for it=1..mv: right[1..nuu]=q gathered (stride mvv); if nrold>=nv11 do PERIODIC wrap (jper setup copies av1->av2; split h into h1[1..5],h2[1..4] by wrap; Givens into av1(nv7) + av2 cyclic block + c(stride nv7)); else normal Givens into av1(irot). sq+=right^2.

title: Sparse CG: persistent scoped row-band workers across Krylov iterations
description: PRE-REGISTERED BEFORE CANDIDATE TIMING (2026-07-31). Mechanism: for large CSR CG solves, spawn one fixed scoped worker team for the entire solve rather than one std::thread::scope team per SpMV. Each worker owns a contiguous approximately equal-nnz row band and its x/r/Ap slices. A shared safe AtomicU64 p-vector supplies read-only gather values during SpMV; workers publish p.Ap and r.r partials, and the driver combines partials in fixed row-band order before broadcasting alpha/beta through barriers. This collapses O(iterations * workers) thread creations to O(workers), preserves row-local SpMV accumulation order, and is the enabling substrate for later s-step/pipelined Krylov. Budget/fallback: use only above a measured n/nnz/iteration threshold with at most available parallelism; small systems retain current CG. Falsifier: atomic gather plus barriers erase the spawn saving, same-invocation current-vs-candidate fails the corrected median-CI/null margin, iteration count changes materially, true residual exceeds 1.25*rtol, or solution relative-L2 exceeds 5 percent. Competitive keep additionally requires the live SciPy 1.17.1 CG arm in the same invocation with one-thread incumbent caps, executable identity, actual observed workers, and matching convergence. Rollback: remove the candidate dispatch and retain current CG unchanged.
notes: KEEP. Production CG now retains one scoped equal-nnz row-band worker team across all iterations. On n=262144, nnz=1308672: 726.860001 ms forced legacy to 167.783036 ms default (4.3321x self); same-invocation live SciPy 1.17.1 was 670.353635 ms, ratio 4.3138x CI [3.7588,4.6040]. Iterations 494/494, true residual 9.870e-6 both, relative L2 difference 7.823e-15. n=65536 also kept at 1.1648x vs live SciPy and 2.5798x self. Gates: strict-RCH release build; workspace check pass; fsci-sparse lib 403 pass; residual differential pass remotely; live-SciPy iterative differential pass locally after RCH worker lacked SciPy; fmt pass; UBS zero critical. Workspace clippy remains blocked by pre-existing fsci-io/fsci-opt warnings; sparse package clippy likewise reports pre-existing lints outside this patch.

title: [perf][sparse] sorted-row two-pointer merge for the splu elimination — replace the per-update hash probe (predicted 1.7-2.0x on instructions/update)
description:
Split off frankenscipy-llywn 2026-08-16 (PeachSummit) with a counted target, a design worked out
against the existing invariants, and a prediction that can be checked BEFORE anything is timed.

## Why this and not something else

Counted with callgrind on the cubic cell (docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md, 2026-08-16), at fill parity
with live SuperLU factoring the same matrix under the same RCM ordering:

    side=10  ours 50.30 instructions per elimination update   SuperLU 15.11   3.33x
    side=12  ours 48.96                                        SuperLU 13.45   3.64x

Flat to 2.7% across a 3.5x change in update count, so it is a per-entry constant. Our LL miss rate
is 0.0% at both sizes, so the kernel is CACHE-RESIDENT: this is instructions, not locality. Roughly
28 of those ~49 instructions are the hashbrown probe (the earlier disassembly put the probe at 52.8%
of program instructions and `factorize_csr` is 91% of the program).

## The change

Represent a factor row as a SORTED `Vec<(usize, f64)>` instead of
`HashMap<usize, f64, BuildHasherDefault<SparseIndexHasher>>`, and apply the pivot tail as a
TWO-POINTER MERGE into a reused scratch buffer, swapping the buffers afterwards so nothing
allocates in the loop.

The inner loop today pays a hash probe per update:

```rust
for &(col, pivot_value) in &pivot_tail {
    add_sparse_entry(&mut rows, &mut column_rows, row, col, -multiplier * pivot_value);
}
```

Merged, it costs one index compare, one multiply-subtract and two stores per element of
`|row| + |tail|`, all sequential.

## The invariants that make it work — checked against the current code, not assumed

1. **At pivot `k`, every active row's minimum column is `>= k`.** A row `r > k` holding a column
   `c < k` would have been in `column_rows[c]`, hence in `candidate_rows` at step `c` (compaction
   only drops rows `< c`, and `r > k > c`), hence `rows[r].remove(&c)` already ran. So
   `rows[row].remove(&k)` is a FRONT POP on the sorted vector, not a search.
2. **Fill only ever lands right of the current pivot**, because `pivot_tail` is filtered to
   `col > k`. So a merge never has to insert left of the cursor.
3. **`rows[k]` is already sorted**, so `pivot_tail` needs no `sort_unstable_by_key` — take the
   suffix after `k`. That removes a sort of the pivot row at every step.
4. **`u_rows` extraction is already sorted**, so its per-row `sort_unstable_by_key` goes too.
5. Only `column_rows` consumes membership, and only to build `candidate_rows`. The merge knows
   exactly which columns are NEW, so it pushes membership for those and removes on exact
   cancellation, as today.

## Bit-identity, and how to prove it rather than argue it

Each `(row, col)` receives exactly ONE addition per pivot step in both designs, and cancellation to
exact zero removes the entry in both. So the factors are bit-identical.

Prove it in-build, not against a stored golden: KEEP the current hash implementation as
`#[cfg(test)] factorize_csr_with_hasher` and add `factorize_csr_sorted` as production, then assert
`row_perm`, `fill_perm`, `l_rows` and `u_rows` equal exactly on fixtures that generate fill. The
generic-over-the-hasher scaffolding needed for that already exists (landed in 7b09da29f), and
`sparse_factor_rows_are_bit_identical_under_the_previous_hasher` is the pattern to copy. Include a
negative arm, or the test can pass comparing a routine to itself.

## Prediction, recorded before measuring

~49 -> ~25-30 instructions per update, i.e. **1.7-2.0x**. It does NOT reach the ~15 target: the
merge processes `|row| + |tail|` elements where the hash path processes `|tail|`, so it trades a
28-instruction probe for roughly two 5-instruction merge steps. If the measurement comes back above
~35, the merge overhead is larger than modelled -- most likely `|row| >> |tail|` late in the
factorization -- and that is the thing to report, not to tune around.

## Verify this way, and in this order

    python3 scripts/splu_update_count.py --sides 10 12          # denominator
    valgrind --tool=callgrind --cache-sim=yes \
      --callgrind-out-file=cg.out ./target/release/perf_splu <side> 9 0 off cubic
    callgrind_annotate cg.out | grep factorize                  # numerator
    # divisor = cubic_spectral_toggle_reads printed by the harness; READ it, do not assume it

Only time it if instructions/update actually moved. A 3% wall difference is undecidable on this box
-- identical source built on two rch workers reads this cell 3.4% apart -- so a timed A/B on a
sub-5% lever will produce a number that means nothing.

## What this does NOT do, stated so the result is not oversold

Instructions per update account for only 3.3-3.6x of the banked 13.0-13.5x deficit. The residual
~3.6-4.1x is efficiency per instruction: SuperLU's `dpanel_bmod` is a dense BLAS-shaped kernel over
supernodal panels with sequential operands. Even a perfect version of this bead leaves that factor
untouched. Supernodal blocking (frankenscipy-9nw95) is the only lever that attacks both.
close_reason: Landed e9c38f771, measured and banked 4d224cb74. Sorted factor rows plus a two-pointer merge replace the per-update hash probe. Bit-identical, pinned in-build against the retained hash-backed reference (492 passed, 0 failed under rch exec). Cubic cell goes 0.0769x -> 0.155-0.157x, at least 1.90x by worst bound, replicated on two ELFs built on two workers with different C toolchains, 1.1% apart with overlapping CIs. Deficit against live SuperLU halves from 13.0x to 6.4x. THE PREDICTION FAILED ON MECHANISM: predicted 1.7-2.0x on instructions per update, delivered 1.145x (48.96->42.74, replicated at both sizes) which is above the failure criterion the bead itself set; the wall gain came from the D1 miss rate halving 3.9%->2.0%, i.e. L1-miss latency, not instruction count. Classified SELF-SPEEDUP -- maintenance, not a win -- and it is still a LOSS against the incumbent.

title: [perf][sparse] eigsh/eigs/svds Arnoldi op closure allocs A.v Vec per step; thread csr/csc_matvec_into through krylov_arnoldi_eigs
description: LEVER: krylov_arnoldi_eigs(op: Fn(&[f64])->Vec<f64>) calls op(&v[j]) every Arnoldi step (line 9102), each allocating a fresh A.v (or A^T A.v) Vec. eigsh/eigs pass |v| csr_matvec(a,v); svds passes the nested |v| csc_matvec(&a_csc, &csr_matvec(a,v)) which allocates TWICE. PLAN (byte-identical): change the helper bound to F: Fn(&[f64], &mut [f64]), hoist a w buffer in the helper, call op(&v[j], &mut w). Callers: eigsh/eigs -> |v,out| csr_matvec_into(a,v,out) (csr_matvec_into already exists, frankenscipy-2hclc); svds -> add a csc_matvec_into mirror + a captured tmp buffer: |v,out| { csr_matvec_into(a,v,&mut tmp); csc_matvec_into(&a_csc,&tmp,out) }. w is consumed into a normalized copy pushed to the basis (same as gmres), so reuse is safe. title: [parity-gap] complex erf small-Re large-Im wrong: series gate routes large |Im| to truncating Maclaurin series
description: erf_complex_scalar and erfc_complex_scalar gated the 80-term Maclaurin series on (z.abs()<=4.0 OR z.re<1.0). The z.re<1.0 clause routed every small-real-part argument to the series regardless of |Im|, but for large imaginary part the series peaks past term 80 (peak n ~ |z|^2) and cancels (max term ~e^{|z|^2}): erf(0.1+10i) was 97% off, erf(0.5-20i) ~100% off, erf(0.1+30i) gave a finite wrong value where scipy overflows to inf. Fix: gate the series on |z|<=4 only; for |z|>4 use the Faddeeva relation erfc(z)=e^{-z^2} w(iz) (wofz), which is accurate across the whole upper half plane (iz has Im=Re(z)>=0 after the Re<0 reflection) and has no asymptotic-floor gap near |z|~4 that the old erfc_complex_asymptotic left. Verified 0 mismatches vs scipy 1.17.1 over a (Re,Im) grid (wofz itself was already clean). scipy.special.erf supports complex, so this IS a scipy-parity gap.
close_reason: Fixed in 621ee257: gate complex erf/erfc series on |z|<=4; |z|>4 uses Faddeeva relation erfc(z)=e^{-z^2}w(iz). erf(0.1+10i) 97% off -> 0 mismatches vs scipy 1.17.1 over (Re,Im) grid.

title: [stats] Chi-squared contingency test and power_divergence
description:
## Goal
Implement chi-squared tests for contingency tables — among the most used statistical tests.

## What to implement
- `chi2_contingency(observed)`: Chi-squared test of independence for a contingency table. Returns (chi2, p, dof, expected).
- `power_divergence(f_obs, f_exp, lambda_)`: Power divergence statistic. Lambda=1 gives Pearson chi-squared, lambda=0 gives G-test (log-likelihood ratio).
- `chi2(df)` distribution (already have Chi2 distribution, use its sf for p-values)

## Implementation approach
- Expected frequencies: e_ij = (row_i_total * col_j_total) / grand_total
- Chi2 statistic: Σ (o_ij - e_ij)² / e_ij
- Degrees of freedom: (nrows - 1) * (ncols - 1)
- P-value: 1 - chi2.cdf(statistic, dof)

## Testing requirements
- 2x2 table with known result
- Uniform table → large p-value
- Independent rows → non-significant
- At least 6 tests
close_reason: Implemented chi2_contingency (5 tests) and power_divergence with Pearson/G-test/general lambda (4 tests). All 9 tests passing.

title: [sparse] Sparse eigenvalues: eigs (Arnoldi) + svds (sparse SVD)
description:
## Goal
Implement Arnoldi-based eigenvalue solver (eigs) for non-symmetric matrices and sparse SVD (svds). Currently we only have eigsh (symmetric, power iteration).

## What to implement
- `eigs(A, k)`: find k eigenvalues/eigenvectors of a sparse matrix using implicitly restarted Arnoldi method. Supports which="LM" (largest magnitude), "SM" (smallest), "LR" (largest real), etc.
- `svds(A, k)`: find k largest singular values/vectors of a sparse matrix. Uses Arnoldi on A^T A or augmented matrix.

## Why this matters
eigs is fundamental for spectral graph analysis (PageRank, spectral clustering, community detection), dynamic mode decomposition, and stability analysis. svds is used for dimensionality reduction (truncated SVD/PCA on sparse data).

## Implementation approach
- Arnoldi iteration: build orthonormal Krylov basis V_m and upper Hessenberg matrix H_m such that A V_m ≈ V_m H_m. Eigenvalues of H_m approximate eigenvalues of A.
- Implicit restart: deflate converged Ritz values using shifted QR steps on H_m (ARPACK-style).
- svds: apply eigs to A^T A or use augmented matrix [0 A; A^T 0].

## Testing requirements
- eigs: known eigenvalues of tridiagonal matrix, verify largest k eigenvalues match
- eigs which="SM": find smallest eigenvalues (requires shift-invert, or use inverse iteration)
- svds: compare k largest singular values against dense SVD for small test case
- Large sparse: 1000×1000 sparse matrix with known spectrum
- At least 6 tests
close_reason: Implemented eigs (Arnoldi-based, 3 tests) and svds (power iteration on A^T A, 4 tests). All 7 tests passing. Also includes Hessenberg QR eigenvalue extraction.

title: [capability][linalg] dense eigh has no subset_by_index -- the O(n^3) back-transform is paid in full for k eigenpairs
description:
Landed 2026-08-16 (RainyPrairie), completing the subset-selection work begun in 0y08i (index) and yumtz (value) on the tridiagonal entry point.

THE GAP: scipy.linalg.eigh takes subset_by_index; fsci-linalg had no dense equivalent, so a caller wanting ten eigenpairs of a 1000x1000 matrix paid for all thousand.

WHY THIS IS THE LARGER PRIZE. eigh_tridiagonal_subset already skips the eigenvector work for unwanted eigenvalues of T, but the DENSE path then back-transforms by Q, and that back-transform is the O(n^3) stage that dominates the eigh deficit against LAPACK dsyevd. Restricting it to k columns makes it O(n^2 k). This is work REMOVED, not rescheduled -- unlike the blocked dsytrd reduction (measured 0.5-0.81x, slower) or any of the scheduling levers tried against this ratio.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTE THAT MATTERS FOR TRUST: the Householder reduction was extracted VERBATIM out of symmetric_eigh_native into symmetric_tridiagonalize_native and both paths now call it. Sharing one reduction rather than maintaining two is what makes the subset path bit-identical to the full path at the reduction stage by construction. That refactor touches a hot path, so the whole fsci-linalg suite was re-run: 546 passed, 0 failed, 42 ignored on rch worker vmi1149989.

Small matrices (n < 3) take a solve-and-slice path, which also covers the 0x0 and 1x1 cases the reduction cannot handle (n-2 and n-1 would underflow).

TESTS: dense residual A*v = lambda*v on the ORIGINAL matrix -- the check that actually proves the back-transform was applied to the restricted block rather than a full one; orthonormality of the returned block; eigenvalues agreeing with the full dense solve to tolerance; eigvals_only skipping the back-transform; a full-range call through the subset entry point reproducing the whole spectrum (must-miss: the restriction is what changes the answer, not the code path); the 2x2 slice path; and refusal of invalid ranges and non-square input.

DELIBERATELY NOT BIT-IDENTITY on the eigenvalues: the full path reaches its spectrum through symmetric_eigh_native own eigensolve and the subset path through eigh_tridiagonal. Those are different routes, the same split already filed for eigvals_only, so pinning bits there would pin a coincidence.

NOT DONE: subset_by_value on the dense entry point (the tridiagonal value form exists and could be layered the same way).
close_reason: Landed in this commit: eigh_subset with scipy subset_by_index semantics, back-transforming only the k selected columns (O(n^2 k) instead of O(n^3)), backed by a reduction extracted verbatim and shared with the full solve. 546/0/42 on vmi1149989.
