title: [signal] spectrogram, STFT, ISTFT, CSD, coherence
description:
## Goal
Implement time-frequency analysis functions. These extend the existing periodogram/welch by providing time-varying spectral estimates — critical for analyzing non-stationary signals.

## What to implement
- `spectrogram(x, fs, window, nperseg, noverlap)`: compute spectrogram (time-frequency representation). Returns (frequencies, times, Sxx) where Sxx[f,t] is the PSD at each time-frequency bin.
- `stft(x, fs, window, nperseg, noverlap)`: Short-Time Fourier Transform. Returns complex STFT matrix.
- `istft(Zxx, fs, window, nperseg, noverlap)`: inverse STFT (signal reconstruction from STFT).
- `csd(x, y, fs, nperseg)`: Cross-spectral density (extension of welch to two signals).
- `coherence(x, y, fs, nperseg)`: magnitude-squared coherence between two signals.

## Why this matters
spectrogram is one of the most-used scipy.signal functions — essential for speech processing, vibration analysis, EEG/ECG analysis, music information retrieval, and radar signal processing.

## Implementation approach
- spectrogram: segment signal, apply window, compute rfft per segment, collect into 2D array
- stft: same as spectrogram but return complex FFT output
- istft: overlap-add reconstruction from STFT segments
- csd: Welch-style averaging of cross-periodograms Pxy = conj(X)*Y
- coherence: |Pxy|² / (Pxx * Pyy)

## Dependencies
- Builds directly on existing welch/periodogram infrastructure
- Uses existing rfft from fsci-fft
- Uses existing window functions

## Testing requirements
- spectrogram of chirp signal: energy should track the instantaneous frequency
- stft → istft roundtrip: reconstructed signal matches original within tolerance
- csd: auto-spectrum (csd(x,x)) should match welch output
- coherence: identical signals → coherence ≈ 1 everywhere
- coherence: uncorrelated signals → coherence ≈ 0
- At least 8 tests
close_reason: Implemented stft, istft, spectrogram, csd, coherence with 8 tests, all passing

title: [sparse] Clear fsci-sparse workspace clippy failures in linalg

title: fsci-stats: bayes_mvs variance/std .statistic uses (n-1) instead of (n-3)
description:
fsci bayes_mvs at lib.rs:15321 sets s2 = var_biased * n / (n-1) = ss/(n-1) (the unbiased sample variance) and uses this as the 'point estimate'. scipy.stats.bayes_mvs uses the Jeffrey's-prior posterior mean of variance, which is ss/(n-3).

REPLICATION (data=[1..10] alpha=0.95):
  scipy var.statistic = 11.7857 (= ss/7)
  fsci  var.statistic =  9.1667 (= ss/9)
  diff = 2.619

The CI bounds (low, high) on var/std MATCH scipy because they use the chi-squared scaling df*s²/chi²_q which cancels the s² choice. Only the .statistic field is wrong.

Likewise std.statistic which is sqrt(s2) - off by sqrt((n-1)/(n-3)).

FIX: at lib.rs:15321 change
  let s2 = var_biased * nf / df;   // ss/(n-1)
to
  let s2 = var_biased * nf / (df - 2.0);   // ss/(n-3)

Existing fsci tests on bayes_mvs are loose checks of low<stat<high which will continue to pass with the fix because the CI bounds bracket the (n-3) point estimate too.
close_reason: Fixed both .statistic fields to match scipy: variance.statistic now = ss/(n-3) (Jeffreys posterior mean), std.statistic now = sqrt(ss/2)·Γ((n-2)/2)/Γ((n-1)/2) (Generalized-Gamma posterior mean). CI bounds unchanged via refactor that uses ss/χ² directly. Anchor test bayes_mvs_matches_scipy_jeffreys_posterior added.

title: [perf][sparse] arena-backed splu factor rows — the 56-byte per-row header is 47.5% of D1 read misses and ordering will not fix it
description:
Split off frankenscipy-9nw95 2026-08-16 (PeachSummit) after the cheap alternative was measured and refuted.
This is scoped as a rewrite, not a tweak, because the measurement says the cheap version cannot work.

## The measured problem

Per-instruction D1 read-miss attribution (callgrind `--dump-instr`, mapped through objdump) on the
splu elimination, `laplacian_3d_cubic`:

```
0x5defc  47.5% of all D1 read misses   imul $0x38 / mov 0x30(%rax,%rcx,1)
                                       indexing the 56-byte SortedFactorRow struct at a
                                       candidate row index; misses on 47% of 2.13M executions
0x5e8bb  35.6%                         vmovupd in the run kernel -- streaming fill data,
                                       compulsory, fixed only by blocking/reuse
```

`SortedFactorRow` is `{ cols: Vec<u32>, vals: Vec<f64>, start: usize }` = 56 bytes, so barely one
header per cache line. The elimination touches them at candidate row indices, so **every candidate
row costs two cold lines: one for the header, one for its data.** SuperLU keeps its factors in flat
arrays with an index and pays one. Our D1 read-miss rate is 7.2% against its 3.4% on the same
ordering.

## Why the cheap version is already ruled out

Sorting the candidate prefix to make the header walk monotone was tried: read-miss rate went
**7.2% -> 7.5%**, i.e. slightly worse. Reverted. The walk was already as prefetch-friendly as it
gets, so the miss is the *layout*, not the *order*. Do not re-try candidate ordering in any form —
the measurement covers the mechanism, not one implementation of it.

## The change

One arena per factorization instead of `n` independently allocated rows:

```rust
cols: Vec<u32>          // all rows' columns, contiguous
vals: Vec<f64>          // all rows' values, contiguous
row_start: Vec<u32>     // offset of each row into the arena
row_len:   Vec<u32>     // live length of each row
```

A row touch then reads `row_start[r]` and `row_len[r]` from two dense arrays that are themselves
sequentially walked, and the data from one arena region. The 56-byte header disappears.

## The hard part, which is why this is a rewrite

Rows GROW when fill is created, and an arena has no room to grow a row in place. Options, in the
order they should be tried:

1. **Two-pass symbolic first.** Compute the fill pattern symbolically, size every row exactly, then
   run the numeric pass into an arena that never grows. This is what SuperLU does and it is the
   honest version. It also makes the numeric pass allocation-free, which is worth something on its
   own.
2. **Append-and-compact.** Grow by appending the new row image at the arena tail and updating
   `row_start[r]`, compacting when waste exceeds a threshold. Simpler, but fragmentation and the
   compaction pass need measuring, and the compaction itself will move bytes.

Option 1 is more work and strictly better; option 2 is a way to test the layout hypothesis before
committing to a symbolic pass.

## Predict before measuring, then check the prediction

The header line disappears entirely, so **D1 read-miss rate should fall toward the incumbent's
3.4%**, and the share at the equivalent of `0x5defc` should go to zero rather than merely shrink.
If read misses do not fall after the header is gone, the attribution was wrong and the remaining
read misses are the streaming loads at `0x5e8bb`, which no layout change fixes — only reuse does,
and that is the supernodal question on the parent bead.

## Verify this way

Measure per-instruction D1mr, not the aggregate. Parse detail that silently yields zeros otherwise:
with `positions: instr line`, the first TWO fields of a callgrind cost line are positions, so `D1mr`
is the fifth EVENT, not the fifth field.

Bit-identity is testable throughout: `sorted_rows_are_bit_identical_to_the_hashed_reference` runs
the retained hash-backed elimination and the shipping one in the same binary and compares
`row_perm`, `fill_perm`, L and U exactly. An arena rewrite must keep passing it unchanged.

## Do not start this under a disk freeze

It needs several build-and-measure cycles to be worth anything. `/data` hit its 58G floor on
2026-08-16; the freeze lifts above 70G free.
notes:
=== STATE 2026-08-16/17 (PeachSummit): TWO PRECONDITIONS CLEARED, ZERO GAIN MEASURED, ONE
OF THEM RESTING ON AN UNVERIFIED NUMBER. Do not start the rewrite until caveat 3 is run. ===

PROMOTED P2 -> P1 because frankenscipy-9nw95 (supernodal) is CLOSED with a mechanism, so
this is now the only named lever on the worst standing ratio (cubic, at most 1.89x slower
than live SuperLU at rounds=41).

--- PRECONDITION (a): INDEX CONTIGUITY. CLEARED, and exactly. ---

An arena does nothing for a single random touch. It pays only if the rows touched at ONE
pivot are near each other, so that pivot's candidate sweep is near-sequential.

  cubic side=16, Colamd (the SHIPPING ordering)  592,107 candidates / 592,107 span = 1.00
  cubic side=16, natural order                   986,894 candidates / 1,015,679 span = 1.03

Under the ordering the shipping path actually uses, the candidate set at every pivot is a
contiguous run of row indices -- span equals count to the unit. The counter discriminates
(natural reads 1.03; a unit test pins a deliberately scattered set at span 3 over count 2),
so 1.00 is a property and not an artifact.

--- PRECONDITION (b): THE LAYOUT IS GENUINELY LOST, NOT ALREADY FREE. CLEARED, and as of
    2026-08-17 CONFIRMED ON THE REAL ELIMINATION (caveat 3 below is discharged). ---

REAL FIGURES, recorded inside factorize_csr on the live rows, two sizes agreeing:

  cubic side=8   AS BUILT 501/511  = 98.0%   AFTER REAL ELIMINATION  36/511  = 7.0%
  cubic side=16  AS BUILT 3847/4095 = 93.9%  AFTER REAL ELIMINATION 344/4095 = 8.4%

Control: a diagonal fixture generates no fill, so no row is grown or reallocated and the
layout must be unchanged -- asserted as EXACT equality, and it passes. Without that arm a
collapse could have been an artifact of the hook.

Note as-built reads 93.9% in situ against 99.4% measured on rows built in isolation: the
elimination's own setup allocations interleave with the factor rows. 93.9% is the honest
number. The stand-in below was directionally right and quantitatively close.

The obvious way this lever dies is if glibc already hands the rows out adjacent, making the
arena worth the difference between "usually adjacent" and "guaranteed adjacent" -- i.e.
nothing. Measured on cubic side=16 Colamd:

  as built (one Vec per row, allocated in row order)   4071/4095 = 99.4% adjacent
  after ONE growth per row                              214/4095 =  5.2% adjacent

So the first half of that worry is CONFIRMED -- glibc really does deliver the layout -- and
the second half REVERSES the conclusion: the elimination grows every row as fill lands on
it, each growth past capacity relocates it, and one growth apiece already destroys it. The
arena is not competing against a layout glibc supplies; it is competing against one glibc
supplies and then loses.

--- WHICH NAMES THE REQUIREMENT, and it is NOT "allocate contiguously" ---

A naive arena that appended rows in row order and grew them on demand would reproduce
exactly this collapse. The arena holds its layout ONLY if each row is placed at FINAL size
and never moves, which requires a per-row symbolic fill count up front.
`symbolic_fill_pattern` already computes precisely that and is already in-tree, left from
the closed supernodal line -- so the dead phase is this lever's required input and 9nw95 is
not wasted.

--- THREE CAVEATS, THE THIRD IS BLOCKING ---

1. NEITHER PRECONDITION IS A PREDICTED WIN. Two supernodal drivers died holding mechanisms
   that were plausible, fitted the numbers, and were wrong (unbounded padding: measured tax
   1.01x; absent structure: width 5.24, 97.2% dense). Keep the prior disciplined.
2. THE MERGE KERNEL IS ALREADY DENSE INSIDE ITS RUNS (96.8% of elements), which is what
   killed supernodal blocking. The arena attacks a different axis -- where rows SIT, not how
   they are traversed -- but that is an argument, not a measurement.
3. DISCHARGED 2026-08-17, and it came out FOR the bead rather than against it. The kill
   condition was: if the real elimination leaves the rows mostly adjacent, precondition (b)
   is refuted and this bead closes without the rewrite. Built and run -- 93.9% -> 8.4% at
   side=16, 98.0% -> 7.0% at side=8, control passing. NOT refuted. Recorded here because
   the condition was written down BEFORE the answer was known, and would have closed this
   bead had it gone the other way.

--- THE ARENA'S DESIGN IS NOW CONSTRAINED BY MEASUREMENT, not by preference ---

The collapse is caused by GROWTH PAST CAPACITY, not by initial placement -- the as-built
figures (93.9-98.0%) show the allocator already gets placement right. So a naive arena that
appended rows in row order and grew them on demand would reproduce the same 8.4% and buy
NOTHING. It is refuted in advance by this measurement. Each row must be placed at FINAL
size from a per-row symbolic fill count (symbolic_fill_pattern, already in-tree) and never
move. After building it, re-measure with the SAME hook: it must read near 100% after
elimination, or the arena is not doing what it was built to do.

--- CLOSING EVIDENCE ---

The arena must be measured against the standing floor, not assumed. The shipping cubic
deficit is at most 1.89x (worst CI floor 0.5291, 4/4 admissible, rounds=41); any arena that
does not move that number materially is a loss, and the scattered family must not regress
below its standing 1.2106x floor.
close_reason: REFUSED ON A COUNTED BOUND, before the rewrite. Three rows into this bead every precondition had been cleared -- candidate sweeps contiguous in row index (1.00 slots/needed row), the layout genuinely destroyed by growth (93.9% -> 8.4%), and one design already refuted (reserve-in-order freezes a SCATTERED layout, 98.0% -> 6.8% at the reserve itself). All of that assumed adjacency would HELP if achieved, and never asked how much. Measured: a row visit on the cubic cell spans 32.0 cache lines and only 0.7% of visits are single-line. Adjacency can only remove the miss at the BOUNDARY between two rows -- at most one line per stream per visit -- so its ceiling is 6.3% of the row-stream misses, and the row-stream is 53.91% of D1 read misses, giving <= 3.4% of total read misses for a whole-factor storage rewrite. The ceiling FALLS with size (21.7% at side=8 -> 6.3% at side=16) because rows fatten, so it is worth least exactly where the deficit lives. Prefetch does not rescue it: the sweep inside a row is already sequential over 32 lines, so adjacency extends the prefetcher's reach by ~1 line in 32. Counter has two arms -- tridiagonal reads exactly 1 line/stream/visit (asserted as equality), cubic reads 32.0 -- so neither 'always many' nor 'always one' passes. DO NOT RE-OPEN ON A LOCALITY ARGUMENT. Re-open only if the row-stream miss share is measured above 53.91%, or lines-per-visit below ~4 on a cell that matters; arena_ceiling_from_row_visit_spans prints both. A layout that reduces the NUMBER of lines a visit spans attacks the compulsory part and is a different lever needing its own pre-costing. Full evidence in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md, row 'THE ARENA IS DEAD BEFORE IT IS WRITTEN' 2026-08-17.

title: [lint][opt] clippy-clean was claimed from --lib/--all-targets, which never compiles the feature-gated incumbent bins
description:
Reopened in substance by PeachSummit 2026-08-16 and fixed the same day in 183819db6; filed as a new bead rather than reopening eqw8v because the CLOSE WAS CORRECT for what it checked and the lesson is about the check, not the closer.

eqw8v was closed on 'cargo clippy -p fsci-opt --lib' and '--all-targets' both exiting 0. Neither compiles a bin behind a non-default feature, so the feature-gated incumbent harnesses were never linted by that evidence. Running the gate the harnesses actually need --

  cargo clippy -j 2 -p fsci-opt --features opt-incumbent-bench --bins -- -D warnings

-- failed with 10 errors: 4 in perf_root_many_scipy and 6 in perf_curve_fit_many_scipy (chunks_exact with a const size x6, needless_range_loop x3, iter().copied().collect() on an owned Vec x1). Because clippy stops the package build, this blocked the gate for EVERY bin in the crate, including perf_minimize_many_scipy and perf_newton_many_scipy, whose conversion beads (llznz, 9nzg9, dw6du, 5e4xq) are open.

FIXED in 183819db6, verified clean on RCH_WORKER=hz2. Behaviour preservation was checked, not assumed: both rewritten range loops ran 0..BATCH over collections already refused unless BATCH-long, and the inner curve-fit loop ran 0..POINTS over rows exactly POINTS long by construction.

THE TRANSFERABLE LESSON, which is why this bead exists at all: --all-targets does NOT imply --features, so a clippy-clean claim taken without the harness's own feature flags is vacuously true for exactly the targets the campaign gates on. Any future 'clippy backlog cleared' close in this repo should cite the feature-gated bin invocation, not --lib or --all-targets.

title: [parity-gap] struve(v, 0) returns 0 for v leq -1 where scipy returns nonzero
description:
fsci struve at crates/fsci-special/src/convenience.rs:969 short-circuits 'if x == 0.0 return 0.0' for ALL v. The series leading term is (x/2)^(v+1) / (Gamma(3/2) Gamma(v+3/2)). At x=0:
  - v > -1: (x/2)^(v+1) -> 0, so H_v(0) = 0 (correct).
  - v = -1: (x/2)^0 = 1, so H_{-1}(0) = 1/(Gamma(3/2) Gamma(1/2)) = 2/pi.
  - v < -1: (x/2)^(v+1) -> infty.
scipy.special.struve(-1.0, 0.0) returns 2/pi (~0.6366). fsci returns 0.0.

Fix: make the x=0 branch v-aware. Return 0 when v > -1, return 2/pi when v == -1, return signed infinity when v < -1.

Acceptance: struve(-1.0, 0.0) within 1e-12 of 2/pi; struve(0.0, 0.0) still 0; struve(1.5, 0.0) still 0. Add a focused regression test for v=-1 and v=0.

title: Halve streamed CG column-index width
description: Change: materialize u32 CSR column indices once per large persistent CG solve and stream those indices in every SpMV iteration, preserving row order and f64 arithmetic. Budget: one O(nnz) conversion and 4 bytes per nonzero; fallback immediately for dimensions beyond u32. Expected loss: keep only if per-iteration bandwidth savings amortize conversion and exact solution parity holds. Calibration: same-ELF environment switch disables narrowing; live SciPy remains in each timed invocation. Isomorphism: identical indices, order, products, and sums, so solution bits should match classic-wide. Target: at least 1.10x over classic-wide and a decided live-SciPy win. title: [feature][sparse] sparse_norm ord=2 (spectral norm) is unimplemented and rejected; scipy computes it
description:
Split from frankenscipy-93plj, which fixed the defect and shipped the signature but deliberately left ord=2 REJECTED rather than approximated -- returning an easier norm for it would have been the original silent-wrong-answer defect wearing a different number.

MEASURED, live scipy 1.17.1 / numpy 2.4.3: on A = [[1,-2,0],[0,3,-4],[5,0,0]], scipy.sparse.linalg.norm(A, 2) = 5.261993684950, which equals numpy.linalg.svd(A)[0] to 12 decimals (full spectrum: 5.26199368, 5.0, 1.5203363). On diag(3,-4) it is 4.0. scipy computes it via svds, i.e. the largest singular value.

fsci-sparse already has svds(a, k, EigsOptions) -> SvdsResult{singular_values (largest first), u, vt}, so this is wiring plus a decision about small/degenerate inputs.

NEGATIVE CASES a fix must pass, and the reason this is not a one-liner:
1. svds is ITERATIVE. A 3x3 is a degenerate case for it, so the implementation must agree with a dense SVD to tight tolerance on small matrices -- pin against 5.261993684950 and 4.0 above, not against svds' own output.
2. A rectangular matrix must work (the spectral norm is defined for any shape) and must equal the largest singular value of the same matrix densified.
3. The all-zero matrix must give 0.0, matching every other ord, without svds being asked for a singular value of a zero operator.
4. A 1x1 matrix [[-7]] must give 7.0.
5. If svds cannot converge, the function must return Err rather than a fallback norm -- the whole point of 93plj was that a plausible substitute is worse than a refusal.

Until this lands, ord=2 correctly returns Err(InvalidArgument), which is pinned by sparse_norm_matches_scipy_including_the_minimum_norms.
close_reason: Landed in fc9b5d6b8. Harness 'rch exec -- cargo test -j 1 -p fsci-sparse --lib': 484 passed, 0 failed, 4 ignored on RCH_WORKER=hz2; clippy clean on hz2; ubs 0 critical. Cited probe: sparse_norm_spectral_matches_the_largest_singular_value. All five negative cases from this bead are covered: (1) pinned to a DENSE SVD (5.261993684950) rather than to svds' own output, since a test asserting an iterative solver reproduces itself proves nothing; (2) rectangular 3x2 gives sqrt(3), the norm being defined for any shape; (3) the all-zero matrix returns 0.0 via a short-circuit BEFORE svds is consulted, so no iterative solver is asked for the singular value of a zero operator; (4) 1x1 [[-7]] gives 7.0; (5) an svds failure propagates Err rather than falling back to a computable norm. Also verified diag(3,-4) = 4.0, since singular values are magnitudes. sparse_norm now covers every ord scipy.sparse.linalg.norm supports for matrices -- fro, 1, -1, inf, -inf, 2 -- and rejects everything else with InvalidArgument, so the three-bead arc lqbg3 -> 93plj -> ukq0n is complete.

title: [opt] trust-exact is model-limited on a scaled objective: the initial Hessian is unscaled, so progress stalls below ~2^-46 even with the tolerance honoured
description:
Filed 2026-08-15 (PeachSummit), split out of frankenscipy-ei0az so that bead could close on what it actually fixed.

ei0az removed the '.max(1.0e-12)' clamp that silently overrode a caller's tolerance, and converted the three now-reachable f64::EPSILON step guards to exact zero. Measured effect on f(x) = s.((x0-1)^2 + 2(x1+2)^2) from (0,0), tol = 1e-30, maxiter 200, RCH_WORKER=vmi1227854:

  2^-k    before ei0az                 after ei0az
  2^-20   success, 3.155e-9 away       converges
  2^-40   SUCCESS, 4.886e-1 away       converges (< 1e-6)
  2^-53   SUCCESS, 2.236e0 (at x0!)    success=false, 2.056e0 after 200 iterations
  2^-60   SUCCESS, 2.236e0 (at x0!)    success=false, iterates

So the false 'success at the starting point' is gone at every scale and convergence is restored through 2^-40. What remains below that is a DIFFERENT limit and is this bead: the routine iterates but barely moves (2.236 -> 2.056 over 200 iterations).

DIAGNOSIS (stated as a hypothesis, not a measurement -- test it before fixing): trust_exact builds its own Hessian model, and the model appears to start unscaled while the true curvature of a 2^-53-scaled objective is order 2^-53. The first trust-region steps are then sized by a model that is ~16 orders too stiff, so each step is minuscule and BFGS needs many iterations to correct the model. The scale-sensitive constants ruled OUT already: trust_bfgs_hessian_update's curvature test is relative ('y_s <= 1.0e-10 * y_norm * s_norm') and its other guard is exact ('s_bs <= 0.0'), so the update itself is not the blocker. Still unexamined: the initial Hessian construction, the initial trust radius, and 'delta = (0.25 * delta).max(1.0e-8)' plus the 'delta <= 1.0e-8' PrecisionLoss exit, both absolute in x-space.

HARNESS WARNING, learned the hard way in ei0az: do NOT compare this against scipy.optimize.minimize(method='trust-exact') handed an ANALYTIC hess -- that arm reaches 2.220e-16 at every scale in 2 iterations, but it is being given what ours has to derive, so the comparison is not like-for-like. scipy's trust-exact rejects hess='2-point' (ValueError), so a matched finite-difference arm needs a different construction -- e.g. compare against scipy's own BFGS/Newton-CG, or supply scipy a numerically-derived Hessian explicitly. Establish a fair arm BEFORE claiming a gap.

NEGATIVE CASES a fix must pass: a well-scaled problem's iterate must not move (the existing trust_exact_* tests); an objective already at its minimizer must still converge at nit=0; and the fix must be shown to help at 2^-53 rather than merely raising maxiter.
notes:
DONE 2026-08-15 (PeachSummit). The gap was real, it was ours, and it is closed.

FAIR ARM FIRST (committed earlier in 560095693): given a finite-difference gradient AND Hessian -- the curvature ours derives -- scipy.optimize.minimize(method='trust-exact', gtol=0) reaches the minimizer EXACTLY in 5 iterations at every scale from 2^-0 to 2^-60. So 'model-limited' was never a ceiling.

FOUR CONSTANTS, all describing the problem's SCALE rather than its geometry:
1. Initial model B0 = ||g||/delta on the diagonal instead of the identity. B carries f/x^2, ||g|| carries f/x, delta carries x, so this is the dimensionally right diagonal and it makes the first Newton step come out with length delta rather than length ||g||.
2. First-update rescale B0 <- (y'y / y's).I (Nocedal & Wright 6.1, eq 6.20).
3. solve_trust_spd_system's Cholesky positivity floor '1.0e-12' made relative to the model's largest diagonal (the L-entry floor scaled as sqrt, so a well-scaled model sits on exactly the old threshold). For a 2^-53 model whose curvature is 1e-16 this floor rejected EVERY pivot, sending every subproblem to the pivoted fallback.
4. trust_region_exact_step's lambda search start '1.0e-6' anchored to the model's largest diagonal. lambda is ADDED to the Hessian diagonal, so it carries the Hessian's units; against a 1e-16 model the first trial shift was ten orders larger than the entire matrix.

Items 1-2 alone were NOT enough -- they fixed 2^-40 (53 -> 22 iterations) and left 2^-53 exactly where it was. Items 3-4 are what closed it, and they were found by reading the subproblem solver after 1-2 measurably failed to help. Worth recording: the first hypothesis was right about the diagnosis and wrong about the blocker.

MEASURED, harness 'cargo test -p fsci-opt --lib' via rch:
  before (vmi1227854): 2^-0 22 iters exact | 2^-40 53 iters exact | 2^-53 2.056 away after 200, 0.394 after 5000
  after  (vmi1152480): every scale 2^-0 through 2^-46 converges exact in 22 iterations; 2^-53 in 9; 2^-60 in 8 at 5.78e-15

PROBE: trust_exact_reaches_the_minimizer_at_every_scale_the_incumbent_does -- six scales, asserting arrival (< 1e-9) AND an iteration bound (<= 40), since the failure mode was slow convergence rather than a wrong answer.

TWO TEST-DESIGN TRAPS HIT AND FIXED, both worth knowing:
- tol must be far below anything the problem can satisfy (1e-30). 'grad_norm <= tol' is ABSOLUTE, so at 2^-40 the starting gradient is already 6.1e-12 and an ordinary tol of 1e-10 is satisfied at iteration ZERO -- correctly, and scipy's default gtol does the same. A test with a realistic tolerance is vacuous here.
- MinimizeOptions must set method: Some(OptimizeMethod::TrustExact). Omitting it silently routes through CASP selection to a different method, which is what produced a 'failure at 2^-20' that no probe could reproduce and that changed scale between runs.

Gates: fsci-opt --lib 340 passed / 0 failed (vmi1153651); clippy -p fsci-opt --lib --tests -D warnings CLEAN (hz2); fmt clean; ubs exit 0 (its 1 critical is the pre-existing deliberate panic! in the poison-recovery test at :4328, outside every edited range).
close_reason: Four scale-describing constants in trust-exact made relative: initial model ||g||/delta, first-update gamma rescale, the subproblem Cholesky floor, and the lambda search start. Fair arm (scipy with FD gradient+Hessian) reaches the minimizer in 5 iterations at every scale, so the gap was ours; now every scale 2^-0..2^-46 converges exact in 22 iterations, 2^-53 in 9, 2^-60 in 8. Probe trust_exact_reaches_the_minimizer_at_every_scale_the_incumbent_does; 340 passed / 0 failed (vmi1153651).

title: [conformance][linalg] eig is 4e-3 to 8e-3 from SciPy on two diag-dominant fixtures, in BOTH Schur routines
close_reason:
NOT A DEFECT. Closing the bead I filed yesterday, and withdrawing the root cause I asserted for it.

MEASURED, same_host: thinkstation1, loadavg [15.24 28.92 31.45], CPU idle 83 pct, iowait 0 pct, incumbent scipy 1.17.1 in the same invocation.

Both arms recover the conjugate pair EXACTLY -- |Im| = 0.041231056256 for n=5 seed=766 and 0.104537074763 for n=8 seed=777, matching scipy to twelve decimals. Nothing is lost by either routine. My previous comment claimed one arm was losing or misplacing the pair; that is refuted.

THE 4e-3 WAS MY COMPARISON, NOT THE CODE. I paired eigenvalue k of one arm against eigenvalue k of the other after sorting. These spectra have ALL REAL PARTS IDENTICAL to ~1e-14 (10.5 five times, 16.5 eight times) plus one small conjugate pair, so the sort orders them by pure rounding noise and the pair lands at a different index in each arm. A real eigenvalue then gets compared against a complex one, and the reported difference is the imaginary part magnitude -- 0.0412 against |lambda| 10.5 = 3.9e-3, exactly the number I filed.

Under optimal (nearest-neighbour) matching the same data gives:
  n=5 seed=766: nalgebra 3.042e-15, francis 1.380e-14
  n=8 seed=777: nalgebra 2.670e-15, francis 1.914e-14
Machine precision, both arms, both fixtures.

CONDITIONING WAS ALSO RULED OUT along the way and that part stands: gaps 1.066e-14 and 8.882e-16 with eigenvalue condition numbers 17.7 and 9.9, predicting ~1e-15. The advice on this bead to check conditioning first was right, and it correctly came back negative -- it just was not the whole answer, because the remaining explanation was in my harness rather than in either arm.

FIXED SO IT CANNOT RECUR: perf_francis_vs_nalgebra now matches each eigenvalue to its nearest counterpart instead of pairing by sort index. Re-running the full 7000-fixture grid with that fix gives disagreed_where_both_converged = 0, down from 6. The convergence result is untouched: 230 recovered, 0 regressed.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE 2026-08-19, no build required. A REAL defect, not a conditioning artifact, and the same family as the sez4r complex-pair flattening.

THE OBSERVATION: make_diag_dominant(n,seed) vs scipy.linalg.eig, sorted, relative to each eigenvalue own magnitude -- n=5 seed=766 gives 7.853e-03 (nalgebra) and 3.927e-03 (francis); n=8 seed=777 gives 6.336e-03 in both arms. Every other fixture of 7000 agrees to 1e-13 or better.

I CHECKED CONDITIONING FIRST, as this bead advised, AND IT DOES NOT EXPLAIN IT:
  n=5 s=766: min eigenvalue gap 1.066e-14, cond(V) 5.019e+01, max eigenvalue condition number 1.766e+01, expected error 3.9e-15
  n=8 s=777: min gap 8.882e-16, cond(V) 2.841e+01, max eig-cond 9.923e+00, expected error 2.2e-15
The eigenvalues are WELL conditioned. Expected perturbation ~1e-15 is twelve orders below the observed 4e-3. Conditioning is ruled out; the advice to check it first was right and it came back negative.

WHAT THE SPECTRA ACTUALLY ARE. scipy returns, for both matrices, eigenvalues whose REAL PARTS ARE ALL IDENTICAL:
  n=5 seed=766: 10.5 five times, with exactly one conjugate pair at +-0.041231056256i
  n=8 seed=777: 16.5 eight times, with exactly one conjugate pair at +-0.104537074763i
Every other eigenvalue is exactly real.

THEREFORE: a deviation of 4e-3 against |lambda| ~ 10.5 is an absolute ~0.04, which IS THE MAGNITUDE OF THE IMAGINARY PART (0.0412). The arms are not accumulating error -- one is LOSING or MISPLACING the conjugate pair, returning it as real or with the wrong imaginary part.

That is the same defect class as the complex-pair flattening fixed on the Francis path: a 2x2 block whose realness test must decide on a spectrum where every real part coincides, so the discriminant is the only signal and it is tiny. This must NOT be closed by widening a tolerance.

NEXT STEP: perf_francis_vs_nalgebra already emits CONTESTED lines carrying BOTH arms full spectra for exactly these cases. Print them and see which eigenvalue the imaginary part lands on. The fixture family -- all real parts equal, one small conjugate pair -- is the cheapest regression test available for the 2x2 classifier.

title: [parity-gap] complex hyp1f1 large |z| catastrophically wrong (Stokes phenomenon near imaginary axis)
description: hyp1f1_complex_parameters always uses the direct Maclaurin series (2000-term cap). For |z| above ~35 the series cancels catastrophically (max term ~e^|z| vs a much smaller result): errors reach 1e69 at z=-99+14i. The two-term A&S 13.5.1 asymptotic (M ~ Gamma(b)[e^z z^(a-b)/Gamma(a) S1 + e^(+-i pi a) z^(-a)/Gamma(b-a) S2]) works to ~1e-9 for |z|>=40 AWAY from the imaginary axis (validated vs mpmath, 675 cases). BUT near arg(z)=+-pi/2 (anti-Stokes lines) the hard branch-sign switch on the subdominant term fails in a wide band even at |z|=80 (rel ~1.8), and the convergent series and the Re(z)<0 Kummer transform also fail there (cancellation ~e^|z|). A correct full-plane fix needs exponentially-improved (Olver) asymptotics with smooth Stokes transition, or contour integration. NOTE: scipy.special.hyp1f1 is REAL-only so this is internal-correctness, not scipy-parity. Real hyp1f1 large-z already handled (ztn7f, 8a4qg, k8kkf).
notes: Fixed in aea5904b via superasymptotic A&S 13.5.1 expansion (optimal smallest-term truncation per block + principal-branch (-z)^{-a} Stokes sign). ~1e-15 across the plane incl. the arg z=±pi/2 band for moderate params; ~1e-6 worst when max|param| nears |z|. RESIDUAL (out of scope, low value): the moderate-|z|/large-|param| corner near the negative real axis (e.g. a=5+2i,b=2-1i at |z|~20-40) is ~1e-2 in both series and asymptotic; needs recurrence-in-a or contour integration, and the standard Kummer integral rep does not apply there (Re(b)>Re(a)>0 fails). scipy.hyp1f1 is real-only so this is internal correctness only.

title: [MEDIUM] conformance: FSCI-P2C-016_constants_core.json is dead — run_differential_test has no 'constants' dispatch arm, fixture uses different schema (fixture_id vs case_id), all 7 cases have mode=null
description:
Review on 2026-04-22:

FSCI-P2C-016_constants_core.json is the only packet fixture with family='constants_core'. It has 7 cases in a schema DIFFERENT from every other FSCI-P2C-* fixture:

    { fixture_id: 'constants_exact_values',
      category: 'fundamental_values',
      operation: 'fundamental_constants',
      description: '...',
      expected_properties: ['speed of light is exact', ...] }

Every other fixture uses {case_id, category, expected, function|operation, args|...}. P2C-016 uses {fixture_id, category, operation, description, expected_properties} with prose-level expectations rather than numeric values.

The run_differential_test dispatch at crates/fsci-conformance/src/lib.rs:7687-7716 has family checks for validate_tol, linalg, array_api, special, fft, optim, casp, cluster, spatial, signal, stats, integrate. 'constants_core' matches NONE -> falls through to the catch-all:

    Err(HarnessError::FixtureParse {
        path, source: ...('unknown fixture family: constants_core')
    })

Mode field is null for all 7 cases (distinct from the Strict/Hardened values everywhere else). If the PacketFamily registry tries to deserialize a ConstantsCase with a missing mode, it errors.

Three possible states:
1. P2C-016 was scaffolded in anticipation of adding fsci_constants conformance but never wired -> dead fixture, schema will need rewrite before use.
2. P2C-016 was intentionally written in the prose-expectations style and was supposed to be consumed by a different (non-differential) runner -> that runner is missing or broken.
3. P2C-016 is the skeleton for a contracts-style metadata packet, not a test fixture -> should live under docs/ or artifacts/, not fixtures/.

Compounded with frankenscipy-di9p (10 families have no scipy oracle): constants is arguably the 11th. There IS a fsci-constants crate with numerical constants; comparing them against scipy.constants would be trivial (scipy.constants has a __dict__ of ~140 named values) but no oracle exists.

Ask:
1. Decide the intent of P2C-016. If obsolete, DELETE the file + remove any residual references.
2. If constants should be conformance-tested, rewrite the fixture in the common {case_id, function, args, expected} shape and add a run_differential_constants entry + scipy_constants_oracle.py that compares each fsci_constants::NAME against scipy.constants.NAME.
3. If P2C-016 is meant to live in docs/contracts, move it out of fixtures/.

Related: di9p (missing oracles), ivg5 (differential entry is self-check -- constants is just more extreme), xo4o (mode coverage), bcv7 (contract_ref dead metadata).
close_reason: Already shipped in commit d4b09f3 (feat(conformance): br-utus — revive FSCI-P2C-016 constants fixture + oracle). FSCI-P2C-016_constants_core.json is in canonical schema (case_id/function/args/expected/mode), run_differential_constants dispatch arm exists, scipy_constants_oracle.py present, differential_test_constants_fixture passes 24/24. title: AUDIT: scipy.linalg.lapack / scipy.linalg.blas low-level routine parity decision
description:
scipy.linalg.lapack and scipy.linalg.blas expose the low-level Fortran LAPACK / BLAS routines as named pythony wrappers (e.g. dgesv, dgemm, dpotrf, zgeev, sger). fsci-linalg is built on nalgebra (pure Rust) and therefore has no Fortran shim; this bead is the explicit AUDIT decision plus a documented contract.

Two outcomes are valid:
1. DECLINE: per fsci-linalg DISCREPANCIES.md (already established), Fortran-binding introspection has no analogue in nalgebra. This bead documents the decline formally per-routine, not just per-trio (find_best_blas_type / get_blas_funcs / get_lapack_funcs).
2. PARTIAL: a curated handful of LAPACK names that map 1:1 to fsci-linalg high-level functions can be exposed as thin wrappers (dgesv -> solve, dgemm -> matmul, dpotrf -> cholesky, zgeev -> eig). This is purely a docstring-and-name layer, not a re-implementation.

Acceptance:
- Audit script crates/fsci-linalg/audit/audit_lapack.py: enumerates scipy.linalg.lapack.__all__ + scipy.linalg.blas.__all__ and prints each.
- DISCREPANCIES.md row per declined routine OR a thin lapack-compat module under fsci-linalg/src/lapack_compat.rs that re-exports the high-level fns under their LAPACK names.
- 5+ fixture cases in FSCI-P2C-002 if option 2 is chosen, asserting the wrapper is bit-identical to the high-level entry point (dgesv -> solve, dpotrf -> cholesky, dgemm -> matmul).

Recommendation: option 2 for the most-requested LAPACK names (dgesv, dgemm, dpotrf, dgetrf, zgeev), option 1 for the rest. Decision belongs to the implementer.

Related: fgxx (parent linalg audit — already declined the introspection trio), o9g3 (qr_updates gap), 0aa1 (matrix-funcs gap).
close_reason: Shipped: LAPACK_MAPPING.md (24/147 LAPACK + 12/46 BLAS curated migration table) + audit/audit_lapack.py (auto-enumerates 480 LAPACK routines + 128 BLAS routines via dir()-grep, parses my mapping doc, prints uncovered) + DISCREPANCIES.md updated to formally decline the full surface and point users at LAPACK_MAPPING.md. fsci-linalg cargo check clean. No Rust code changes (decision: thin wrapper layer offers no value over grep-replace migration).

title: [CRITICAL] conformance: 166/257 (64.6%) of FSCI-P2C-006 fixture cases reference functions NOT in scipy_special_oracle.py func_map — conformance is 35% illusory
description:
Review-mode audit on 2026-04-22 crosswalked the 257-case fixture against the oracle dispatcher:

    fixture: crates/fsci-conformance/fixtures/FSCI-P2C-006_special_core.json (176 distinct functions, 257 cases)
    oracle:  crates/fsci-conformance/python_oracle/scipy_special_oracle.py   (90 dispatchers)

Result: 166 of 257 cases (64.6%) reference functions NOT in the oracle's func_map. The oracle returns status='error' / result_kind='unsupported_function' for all of them. The Rust conformance runner either:
a) Counts those as passing (if it treats 'unsupported' as 'no ground truth, accept Rust output') — effectively SKIPS 64.6% of the declared conformance surface, or
b) Counts them as failing (if it treats 'unsupported' strictly) — which contradicts the 257/257 green status reported in earlier session notes.

Either way, the '100% special parity' claim in the conformance dashboard is WRONG by a factor of ~3.

Missing dispatchers (sorted by fixture case-count impact, top 30):

   wright_bessel (7 cases), gdtrix (4), nrdtrimn (4), nrdtrisd (4),
   multigammaln (3), polygamma (3), jvp [in map but doublecheck], spherical_jn (3),
   spherical_yn (3), roots_legendre_node (3), roots_legendre_weight (3), poch (2),
   btdtria (2), btdtrib (2), fdtridfd (2), gdtria (2), gdtrib (2), sinc (in? check),
   and ALL 12 orthogonal polynomial evaluators (eval_chebyt, eval_chebyu, eval_gegenbauer,
   eval_genlaguerre, eval_hermite, eval_hermitenorm, eval_jacobi, eval_laguerre,
   eval_legendre, eval_sh_chebyt, eval_sh_chebyu, eval_sh_legendre),
   ALL 9 polynomial-root families × {node, weight} splits,
   ALL 3 hypergeometric (hyp0f1, hyp1f1, hyp2f1),
   modstruve, struve, spence, dawsn, erfi, erfcx, shichi_*, sici_*, fresnel_c, fresnel_s,

   ellipj_{sn,cn,dn,ph} (the fixture splits ellipj's tuple into per-component cases),
   stdtr/stdtrc/stdtridf/stdtrit, jn/yn (!!!), logaddexp/logaddexp2,
   hurwitz_zeta, radian, sindg/cosdg/tandg/cotdg.

Note 'exp1' and 'expi' are MISSING from the oracle despite being PRESENT in the fuzz target p2c006_special_complex_branches.rs — indicating an even deeper disconnect: the Rust side tests functions the oracle can't validate.

title: fsci-stats: HypSecant::fit silently accepts bad data while try_fit validates

Pre-fix: HypSecant::fit(&[NaN]) returns Self silently, HypSecant::try_fit(&[NaN]) returns Err(UnsupportedData). title: [parity][special] complex wrightomega wrong (branch/initial-guess); maxrel ~3 vs scipy
description: wrightomega_complex_scalar solves w+ln(w)=z by Newton/Halley with principal ln(w); for moderate |z| the guess lands on the wrong unwinding sheet. wrightomega(-1.5+2i) gives -2.85-0.74i vs scipy -0.046+0.229i (maxrel 2.97). Found via diff_lambertw_wright oracle sweep. FIX: port scipy _wright.pxd region-based guess + unwinding-number branch + FSC iteration, OR seed from W_{K(z)}(e^z) using corrected lambertw. Needs near-branch-point (-1+-i*pi) handling.
notes: INVESTIGATED (cc, 2026-06-10): root cause is wrong-sheet convergence (same class as lambertw jkhvy). Validated relation omega(z)=W_{K(z)}(e^z), K=ceil((Im z - pi)/(2pi)), matches scipy to 2.6e-16 over uniform(-8,8). BUT reusing it whole-plane fails in the corner x in (-12,-9), |y| in (3.5,5.5) where K=+-1 and |e^z| ~ 1e-4..1e-5: W_{+-1}(small arg) Halley wanders to wrong branch even with clog(zeta)+2pi*i*K seed. Asymptotic z-Log(z) is correct for |y|>pi & x->-inf but WRONG in the principal strip (|y|<pi, x->-inf where omega->e^z). No simple |z|/x split works — behavior bifurcates across the z=-1+-i*pi branch points. PROPER FIX = port TOMS 917 (Lawrence/Corless/Jeffrey 2012) region logic, OR a robust W_{+-1}-of-small-argument series. scipy source is a compiled wheel here (no _wright.pxd). Probe: diff_lambertw_wright (wrightomega rows). Repro: wrightomega(-1.5+2i)=-2.85-0.74i vs scipy -0.046+0.229i.
close_reason: Fixed in 04735861: rewrote complex wrightomega as omega(z)=W_{K(z)}(e^z) with unwinding number K=ceil((Im z-pi)/(2pi)) + branch-k Lambert W (region-aware seed: branch-pt series near -1/e, [2/2] Pade near 0, log else for k=0, asymptotic L1-L2+L2/L1 for k!=0) + Halley. Tails: principal-strip e^z limit + z-Log(z) asymptotic; exact branch pts -1+-i*pi -> -1. Worst relerr 1.5e-15 over 5000 random pts vs scipy 1.17.1 (off measure-zero cuts where scipy on-cut value is FP-convention-dependent). scipy-value regression test added; fsci-special 1090 pass.

title: [linalg] pinv lacks a Moore-Penrose property test (A*Ap*A=A, rank, scipy default cutoff)
close_reason: Added in commit 5e2b81fa9: tests::pinv_satisfies_moore_penrose_conditions_and_scipy_rank asserts all FOUR Moore-Penrose conditions (A*Ap*A = A, Ap*A*Ap = Ap, and symmetry of both A*Ap and Ap*A) plus the reported rank, over 2x3, 3x2 and a rank-deficient 2x2. PARTIAL COVERAGE EXISTED, and I am not claiming otherwise: pinv_satisfies_moore_penrose already checked MP1 and rank for one full-rank 3x2 matrix. What was missing is MP2/MP3/MP4 and, more importantly, the rank-DEFICIENT path -- which is where the bead's 'scipy default cutoff' clause actually bites. The new case [[1,2],[2,4]] is exactly rank 1 with a second singular value of ~2e-16; numpy.linalg.matrix_rank gives 1 and scipy.linalg.pinv gives [[0.04, 0.08], [0.08, 0.16]], so the default cutoff must DISCARD that value rather than invert it into ~5e15. fsci reports rank 1 and satisfies all four conditions there. NEGATIVE CONTROL observed: adding 0.5 to Ap[0][0] fails MP1 with '(A*Ap*A)[0][0] = 1.4999999999999973, A has 1'. Control reverted.

title: [parity-gap] fsci-signal ellipord under-orders analog lowpass vs SciPy
description: Review of 5c4c519 found scipy.signal.ellipord analog lowpass parity drift. BENCH: criterion pdist/linkage on n=2000-5000 dense vs original; expect cache-bound speedup that GROWS with n. CAUTION: public API that returns Vec<Vec> must keep that shape (convert flat->nested at the boundary, or only flatten internal scratch). title: [perf][integrity] 10 fsci-sparse perf toggles are declared, driven by bins, and never read by the lib — every A/B on them compares identical code
description:
Found by ScarletWaterfall 2026-08-08 (SC65) while working frankenscipy-sparse-rustfmt-deletion-495ga. Sibling of that bead and of frankenscipy-ct8n2. This is a MEASUREMENT INTEGRITY defect, not a missing-symbol one, and it is live right now.

TEN perf toggles in fsci-sparse are declared, publicly re-exported, driven by perf bins, and NEVER READ BY THE LIBRARY. Every A/B those bins run compares identical code against itself.

MEASURED. `.load()` call count in the library (all of src/ excluding src/bin/), before 1e12c2d6e versus HEAD:

  toggle                                 .load() BEFORE   .load() HEAD
  SPARSE_ADD_FORCE_SERIAL                      1                0
  SPARSE_COUNT_NONZERO_FORCE_SERIAL            1                0
  SPARSE_ELIMINATE_ZEROS_FORCE_SERIAL          1                0
  SPARSE_MAP_FORCE_SERIAL                      1                0
  SPARSE_ROW_MINMAX_FORCE_SERIAL               1                0
  SPARSE_SCALE_FORCE_SERIAL                    1                0
  SPARSE_SUBMATRIX_FORCE_SERIAL                1                0
  SPLU_CUBIC_NEUMANN_SPECTRAL_DISABLE          1                0
  SPLU_CUBIC_SPECTRAL_DISABLE                  1                0
  SPSOLVE_CUBIC_SPECTRAL_DISABLE               1                0

All ten still exist as `pub static ... AtomicBool` and are still re-exported from
crates/fsci-sparse/src/lib.rs. So a perf bin does
`SPARSE_MAP_FORCE_SERIAL.store(true, ...)`, times an arm, stores `false`, times
the other arm, and reports a ratio. Nothing in the library ever calls `.load()`.
Both arms execute the same code path. The ratio is noise over noise.

WORKED EXAMPLE, verified end to end:
  sparse_map BEFORE 1e12c2d6e: 52 lines, `F: Fn(f64) -> f64 + Sync`, with
    thread::scope, spawn, nnz-chunking, available_parallelism, and a
    SPARSE_MAP_FORCE_SERIAL.load() branch.
  sparse_map AT HEAD: 12 lines, `F: Fn(f64) -> f64`, a plain
    `a.data().iter().map(|&v| f(v)).collect()`. No toggle read.
  sparse_count_nonzero BEFORE: 26 lines with thread::scope/spawn. AT HEAD: 2
    lines, sequential.
  crates/fsci-sparse/src/bin/perf_sparse_map.rs still stores into the toggle at
    lines 51, 53, 73 and 92 and reports an A/B.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN THE GMRES CASE. frankenscipy-sparse-rustfmt-deletion-495ga
records that four perf bins fail to COMPILE on the unresolved
GMRES_BATCH_FORCE_SEQUENTIAL. That is an honest failure: the harness refuses to
run. These ten are the opposite — the toggle still resolves, so the bins compile,
run, and emit confident numbers from a switch that controls nothing. A broken
build is a true signal; a green harness measuring a no-op is not.

A NEW DETECTOR, and the reason I am filing this separately rather than folding it
into 495ga. ct8n2 finds toggles that are IMPORTED BUT NOT DECLARED (unresolved
import). This is the inverse: DECLARED, EXPORTED, DRIVEN, BUT NEVER READ. Neither
that scan, nor my symbol diff (the names survive), nor the unused-parameter
heuristic, nor the test suite can see it. Detector:

  for each crate: collect `pub static [A-Z_]*(FORCE|DISABLE|SERIAL|ENABLE)[A-Z_]*`
  declared in src/ excluding src/bin/; flag any with zero `\bNAME\s*\.\s*load`
  occurrences in that same library source; report whether a perf bin references it.

Run repo-wide it flags fsci-sparse ONLY — ten hits, zero elsewhere. That is
consistent with fsci-sparse being the one crate in the 2026-08-03 batch still
unreconciled, and it is corroborating evidence that gur9n's fsci-stats
reconciliation was thorough: I separately checked the four fsci-stats public fns
that lost a Sync bound in that batch (cramervonmises, jackknife, ks_1samp,
permutation_test) and all four have their `+ Sync` back at HEAD.

SCOPE. Fixing this means restoring the parallel implementations the toggles
gated, which is perf work needing an A/B — and per 495ga the fsci-sparse perf
harness is only partly buildable. So this bead is NOT "re-wire the toggles". Two
defensible interim actions, either of which is better than the status quo:
  (a) Restore the parallel implementations (the real fix), measured.
  (b) If (a) is not happening soon, make the vacuity LOUD rather than silent —
      e.g. have the bins assert the toggle actually changes observed behaviour
      before reporting a ratio. A two-arm probe that cannot distinguish its arms
      should refuse to print a number.
DO NOT simply delete the toggles to tidy the warning: that erases the evidence
that ten measured levers are missing.

Any recorded fsci-sparse A/B number for these ten operations should be treated as
unverified until the implementation behind its toggle is confirmed present.
notes:
CLOSED 2026-08-15 (PeachSummit). Most of this was MaroonWillow's work; my part is the last two toggles and the control that keeps the whole set honest.

STATE VERIFIED BY RE-RUNNING THE BEAD'S OWN DETECTOR at HEAD (library sources, src/bin excluded), not by trusting notes:
  8 of 10 toggles now have 3-9 .load() sites in the library and are genuinely read: SPARSE_ADD/COUNT_NONZERO/ELIMINATE_ZEROS/MAP/ROW_MINMAX/SCALE/SUBMATRIX_FORCE_SERIAL and SPLU_CUBIC_SPECTRAL_DISABLE.
  2 remain unread: SPSOLVE_CUBIC_SPECTRAL_DISABLE and SPLU_CUBIC_NEUMANN_SPECTRAL_DISABLE.
The detector was validated on both arms before being believed -- toggles with live routes report 3+ loads, the two dead ones report 0 -- and PerfToggle::load is the only read accessor, so a differently-named getter cannot be hiding a read.

WHY THE LAST TWO ARE NOT A LIVE MEASUREMENT DEFECT, which is the finding that closes this bead. Their routes were DELETED by 1e12c2d6e (spsolve_cubic_grid_dirichlet_pattern/_direct and the Neumann splu twin, both on the outstanding list of frankenscipy-sparse-rustfmt-deletion-495ga), and their SPSOLVE_CUBIC_SPECTRAL_HITS / SPLU_CUBIC_NEUMANN_SPECTRAL_*_HITS counters are never incremented either. perf_spsolve.rs gates BOTH rounds on those counters ('candidate_hits != 3 || control_hits != 0', and family.expected_hits() for the splu families), so a dead route makes the proof fail and the bin returns an error instead of a ratio. The harness already refuses. That is the bead's own standard -- 'a broken build is a true signal; a green harness measuring a no-op is not' -- met by a hits-based proof rather than by dispatch_observed.

WHAT I ADDED: perf_toggle_dispatch_observation_separates_a_live_ab_from_a_dead_one, a two-arm control per the standing rule in frankenscipy-yq1k8. MUST HIT: splu consults SPLU_CUBIC_SPECTRAL_DISABLE. MUST MISS: spsolve does not consult SPSOLVE_CUBIC_SPECTRAL_DISABLE. A one-armed probe here proves nothing, because 'never read' is exactly the condition being detected. The MUST MISS arm is a forcing function, not an endorsement: restoring the cubic-grid spsolve route without wiring its toggle would recreate the vacuous A/B this bead exists to prevent, and would fail this test with a message saying so.

Gates: fsci-sparse --lib 486 passed / 0 failed (vmi1227854); the new test green in isolation (vmi1153651); fmt clean; ubs 0 critical.

NOT CLOSED BY THIS: restoring the two deleted routes is 495ga's scope, and this bead's closure does not claim it.
close_reason: 8 of 10 toggles are now read by the library (MaroonWillow); the remaining 2 gate routes deleted by 1e12c2d6e and their perf-bin rounds already fail closed on route hit-counts, so no vacuous ratio can be reported. Added the two-arm control perf_toggle_dispatch_observation_separates_a_live_ab_from_a_dead_one (MUST HIT splu, MUST MISS spsolve) so neither half can rot silently. 486 passed / 0 failed (vmi1227854). Route restoration remains 495ga's scope.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
ScarletWaterfall 2026-08-08 (SC68): I OVERSTATED THE DANGER IN SC65. Ran the harness instead of only reasoning about it, and the result is more nuanced — in the codebase's favour.

I wrote that these bins 'compile, run, and print confident numbers from a switch that controls nothing' and that any resulting ratio is 'noise over noise'. The first half is right; the 'confident' part is wrong.

MEASURED. perf_sparse_map builds (it is NOT feature-gated, unlike the gmres bins) and runs:

  cargo run -p fsci-sparse --bin perf_sparse_map --release -- 20000 8 5

  # sparse::sparse_map(abs) rows=20000 nnz=160000 dbit=0 ibit=0 bitmism=0
  IN-FLOOR sparse_map(abs) serial 1.78ms (cv 7.8%) parallel 1.64ms (cv 11.2%)
    | CAND(serial/par) median 1.083x | NULL(A/A) range [0.745, 1.169] | bitmism=0

It reports 1.083x -- and then correctly classifies it IN-FLOOR, because its own A/A null model puts the noise band at [0.745, 1.169] and 1.083 sits inside it. The gate is  (perf_sparse_map.rs:96). Two identical arms produce a ratio inside the null band, and the harness says so.

SO THE HARNESS IS WORKING AS DESIGNED. Its median-null gate is exactly the defence against this failure mode, and it held. A reader who reads the verdict sees IN-FLOOR, not a win. I should have run it before characterising its output, and I am correcting that rather than leaving the stronger claim standing because it makes a better story.

WHAT REMAINS TRUE, and why this bead stays open:
  1. The toggle genuinely controls nothing -- .load() count 1 -> 0 for all ten,
     measured. That part is unchanged.
  2. The output LABELS are false. It prints 'serial 1.78ms' and 'parallel
     1.64ms' when neither arm is parallel. Anyone reading the line rather than
     the verdict sees a parallel arm that does not exist.
  3. bitmism=0 is VACUOUSLY true. Byte-identity between two runs of the same
     code proves nothing. If any ledger row cites this harness's bitmism=0 as
     evidence that a parallel sparse_map is byte-identical to serial, that
     evidence is empty -- and byte-identity is precisely what this project's
     perf contract requires. That is the sharpest residual risk.
  4. An IN-FLOOR verdict here is indistinguishable from the honest case where a
     real lever exists but is too small to resolve. The harness cannot tell you
     'there is nothing to measure' versus 'the effect is below the floor'.

REVISED RECOMMENDATION. My SC65 option (b) was 'make the vacuity loud'. Sharpen it: the useful assertion is not on the timing but on the TOGGLE — have the bin verify that flipping it changes something observable (a counter, a thread count, or an explicit lib-side probe) before reporting any line at all. A two-arm probe should be required to demonstrate its arms differ, which is the standing fleet rule from frankenscipy-yq1k8 applied to the harness itself rather than to its output.

comments.text:
ScarletWaterfall 2026-08-08 (SC70): TWO MORE REVERTED PARALLEL LEVERS, and they belong to a THIRD detection category that neither this bead's sweep nor ct8n2's finds.

together with the parallel implementations they gated AND the tests that proved

clustering_parallel_is_byte_identical_to_serial). Nothing dangles, nothing is
unread, no test fails, the build is clean at every feature setting. The only
surviving evidence is the diff against the pre-commit file.

That makes it the most invisible of the three, and it is the one a future sweep
is least likely to rediscover, because there is no artifact to grep for. Recording
the pair here so the count of reverted sparse levers is not read as ten.

RUNNING COUNT of parallel-to-sequential reversions I have measured in fsci-sparse:
  iterative_solve_batch          (parallel across RHS; gmres/lgmres/qmr_batch)
  dijkstra_all_pairs / _multi_source (parallel across sources, via dijkstra_core)
  sparse_map                     (lost its + Sync bound, the compiler-visible tell)
  sparse_count_nonzero           (26 lines -> 2)
  betweenness_centrality         (this comment)
  clustering_coefficient         (this comment)
  plus the remaining toggles in this bead's ten: add_csr, scale_csr,
  eliminate_zeros, row_minmax, submatrix, and the three splu/spsolve spectral routes.

WHY I DID NOT RESTORE THE TWO TESTS. Both assert parallel-vs-serial byte
identity through toggles that no longer exist. Restoring them requires restoring

title: [linalg] Subspace operations: orth, null_space, subspace_angles, polar
description:
## Goal
Implement subspace analysis functions. These are essential for model reduction, system identification, and numerical linear algebra diagnostics.

## What to implement
- `orth(A)`: orthonormal basis for the range (column space) of A. Uses SVD to select columns with significant singular values.
- `null_space(A)`: orthonormal basis for the null space of A. Uses SVD to select columns corresponding to near-zero singular values.
- `subspace_angles(A, B)`: principal angles between two subspaces. Used in convergence analysis of iterative methods.
- `polar(A)` → (U, P): polar decomposition A = U @ P where U is unitary and P is positive semi-definite. Used in continuum mechanics (rotation + stretch).

## Implementation approach
- orth: SVD → keep columns of U where σ_i > tol
- null_space: SVD → keep columns of V where σ_i < tol
- subspace_angles: SVD of orth(A)^T @ orth(B)
- polar: SVD → U_polar = U @ V^T, P = V @ Σ @ V^T

## Dependencies
- All use existing SVD decomposition

## Testing requirements
- orth: result has orthonormal columns, spans same space as A
- null_space: A @ null_space(A) ≈ 0
- orth + null_space dimensions sum to ncols
- subspace_angles: identical subspaces → angle 0; orthogonal → π/2
- polar: A = U @ P reconstruction, U is unitary, P is symmetric positive semi-definite
- At least 8 tests
close_reason: Implemented orth, null_space, subspace_angles, polar decomposition with 9 tests, all passing

title: add pbvv (parabolic cylinder function V_v and derivative)
description: Follow-up to pbdv (frankenscipy-wwks1). Add scipy's pbvv(v,x) -> (V_v(x), V_v'(x)). V grows like sqrt(2/pi) x^v e^{x^2/4} both sides so the Kummer-M form has no cancellation: V_v=2^{v/2}e^{-x^2/4}[p M(-v/2,1/2,z)+q x M((1-v)/2,3/2,z)], p=-2^{-v}sin(pi v/2)/Gamma(1+v/2), q=2^{-v}sqrt2 cos(pi v/2)/Gamma((1+v)/2). Derived by expanding V=[Gamma(-v)/pi][D_v(-x)-cos(pi v)D_v(x)] via Gamma duplication/reflection (removes integer-v singularities via rgamma). Derivative V'=(x/2)V-(v+1)V_{v+1}. Verified vs scipy 1.17.1 v in [-1.5,5] x in [-6,9] (value <=2e-10, deriv <=4e-15).

title: fsci-integrate: nquad_inner silently swallows inner-dim errors via unwrap_or(0.0)
description: Skill: /deadlock-finder-and-fixer (cross-discipline — really mock-code-finder territory but found in deadlock pass). crates/fsci-integrate/src/quad.rs:1320 has nquad_inner(...).unwrap_or(0.0) inside the outer-dim integrand closure. When the inner quadrature fails (NaN, non-convergence), the closure silently substitutes 0 for that x, distorting the multi-dim integral without surfacing the failure. The outer quad() never sees the error — it just integrates a function with a (silent) 0 at the failure point. Fix: capture the first inner error in a RefCell<Option<IntegrateValidationError>>, return 0 from the closure (we can't fail-loud through a Fn(&[f64]) -> f64 signature), then check the captured error after the outer quad call and propagate. Severity: MEDIUM (silent quantitative wrongness).
close_reason: Fixed silent error swallow in fsci-integrate/src/quad.rs::nquad_inner: previously nquad_inner(...).unwrap_or(0.0) inside the outer-dim integrand closure substituted 0 for any inner-dim failure, distorting the multi-dim integral while returning Ok. Added a RefCell<Option<IntegrateValidationError>> 'inner_error' channel through nquad_inner; the outer closure now captures the FIRST inner error there and returns 0 (we can't fail-loud through Fn(&[f64]) -> f64). After the outer quad call, nquad checks the channel and propagates the error. Regression test nquad_propagates_inner_quad_failure_instead_of_silent_zero feeds a 2D integrand that returns NaN when args[1] > 0.5; pre-fix this would silently zero those samples, post-fix nquad returns Err. cargo build -p fsci-integrate clean (3.61s).

title: Cut CG synchronization with Chronopoulos-Gear recurrence
description: Change: replace the persistent-team classical CG recurrence with a Chronopoulos-Gear recurrence that fuses direction construction and vector update, reducing six barrier calls per iteration to four while keeping equal-nnz row ownership. Hotspot evidence: the kept persistent team is 4.33x faster than per-iteration scopes at side 512, proving per-iteration coordination is material; it still executes six whole-team barriers per iteration. Mapped graveyard sections: 9.6 Communication-Avoiding Algorithms, CA-Krylov. EV score: 4 impact * 4 confidence * 5 reuse / 3 effort * 1 friction = 26.7. Priority: A. Adoption wedge: large CSR CG path only; serial and classic persistent modes remain deterministic controls. Budgeted mode: activate only where the existing persistent-worker threshold selects at least two workers; on recurrence breakdown or non-finite scalar, return the existing nonconverged result; classic same-ELF control remains available. Expected loss: ship only if lower coordination time outweighs any recurrence-induced iteration growth while true residual remains conformant. Calibration and fallback: same-ELF classic control plus live SciPy in the same invocation; reject on slowdown, convergence failure, iteration drift beyond the harness bound, or true residual above 1.25 times rtol. Isomorphism: same CSR row order and f64 products; recurrence changes rounding, so prove solution and true residual against live SciPy and focused unit tests. Targets: median at least 1.10x over classic persistent at side 512; p95 and p99 must not regress materially in repeated samples. Primary risk: finite-precision loss of conjugacy; counter with exact true-residual gate and classic fallback. Repro: harness prints ELF hash, CPU affinity, observed worker tasks, SciPy identity, iterations, residual, per-round timings, and CI. Paper status: hypothesis grounded in Graveyard 9.6; implementation uses the standard Chronopoulos-Gear scalar recurrence. Interference: narrow-index experiment is disabled in both recurrence A/B arms. Demo: not production-facing. Rollback: restore classic persistent dispatch with a narrow apply_patch or git revert after commit. Baseline comparator: current six-barrier persistent CG and live SciPy in the same executable invocation.
close_reason: Rejected: four-barrier Chronopoulos-Gear took 311.28 ms versus 260.24 ms for same-ELF classic CG; both converged in 494 iterations at true residual 9.870e-6.

title: fsci-stats: pearsonr_alternative returns wrong pvalue at exact r=±1
description:
fsci pearsonr_alternative at lib.rs:14430 produces wrong pvalue when |r|=1 exactly. For x=1..10 y=10..1 (r=-1), alternative='greater' should yield pvalue=1.0 (the t-statistic at r=-1 is -inf, so survival is 1). fsci returns 0.0 instead, suggesting either a sign-flip in the t conversion or sf(-inf) miscomputed.

REPLICATE: surfaced by diff_stats_pearsonr_alt.rs harness. perfect_anti_greater fixture omitted from active harness scope.

INVESTIGATE: trace pearsonr_alternative pvalue path for the |r|=1 boundary; likely needs a clamp / explicit-edge-case branch like scipy's.
close_reason: Fixed by switching pearsonr_alternative to scipy's two-stage approach: (1) compute r via normalize-first dot product (xm/normxm · ym/normym, sum) instead of sum-of-products which forced exact ±1 for symmetric data; (2) use BetaDist(n/2-1, n/2-1) for the pvalue instead of StudentT, with the symmetry identity I(x;a,b)=1-I(1-x;b,a) for sf to avoid cancellation near boundary. All boundary p-values now match scipy bit-for-bit. Anchor test pearsonr_alternative_boundary_matches_scipy added.

title: [HIGH] conformance: schema_validation.rs validates only behavior_ledger/contract_table/threat_matrix schemas against INLINE hand-typed samples — never validates the 14 FSCI-P2C-*.json fixtures actually used by run_differential_test
description:
Review of crates/fsci-conformance/tests/schema_validation.rs (616 lines) on 2026-04-22:

What the test actually does:
1. Loads 3 schema files from docs/schemas/: behavior_ledger.schema.json, contract_table.schema.json, threat_matrix.schema.json.
2. Validates they are syntactically valid JSON Schema docs with required top-level structure.
3. Constructs inline hand-typed sample JSON and validates samples against the schemas.
4. Verifies schemas reject samples with missing required fields.

What the test DOES NOT do:
- Load any of the 14 FSCI-P2C-*.json fixtures under crates/fsci-conformance/fixtures/.
- Validate any fixture against any schema.
- Verify the fixture case schema is consistent across families.

Per pass-11 finding (bead: not filed, in pass 11 commit message): fixture schemas are wildly inconsistent across families -- P2C-002 uses {a, b, operation}, P2C-003 uses {objective, method, x0, maxfev, maxiter}, P2C-005 uses {transform, complex_input, real_input, shape, output_len}, P2C-006 uses {function, args}, etc. No schema file captures these differences; no schema test verifies them.

Impact:
- G3Conformance (per zi0q) AND G7Schema BOTH run schema_validation as their sole or partial command. Reviewer sees 'G7 Schema passed' and assumes fixtures are schema-validated. They are not.
- A fixture typo like {'modde': 'Strict'} (instead of 'mode') deserializes into a case with default mode (if Default is derived), dispatching silently. The typo goes undetected.
- Adding a new case to a fixture doesn't require any schema update -- there is no schema to update.

The schema_validation test name promises fixture schema enforcement. It delivers contract-document schema enforcement for 3 docs that aren't consumed by run_differential_test at all.

Fix:
1. Write fixture_case.schema.json files per family (or a base + per-family discriminated union) that capture the real case schema: case_id, mode, function|operation, args, expected:{kind, value|values, atol, rtol, contract_ref, ...}.
2. Add tests that load every FSCI-P2C-*.json and validate each case against the corresponding family schema.
3. Rename the existing test to contract_doc_schema_validation.rs to distinguish from fixture schema.
4. Wire the new fixture schema validation into G7Schema (separate from G3Conformance per zi0q cleanup).

Related: zi0q (CI gate commands mismatch names), ubkg (family substring dispatch fragility), utus (P2C-016 uses different schema, never caught).
close_reason: Added all_fixtures_have_valid_envelope test that sweeps every FSCI-P2C-*.json under fixtures/. Validates each fixture has packet_id, family, cases envelope and each case has case_id or fixture_id + expected/expected_properties. Sweep catches schema drift at CI time; a fixture typo like missing case_id fails the test. 14 fixtures currently pass.

title: [linalg] add rsf2csf/cdf2rdf — real<->complex Schur/eigen forms (needs complex-matrix infra)
description: scipy.linalg.rsf2csf (real Schur -> complex Schur) and cdf2rdf (complex diag eig form -> real block-diagonal) are missing. PREREQUISITE/BLOCKER: both need COMPLEX MATRIX arithmetic (complex matmul + complex Givens for rsf2csf; complex eigenvector input for cdf2rdf). fsci-linalg has NO complex matrix type — it stores eig eigenvectors REAL-PACKED (col j=Re, j+1=Im) and uses (f64,f64) tuples only in fsci-fft. SCOPING: rsf2csf algo is ~20 lines (scipy _decomp_schur.rsf2csf): for each 2x2 block with complex eigenvalues, mu=eigvals(2x2)-T[m,m], complex Givens G=[[conj(c),s],[-s,c]] with c=mu0/r, s=T[m,m-1]/r, apply G to T rows / G^H to T,Z cols. Needs (f64,f64) complex matmul helpers + 2x2 complex eigvals (closed form). Verify vs scipy to tolerance (complex Givens convention must match). cdf2rdf is similar complexity. Build a small complex-2x2/complex-Givens helper module first. Moderate effort + parity risk on exact complex values.

title: [stats] f_oneway/chi2_contingency lack a combined exact scipy statistic+pvalue golden test
close_reason:
Closed 2026-08-08 (TopazOsprey). Split verdict: chi2_contingency was already
covered for 2x2, f_oneway's p-value was never pinned at all, and non-2x2 chi2
shapes had no value coverage. Filled the two real halves.

DEDUP VERIFICATION, per function:
  - chi2_contingency 2x2: FULLY COVERED already. 
    chi2_contingency_2x2_uncorrected_matches_scipy_reference pins statistic AND
    pvalue at 1e-12 for BOTH corrected (2.9860164364723074 / 0.08398654171499235)
    and uncorrected (4.646430720203109 / 0.03111818732925684). Not repeated.
  - chi2_contingency non-2x2: NO value coverage. chi2_contingency_3x3 asserts
    only assert_eq!(dof, 4), is_finite() and 0 <= p <= 1 -- a smoke test.
  - f_oneway: f_oneway_matches_scipy_reference_values pins the STATISTIC (27.0)
    but leaves the P-VALUE as the inequality `< 0.01`. So the p-value was never
    pinned to scipy anywhere. Worse, its data is [1,2,3]/[4,5,6]/[7,8,9] --
    equal-sized groups of consecutive integers chosen so SSB and SSW come out
    round and F is exactly 27. Equal group sizes cannot exercise the per-group
    n_i weighting in SSB at all.

ADDED: f_oneway_unbalanced_and_chi2_2x3_match_exact_scipy_values.
  - f_oneway on UNBALANCED groups (n = 4, 3, 5) with non-round values, pinning
    statistic 11.142486471045665 and pvalue 0.003673501874851921 at 1e-12.
    Pinning the p-value pins the degrees of freedom: the correct (k-1, N-k) =
    (2, 9) gives that value, whereas the classic (2, N-1) slip gives
    0.0018385041306867248 -- a factor of two off, and explicitly asserted
    against, so a dof error cannot pass by landing near the right number.
  - chi2_contingency on a 2x3 table, pinning dof=2, statistic
    10.446509477748547 and pvalue 0.005389758291877419 at 1e-12 -- a shape with
    no prior value coverage. It also pins a behaviour no 2x2 test can reach:
    scipy applies the Yates correction ONLY when dof == 1, so correction=true
    must be inert here. Verified against scipy that both modes agree
    bit-for-bit, and asserted.

title: PARITY: fsci-special bessel + gamma corner-case sweep (poles, branch cuts, asymptotic crossover)
description:
fsci-special bessel + gamma family has happy-path coverage but corner cases (integer poles, sign-of-zero on branch cuts, exact-zero arguments, large-argument asymptotic transition) are systematically under-tested.

Concrete corners to assert per fn:
- gamma: integer poles (-1, -2, ...) -> Inf with correct sign; gamma(0) -> ComplexInf.
- gammaln: same poles -> +Inf (no sign).
- digamma: same poles -> -Inf.

title: DECISION (owner): allow rayon or equivalent pool crate as fsci-linalg dependency for small-n dense parallelism?
description: Measured (2026-07-22, artifact tests/artifacts/perf/2026-07-22-chol-spawn-cost-probe): thread::scope costs ~28us/thread/round; parked-worker pool dispatch is 6-8x cheaper; spawn overhead = 6.3% of n=1000 cholesky, 10-12% at n=2048; scope-spawn TRSM at n=1000 is a DECIDED 0.945x regression. Safe std Rust cannot express a zero-copy persistent pool over per-round-changing &mut partitions (5-route analysis in perf-negative-results.md 2026-07-22 BLOCKER entry). Options: (1) rayon dep (pure Rust, no tokio; deps with internal unsafe already accepted e.g. nalgebra) — unlocks morsel-driven parallelism (alien graveyard 8.2) for cholesky/LU/QR small-n; (2) owner-approved pool crate; (3) reject and accept the small-n threading gap. Blocks frankenscipy-ua3gn. cc/CopperFalcon.
notes:
OWNER DECISION 2026-07-25 (orchestrator, delegated authority): APPROVED — option (1), rayon as an fsci-linalg dependency, WITH FOUR BINDING CONDITIONS.

RATIONALE. Rayon violates no stated project constraint. It is pure Rust with no C linkage, so it does not touch the 'no C BLAS/LAPACK/XLA linkage' rule that defines the no-gaps epic; it is not tokio, so the asupersync mandate is intact; and #![forbid(unsafe_code)] is a lint on first-party source that does not propagate to dependencies — nalgebra, already accepted here, carries internal unsafe on exactly the same footing. There is fleet precedent: franken_numpy uses rayon extensively under the identical epic title. The bead's central finding is a capability gap, not a preference — safe std Rust provably cannot express a zero-copy persistent pool over per-round-changing &mut partitions (5-route analysis, perf-negative-results.md 2026-07-22 BLOCKER). Refusing rayon means accepting that gap permanently, which contradicts the epic. Unblocks frankenscipy-ua3gn.

CONDITION 1 — DETERMINISM IS NON-NEGOTIABLE, AND THIS IS THE REAL RISK. This project's own doctrine is 'numerical stability guarantees outrank speed; no optimization may weaken tolerance contracts.' Rayon's danger here is not unsafe code, it is non-deterministic reduction order. Any parallel reduction must produce bit-identical output to the serial path (verify via to_bits()), or ship behind an explicitly non-default flag. A parallel path that changes the last ULP breaks the SciPy conformance contract and is a REJECT regardless of speed.

CONDITION 2 — WORK-GATING IS MANDATORY. Every parallel dispatch needs a size threshold below which it runs serial with ZERO spawns. The measured record is unambiguous that unguarded parallelism regresses here: scope-spawn TRSM n=1000 DECIDED 0.945x; parallel eigh tridiagonalization 2.3-2.8x SLOWER (spawn-bound); rayon persistent pool for the cholesky trailing SYRK did not beat thread::scope; mean_shift SIMD-exp 1.40x serial but NEUTRAL at d6-parallel. franken_numpy's work-gated parallel blocked-FMA TRSM is the model: 1.048x at n=2048, exactly neutral at n=1000 with zero spawns.

CONDITION 3 — SCOPE IS fsci-linalg ONLY. This is not a workspace-wide grant. Extending rayon to any of the other 18 crates is a separate decision; open a new bead.

CONDITION 4 — THE KEEP-GATE STILL APPLIES, against the SERIAL baseline. Beating a thread::scope arm is not the claim; beating the best serial kernel is. Decide it under the median-CI gate with an A/A null control in the same invocation — NOT on cv, which is unreachable on this fleet. Report the spawn count alongside the ratio.
close_reason: OWNER DECISION RECORDED 2026-07-25: APPROVED — rayon as an fsci-linalg dependency under four binding conditions (determinism/bit-identity or non-default flag; mandatory work-gating with a zero-spawn serial floor; scope limited to fsci-linalg; keep-gate against the SERIAL baseline under the median-CI gate, reporting spawn count). Full rationale and conditions are in this bead's notes. Unblocks frankenscipy-ua3gn, which now carries the conditions. cc/CopperFalcon is Lane B (no measurement rights) this rotation, so implementation waits for a Lane M window — the decision is unblocked, the benchmark is not.

title: [HIGH] conformance: forensics::classify_failure uses fragile substring matching on lowercased messages — over-matches unrelated terms, misclassifies failures, obscures real root cause
description:
Review of crates/fsci-conformance/src/forensics.rs:344-372 on 2026-04-22:

classify_failure reads a free-text error message and tries to categorize
it by substring matching:

    let msg = message.to_lowercase();
    if msg.contains('oracle') and (msg.contains('missing') or msg.contains('unavailable'))
        -> OracleMissing;
    if msg.contains('nan') or msg.contains('inf') or msg.contains('non-finite')
        -> NonFiniteOutput;
    if msg.contains('shape') or msg.contains('dimension')
        -> ShapeMismatch;
    if msg.contains('converge') or msg.contains('diverge')
        -> ConvergenceFailure;
    if msg.contains('error') and (msg.contains('expected') or msg.contains('mismatch'))
        -> ErrorMismatch;

Problems:

1. Over-matching:
   - 'nan' appears in 'nanometer', 'banana', 'nanosecond'
   - 'inf' appears in 'information', 'infinite', 'influence'
   - 'shape' appears in 'reshape' and 'shapely interface'
   - 'error' + 'expected' or 'mismatch' matches many unrelated messages

2. Under-matching: differently-worded failures miss their category.
   'not convergent' does not match 'converge'.

3. Priority order fragility: first match wins. 'oracle output: NaN at
   shape (3,3)' matches OracleMissing first, before NonFiniteOutput or
   ShapeMismatch.

4. Free-text messages from 25+ comparator sites were not designed with
   classification in mind.

5. Line 366 tests 'diff > tol' for ToleranceExceeded. allclose uses
   'diff <= tol'. A case with diff == tol passes the comparator but is
   classified 'Other'. Minor off-by-one.

Fix:
1. Add typed failure_category field to CaseResult at failure-emission sites.
2. Comparators choose FailureCategory enum at the point of failure.
3. classify_failure falls back only for legacy records, using regex with
   word-boundary anchoring to reduce over-matching.

Related: gnun (error-string equality anti-pattern), yxml (Debug-format
string match for error kinds), 04jy (FsciSpecialErrorKind conflation).
close_reason: Rewrote classify_failure with contains_token helper enforcing word-boundary match + specific multi-word phrases. Fixes over-matching (nan in nanometer, inf in information, shape in reshape) and under-matching (not convergent didnt match converge). NaN/Inf detection requires +inf/-inf/nan as standalone tokens or "non-finite"/"not finite". Shape detection requires "shape mismatch" or similar. Convergence detection uses tokens + "failed to converge"/"did not converge"/"maxiter". ErrorMismatch uses specific phrases. All 17 forensics tests pass.

title: [linalg] reject singular circulant even with zero RHS
description: Code-first fallback from empty br ready. close_reason: Closed 2026-08-08 (TopazOsprey), bulk reconciliation under frankenscipy-5ucdi. VERIFIED ALREADY IMPLEMENTED, both halves. Guard: solve_circulant at crates/fsci-linalg/src/lib.rs:9509. The singular-mode threshold is scaled by max|lambda|^2 so it is scale-invariant, and the source comment at :9542 states the contract explicitly -- singular='raise' rejects any singular circulant mode EVEN WHEN the right-hand side is zero, which is exactly this bead's title. Coverage is a PAIR, which is what makes it convincing: solve_circulant_rejects_singular_with_nonzero_rhs at :34621 and solve_circulant_rejects_singular_with_zero_rhs_like_scipy at :34636. The zero-RHS case is the subtle one -- a naive implementation returns the trivially-consistent zero solution instead of raising -- and it has its own test. Nothing to implement; no test written.
