title: fuzz: pdist + is_valid_dm/is_valid_y validators have no fuzz coverage
description: Skill: /testing-fuzzing. The is_valid_dm, is_valid_y, num_obs_dm, num_obs_y helpers I just shipped (commit 33c22f3) lack a fuzz harness. p2c011_spatial_squareform.rs only covers the squareform_to_matrix↔squareform_to_condensed roundtrip on raw f64 input, not the validator+pdist composition. A new harness p2c011_spatial_pdist_validators.rs will: (1) generate random X (rows×dim), (2) compute pdist(X) for each metric, (3) verify is_valid_y(pdist) and num_obs_y(pdist) == X.len(), (4) verify squareform(pdist) is is_valid_dm, (5) verify the matrix has zero diagonal and is symmetric. Catches any future regression in the validators or pdist's invariants.
close_reason: Shipped fuzz/fuzz_targets/p2c011_spatial_pdist_validators.rs (registered in fuzz/Cargo.toml) with 5-seed corpus. Compiles via cargo check --bin p2c011_spatial_pdist_validators. Exercises pdist across 8 metric variants and verifies five invariants: pdist length = n(n-1)/2, non-negative entries, is_valid_y acceptance, num_obs_y inverse, and full squareform↔condensed roundtrip with is_valid_dm at 1e-9 tolerance.

title: [parity-gap] hyp1f1 nonpos-integer a returns 0 at large z; negative-integer b returns NaN not +inf
description: hyp1f1(a,b,z) with a a nonpositive integer is an exact degree-|a| polynomial, but (1) for z>200 the DLMF 13.7.2 asymptotic carries a 1/Gamma(a)=0 factor and returned ~0 (hyp1f1(-1,0.5,300) gave 0 vs scipy -599; hyp1f1(-5,1,300) gave 0 vs -1.86e10), and (2) a negative-integer b was rejected to NaN even when a terminates the series before the (b)_k pole (hyp1f1(-1,-2,5) gave NaN vs scipy 3.5). Separately, genuine poles (non-terminating a with b a nonpositive integer incl b=0, or nonpos-int a with |a|>|b|) returned NaN where scipy returns +inf. Fix: detect nonpos-integer a first and evaluate the terminating series for all z (|a|>|b| both nonpos int -> +inf pole); change the b-pole guard to +inf in permissive modes; and terminate hyp1f1_series at the (a+n)=0 step to avoid 0/0 when |a|=|b|. Verified: 480-case (a,b,z) grid now 0 mismatches vs scipy 1.17.1.
close_reason: Fixed in 4fcba419: nonpos-int a evaluated as terminating polynomial for all z; b-pole and |a|>|b| return +inf matching scipy; hyp1f1_series terminates at (a+n)=0 to avoid 0/0. 480-case grid 0 mismatches vs scipy 1.17.1.

title: fsci-stats: Fisk.pdf and Mielke.pdf wrong at x=0 boundary
description: Fisk.pdf and Mielke.pdf in crates/fsci-stats/src/lib.rs short-circuit to 0 for x <= 0, but at x=0 the formulas have a shape-dependent limit. Fisk.pdf = c·x^(c-1)/(1+x^c)² → ∞ for c<1, → 1 for c==1, → 0 for c>1 (scipy returns inf/1/0 in those regimes). Mielke.pdf = k·x^(k-1)/(1+x^s)^(1+k/s) → ∞ for k<1, → 1 for k==1, → 0 for k>1. Continuation of the BetaDist (9e4bfd9) and Arcsine (39431bb) boundary fix rotation. Add boundary regression tests for both distributions covering all three regimes.
close_reason: [LOW] Fixed Fisk.pdf and Mielke.pdf boundary defects at x=0 in crates/fsci-stats/src/lib.rs (continuation of BetaDist 9e4bfd9 + Arcsine 39431bb rotation). Both distributions short-circuited to 0 for x<=0, but at exactly x=0 the formulas have shape-dependent limits per scipy. Fisk.pdf(0) = c·0^(c-1)/(1+0)² → +∞ for c<1, → 1 for c=1, → 0 for c>1. Mielke.pdf(0) follows the same pattern in k. New code branches on shape vs 1 at x=0. 2 regression tests pin all three regimes plus outside-support behavior. fsci-stats --lib: 1040 → 1042.

title: [conformance][sparse] lsqr and lsmr default iteration limits diverge from scipy
notes:
2026-08-18 RainyPrairie -- DAMP LANDED ON BOTH LEAST-SQUARES SOLVERS (unbuilt).
7ed51c0eb lsmr_damped, 572bfa44a lsqr_damped. SciPy exposes `damp` on both; we had it
on neither, so this is a missing CAPABILITY rather than a divergence.

THE TWO DAMPINGS ARE DIFFERENT ALGORITHMS, which is the part worth recording:
 * LSMR folds damp into the first rotation of its second QR recurrence, one call:
   _sym_ortho(alphabar, damp), lsmr.py:344. Our port already had the hook -- the line
   read symmetric_orthogonalization(alpha_bar, 0.0) and that 0.0 IS the slot -- and
   the residual recurrence already threaded c_hat/s_hat, so damp entered correctly
   with no further change.
 * LSQR applies an EXTRA plane rotation eliminating the damping parameter, producing
   psi, which accumulates as res2 into the residual estimate (lsqr.py:441-452,
   494-496). Copying LSMR's treatment across would have compiled, run, and been wrong.

For LSQR three places had to change together: the rotation; BOTH residual estimates
(ours uses phi_bar as its proxy in two separate convergence checks, so fixing one
would have made the early-exit and the least-squares test disagree about the same
quantity); and the running ||A|| estimate, which gains damp^2 because the operator
normed is the AUGMENTED one -- that feeds ar_norm/(a_norm*r_norm), so omitting it
would compare a damped residual against an undamped norm.

ADDITIVE API, measured not assumed: IterativeSolveOptions is built with FULL struct
literals at 82 sites against 10 uses of ..Default::default(), so a new field is a
compile error at roughly seventy call sites across three crates -- unverifiable under
the freeze. Both existing signatures are unchanged, so no caller is affected even if
the new code needs a fix. damp is also meaningless for the nine Krylov solvers, which
do not take it in SciPy either.

DOCUMENTED DIFFERENCES FROM SciPy, stated at both functions rather than left to be
found: residual_norm stays the ORIGINAL system's relative residual (SciPy's normr is
the augmented system's and includes the damp*x block; they agree only at damp=0), and
a negative damp is accepted since it enters only as damp^2. Non-finite damp IS
rejected -- it would poison the rotation and propagate NaN into every later iterate.

THE CROSS-CHECK IS THE TEST I WOULD KEEP IF I COULD KEEP ONE: lsqr_damped and
lsmr_damped must agree on the damped minimizer. They minimize the same functional by
different recurrences, so agreement is evidence BOTH ports are right in a way neither
test alone provides -- and it is exactly what catches the LSMR-treatment-pasted-into-
LSQR error.

TO VERIFY when the volume frees: cargo test -p fsci-sparse -- lsmr_damp lsqr_damp.
The damp=0 bit-identity tests are the ones to watch; anything else failing is new
code, but those failing means the existing solvers were perturbed.

title: PARITY: replace fsci-signal remez least-squares approx with true Parks-McClellan exchange (DISC-008)
description:
fsci_signal::remez (lib.rs ~7657) is documented in-source as a 'Simplified Remez: frequency-sampling method as approximation' — it solves a WEIGHTED LEAST-SQUARES fit on the cosine basis, NOT the minimax/equiripple Remez exchange that scipy.signal.remez implements. Verified divergence vs scipy 1.17.1: remez_lp_11([0,0.2,0.3,0.5],[1,0]) maxdiff 1.9e-2; remez_bp_15([0,0.1,0.15,0.3,0.35,0.5],[0,1,0]) maxdiff 4.5e-2. Tracked as DISC-008.

KEY LEVERAGE: the equiripple (Chebyshev minimax) optimum is UNIQUE (alternation theorem), so a CORRECT Parks-McClellan port will match scipy to high precision (~1e-6) regardless of impl details — unlike least-squares, there is one right answer.

IMPLEMENTATION (McClellan-Parks-Rabiner 1973, as in scipy sigtools _remez):
- Type I (odd numtaps, symmetric): H(w)=sum_{k=0}^{r} a_k cos(k w), r=(numtaps-1)/2; nfcns=r+1 basis fns; r+2 extremal freqs.
- Dense grid over bands; scipy grid_density=16 default, delf=0.5/(grid_density*nfcns); desired/weight piecewise per band.
- Init r+2 extremal indices evenly across grid.
- Remez loop: (a) deviation delta = (sum b_k D_k)/(sum b_k (-1)^k / W_k) with barycentric weights b_k=prod_{j!=k}1/(x_k-x_j), x=cos(w); (b) C_k=D_k-(-1)^k delta/W_k; barycentric-interpolate A(x) through r+1 pts; (c) weighted error E(f)=W(f)(A-D) over grid; (d) find new r+2 alternating extrema; (e) converge when max|E|~|delta|.
- Build impulse response: sample A at r+1 equally-spaced freqs, inverse cosine-DFT -> a_k -> symmetric h.
- Handle types: even numtaps (Type II, zero at Nyquist), antisymmetric (Hilbert/differentiator) later; start with Type I bandpass.

VERIFY: extend crates/fsci-signal/src/bin/check_firwin2_remez.rs (already compares to scipy values) + scipy_signal_oracle.py; target maxdiff<1e-6 on remez_lp_11 + remez_bp_15, then tighten FSCI-P2C-011 remez tolerances 0.06->1e-6 and mark DISC-008 RESOLVED. scipy IS available in-env (python3 -c 'import scipy' works locally + rch) for direct verification.

CAUTION: extrema-search robustness (band-edge candidates, exact r+2 alternations, flip when too many found) is the classic PM bug source — needs careful testing across band configs, NOT a rushed impl. Behavior parity is absolute; do not ship until verified vs scipy.
close_reason: done

title: [io] reject non-32-bit IEEE float WAV reads
description:
## What

wav_read currently treats IEEE float (audio_format=3) with 8/16/24-bit sample sizes as PCM, which silently mis-decodes malformed WAV headers.

## Fix

- Reject audio_format=3 unless bits_per_sample == 32 (the only float width we implement).
- Add a regression test for a float-format header with 16-bit samples.

## Why

Avoids mis-decoding malformed files and makes behavior explicit for unsupported float widths.
close_reason: Rejected IEEE float WAV with non-32-bit samples and added regression test
